Nuclear Theory.title: Meson spectroscopy from lattice QCD
Nuclear Theory.summary: Determining the meson spectrum directly from Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) remains a central challenge, since QCD is strongly coupled at low energies and most excited states appear as resonances in hadronic decay channels. Advances in lattice QCD and scattering theory now provide a systematic framework for extracting meson spectra and resonance properties from first principles. Here I present an overview of this program and review current state-of-the-art calculations in meson spectroscopy from lattice QCD. I highlight recent progress in the extraction of resonant and coupled-channel amplitudes, along with frontier developments in three-body dynamics and the determination of meson photo-couplings. Together, these advances are bringing us closer to a comprehensive first-principles description of the excited meson spectrum.
Nuclear Theory.comment: Proceedings of a plenary talk at the MESON conference (Kraków, June 2026)

Nuclear Theory.title: Algebraic models of alpha-cluster nuclei
Nuclear Theory.summary: In this contribution I review the algebraic cluster model (ACM) for $α$-conjugate nuclei with $A=4n$ and its extension to the cluster shell model (CSM) for $A=4n+x$ nuclei. The CSM describes the splitting of single-particles levels in a deformed field generated by the cluster of $α$-particles. As an example, I discuss the energies, electromagnetic transitions and form factors of the neighboring nuclei $^{12}$C and $^{13}$C.
Nuclear Theory.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, proceedings of Cluster26, to be published by Journal of Physics: Conference Series

Nuclear Theory.title: Color transparency effects on the deuteron spin observables in the hard $pd \to ppn$ reaction
Nuclear Theory.summary:
The pionless breakup of a deuteron induced by 15 GeV/$c$ beam proton is considered theoretically in the kinematics
  where both outgoing protons are fast and the neutron is slow in the rest frame of the deuteron.
  Significant influence of color transparency on the deuteron vector and tensor analyzing powers is expected.
Nuclear Theory.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, Contribution to the proceedings of the International conference "Particle Physics at Medium and High Energies", June 2-5, 2026, Protvino, Russia

Nuclear Theory.title: Complex potential and the thermal width of quarkonium in quark-gluon plasma
Nuclear Theory.summary: We study the complex heavy quark anti-quark potential in lattice 2+1 flavor QCD at non-zero temperature. We point out a close relation between the imaginary part of the potential and the thermal quarkonium width. Using this relation, we estimate the thermal width of charmonia and bottomonia at high temperatures, which are not yet accessible with direct lattice QCD calculations of the quarkonium correlation functions and compare these to the results of the T-matrix analysis. For some of the excited quarkonia states, our estimates of the thermal width are smaller than the ones obtained in the T-matrix analysis.

Nuclear Theory.title: Bayesian inference of the dense matter equation of state built upon extended Skyrme interactions: A generalization
Nuclear Theory.summary: The nonrelativistic theory of nuclear matter (NM) based on Brussels-Skyrme interactions is employed to develop models for dense and neutron-rich matter within a Bayesian framework. We employ the following set of constraints: the four best-known nuclear empirical parameters, the density dependence of the energy per particle in pure neutron matter (PNM), the density dependence of the Landau effective mass ($m_\mathrm{eff}$) of neutrons in PNM and symmetric NM, and a lower limit on the maximum gravitational mass that neutron stars (NSs) can support. In addition, a number of ``sanity checks'' are added: the values of the speed of sound, neutron and proton Landau effective masses, and Fermi velocities are constrained up to the central density of the most massive NS configuration and for isospin asymmetries $δ=(n_n-n_p)/(n_n+n_p)$ ranging from 0 to 1. Our ensemble of models \emph{fully} explores the capacity of nonrelativistic Brussels-Skyrme effective interactions to describe NM at densities exceeding several times the nuclear saturation density. This is a necessary step toward a better understanding of the properties of dense matter and possible correlations between the parameters of NSs and the parameters of NM. Due to the pronounced U-shaped density dependencies of $m_\mathrm{eff}$, which qualitatively agree with the predictions of ab initio calculations featuring three-body forces, all our models exhibit a non-monotonic ``rise-and-fall'' behavior of the thermal pressure ($p_\mathrm{th}$) as a function of density, which in extreme cases leads to $p_\mathrm{th} < 0$. This work is a generalization of [Beznogov and Raduta, Phys. Rev. C 110, 035805 (2024)].
Nuclear Theory.comment: 15 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in PRC

Nuclear Theory.title: Characterizing $\pT$-differential Radial-Flow Fluctuations in Au+Au Collisions at FAIR with a Multi-Phase Transport Model
Nuclear Theory.summary: We report the first predictions of the transverse-momentum ($\pT$)-differential radial-flow fluctuation observable, $\vzpT$, in Au+Au collisions at the top SIS100 energy, $\snn=4.9$~GeV, which will be available at the FAIR accelerator complex. Radial flow and its fluctuations are studied for different centrality intervals and reference-$\pT$ selections to investigate the properties and robustness of the calculated long-range correlation. $\vzpT$ displays a characteristic evolution from negative values at low $\pT$ to positive values at higher $\pT$. The integrated $v_0$, obtained with different reference-$\pT$ intervals, follows a common trend, with an approximately inverse-square-root dependence on the inclusive charged-particle multiplicity ($\nch$). The $\vzpT$ signal changes little when the pseudorapidity gap is varied between 0.2 and 0.8, or when the edges of the reference-$\pT$ interval are varied, in the bulk region. For identified particles, the pion and proton $\vzpT$ are ordered at low $\pT$, qualitatively similar to the mass ordering seen at higher energies. However, unlike at higher collision energies, $\vzpT$ does not exhibit constituent-quark scaling, so the results do not support an interpretation in terms of partonic collectivity. These results provide constraints on the evolution of radial correlations toward lower collision energies and motivate comparisons with complementary observables to clarify their connection to collective dynamics.

Nuclear Theory.title: The role of spin polarization in event-by-event fluctuations
Nuclear Theory.summary: The event-by-event initial state fluctuations constitute a critical physical quantity for understanding the dynamics of high-energy heavy-ion collisions. Due to the extremely limited available experimental data of such fluctuations, it is difficult to constrain or direct the characterization of the underlying initial state properties. This work constrains the correlation function between the initial eccentricity and the asymmetry by employing a parton distribution function that incorporates spin polarization induced by thermal vorticity and thermal shear. Based on the kinetic theory calculations, we found that the asymmetry fluctuations considering spin polarization have a significant splitting effect compared to those without spin polarization. These splitting exhibit pronounced system size and energy dependence. Moreover, the ratios of correlation function display similar system size and energy dependence--particularly in the low-temperature regime ($T \lesssim$ 0.12 GeV). These results suggest that spin polarization may serve as a useful constraint method for the event-by-event initial state fluctuations of heavy-ion collisions.

Nuclear Theory.title: Properties of the $D_{s0}^*(2317)^\pm$ in hot and dense nuclear matter
Nuclear Theory.summary: We investigate the properties of the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^\pm$ in hot and dense nuclear matter using a coupled-channel molecular model built on next-to-leading-order heavy meson chiral perturbation theory. In-medium modifications to the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ stem from changes to the $DK$ channel within the coupled $DK$-$D_s η$ system. As nuclear density increases, the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ quasiparticle peak shifts toward lower energies and broadens, tracking the behavior of the $D$-meson spectral function. As for temperature effects, those are milder, with the thermal smearing of the Fermi surface and the melting of $Σ_c N^{-1}$ excitations in the $D$-meson spectral function shifting the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ peak back toward its free-space mass while narrowing it. Conversely, the behavior of the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$ is governed by the $\bar D \bar K$ channel and its medium behavior is driven by the $\bar K$ spectral function. With increasing temperature, the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$ also approaches its free-space mass, but its width broadens before saturating at high temperatures. Incorporating explicit medium dependencies into the interaction kernel, driven by density and/or temperature variations in the pion decay constant, further shifts the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ mass lower and narrows its width with temperature. As for $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$, its mass also drops with temperature but its width increases. These contrasting medium behaviors offer a promising pathway to constrain the internal structure of these exotic states.
Nuclear Theory.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D. Numerical data are available as ancillary files

Nuclear Theory.title: Is XTE J1814-338 a dark matter-admixed neutron star?
Nuclear Theory.summary: We explore the possibility that the ultracompact object XTE J1814-338 is a dark matter-admixed neutron star (DNS) based on a general-relativistic two-fluid approach, in which one fluid describes ordinary nuclear matter and the other dark matter. The equations of state of nuclear matter and dark matter are described by the Brueckner-Hartree-Fock (BHF) theory with realistic three-body forces and a generic bosonic self-interacting dark matter model, respectively. Based on the observational data, we determine the parameter space for XTE J1814-338 as a DNS, and find that only a halo stellar configuration with a high dark matter fraction is allowed. Furthermore, we predict other observable properties of XTE J1814-338 and provide robust lower bounds for these quantities.

Nuclear Theory.title: Quantum Simulation of Hadronization: From String Breaking to Event Generation
Nuclear Theory.summary: High-energy collisions produce large numbers of quarks and gluons that are bound into hadrons by the confining interactions of quantum chromodynamics (QCD). This hadronization process is intrinsically real-time and non-perturbative. Event generators describe hadronization using phenomenological models with parameters fitted to data rather than calculated from QCD. Uncertainties in these models limit the precision of certain measurements at the Large Hadron Collider. Quantum computers could enable first-principles simulations of these dynamics. Existing quantum simulations of gauge theories have demonstrated string-breaking dynamics. This white paper summarizes the conclusions of the InQubator for Quantum Simulation workshop \textit{From String Dynamics to Event Generation with Quantum Simulation}. We develop a roadmap for extending these simulations to inform phenomenological models of hadronization. A sequence of toy models is proposed for connecting current quantum simulations to QCD. The observables that should be extracted are listed, and the challenges that separate present simulations from quantitative predictions are identified. We propose a staged program in which quantum simulations first provide qualitative modifications to event generators and later provide quantitative input.

Nuclear Theory.title: Heavy quarkonium dynamics beyond the binding energy over temperature expansion
Nuclear Theory.summary: We revisit the pNRQCD open-quantum-system description of bottomonium in a quark-gluon plasma, writing the full master equation in a spherical basis and establishing a framework for its numerical treatment. The equation does not rely on an expansion in the ratio of the binding energy over the temperature, while retaining the Born, Markov, and dilute approximations. It depends on suitable convolutions of Coulombic Green's functions with real-time chromoelectric correlators, rather than a finite set of transport coefficients. It contains jump-operator contributions that enter with both positive and negative signs, so it is not of a Lindblad type. We utilize optimal operator rotations to minimize the negative sector and define a positive-sector approximation that retains only the optimized positive terms, obtaining in this way a Lindblad equation that can be simulated efficiently with the open-source code QTraj for arbitrary chromoelectric spectral functions. We treat the discarded sector as a systematic uncertainty associated with positivity-breaking effects of the pseudo-Lindblad generator. Positivity breaking effects can be attributed to the approximations made in the derivation of the quarkonium master equation, such as the Born--Markov approximations. Using a spectral model constrained by known infrared and ultraviolet limits, we compute the in-medium width and Bjorken-evolved survival probabilities of the $Υ(1\mathrm{S},2\mathrm{S},3\mathrm{S})$. The computations show the convergence of the binding-energy-over-temperature expansion at high temperatures and provide the first large-scale quantum-trajectory simulation results for bottomonium in the low temperature regime. We can thus follow the bottomonium evolution over the full temperature range relevant in heavy-ion collisions.

Nuclear Theory.title: A multi-wavelength view of PSR J0437-4715 with NICER and other missions: Radius measurements from far-ultraviolet to hard X-ray pulse profile modeling
Nuclear Theory.summary: We report updated mass and radius measurements for the millisecond pulsar PSR J0437-4715 obtained with pulse profile modeling of the emission from the far-ultraviolet to the hard X-rays. Using an extended 2.56 Ms Neutron Star Interior Composition ExploreR (NICER) dataset together with XMM-Newton, Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope ARray and Hubble Space Telescope observations, we perform Bayesian inference with models describing the thermal emission from hot spots of increasing complexities, together with the rest of the warm NS surface, as well as the non-thermal emission component represented by a phase-dependent (pulsed) power-law. With this comprehensive model and broadband data set, as well as radio timing priors on the mass, distance and inclination, our headline result for PSR J0437-4715 led to a mass M = 1.377(-0.034)(+0.038) Msun and an equatorial radius Req = 11.35(-0.39)(+0.40) km, one of the narrowest measurements of Req from NICER observations of millisecond pulsars. The geometric configuration favors a non-antipodal hot spot distribution, as noted in previous analyses of this pulsar. When combined with recent measurements of M and Req of other pulsars, the tight constraints from PSR J0437-4715 further reduce the allowed range of the dense matter equation of state, excluding those that predict radii above 12.0 km (at the 68% level) for all NS masses.
Nuclear Theory.comment: Submitted to ApJL, 39 pages, 23 figures, 5 tables

Nuclear Experiment.title: Magnetic Johnson noise from arbitrarily shaped conductors: experimental validation of the fluctuation-dissipation finite-element method
Nuclear Experiment.summary: Magnetic Johnson noise--magnetic noise caused by thermal current fluctuations in conducting materials--can interfere with measurements and limit their sensitivity. As the sensitivity of experiments increases, it becomes increasingly important to accurately estimate the magnetic Johnson noise from experimental components with complex shapes during both the design and analysis phases. A particularly powerful approach is to combine the fluctuation-dissipation theorem with finite-element calculations. This versatile approach can be used to calculate the magnetic Johnson noise from conductors of arbitrary geometry for a wide range of frequencies and for magnetic field detectors with general geometries, such as a finite-sized loop or a gradiometer. Using a SQUID gradiometer array, we measured the magnetic Johnson noise from conductors with complex geometries and compared the results with calculations performed using this method. The calculations reproduce both the measured noise amplitude and its frequency dependence, providing an experimental validation of this method. We also performed a detailed analysis of how the geometry and material parameters affect the frequency dependence of magnetic Johnson noise.

Nuclear Experiment.title: Absolute intensity measurement of pulsed muon beams using in-beam activation
Nuclear Experiment.summary: The absolute number of negative muons contained in a beam is essential for many experiments at accelerator facilities, but determining this number in pulsed beams has been difficult, particularly at high intensities. A method utilizing the yield of the $β$ delayed $γ$ rays from the residual nuclei following the muon nuclear capture reaction has recently been demonstrated for determining the muon number in the pulsed muon beam. In particular, the in-beam activation method employs isotopes with short lifetimes, enabling the beam intensity to be monitored during beam irradiation. However, the applicability of this method was limited because the required production branching ratio (BR) data were available only for a limited number of isotopes, restricting its use to specific experimental conditions. To broaden the applicability of this method, we searched for new candidate isotopes that are suitable for beam intensity measurement using the in-beam activation method and assessed their feasibility to a wide range of experiments. Based on the strength of the production BR, the muon capture probability, the practical detection efficiency of the detector, and the rarity of the target material in the surrounding structures, the reactions $^\mathrm{nat}$Ag ($μ^-, ν_μx$) $^{107m}$Pd and $^\mathrm{nat}$Pd ($μ^-, ν_μx$) $^{107m, 105m}$Rh are identified as a useful references for determining the number of muons in pulsed beams using the in-beam activation method.

Nuclear Experiment.title: Current Results on Light Hypernuclei in the WASA-FRS HypHI Experiment
Nuclear Experiment.summary: The current understanding of light hypernuclei, subatomic nuclei exhibiting strangeness, is being actively investigated by several collaborations. Recent studies employing high-energy heavy-ion beams have revealed unexpected results for the three-body bound state $^3_Λ$H, known as the hypertriton. Experimental measurements of its lifetime and binding energy across multiple experiments have produced a puzzling situation referred to as the ``hypertriton puzzle''. This puzzle is the central focus of the data analysis from the WASA-FRS HypHI experiment at GSI-FAIR within the SuperFRS Experiment collaboration. Light hypernuclei are being investigated using 1.96 GeV/u $^6$Li beams impinging on a fixed carbon target, in conjunction with the WASA detector system and the Fragment Separator (FRS) at GSI-FAIR. The WASA-FRS experimental campaign was carried out during the first quarter of 2022. The primary objective of the experiment is to measure the lifetimes of $^3_Λ$H and $^4_Λ$H. The possible observation of the nn$Λ$ state constitutes the second component of the WASA-FRS research program. This contribution provides an overview of our investigation of hypernuclei. Focusing on the WASA-FRS HypHI experiment, details of the current analysis status are presented.
Nuclear Experiment.comment: Proceedings of the 15th International Conference on Hypernuclear and Strange Particle Physics (HYP2025), Tokyo (Japan), 29 September 2025 - 3 October 2025. To be published in JPS Conf. Proc

Nuclear Experiment.title: Comparing the fusion of $^{19}$O and $^{20}$O ions with protons at near barrier energies
Nuclear Experiment.summary: Proton capture on $^{19,20}$O nuclei was measured in inverse kinematics with the active-target detector MuSIC@Indiana using CH$_4$ as the target gas. Direct measurement of the (p,n) cross section was enabled by the intrinsically high efficiency and self-normalizing nature of the measurement. The excitation function of both (p,n) reactions exhibits an oscillatory behavior. For the neutron-rich nuclei studied, determining the (p,n) cross section provides access to the proton fusion cross section because the proton's de Broglie wavelength is much larger than that of the heavy ion. A significant suppression of the cross section in $^{19}$O compared to $^{20}$O is observed, suggesting level-density differences. While the coupled channel calculations reproduce the oscillatory behavior observed in the case of $^{20}$O, they fail to predict the oscillatory behavior observed in $^{19}$O or the overall suppression of the fusion cross section.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: A first look at strange-quark polarization in top-quark decays with CMS Open Data
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a first realization of strange-quark polarimetry in top-quark decays. The longitudinal polarization of $Λ$ baryons is measured in the strange jets of hadronic $W\to c\bar s$ decays in semileptonic top-quark pair events, using 16.39 fb$^{-1}$ of the public CMS data of pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. The $W$ decay produces the strange quark fully polarized, so that the $Λ$ polarization measures the transfer of the quark polarization in fragmentation. With the limited statistics available, our result is consistent both with zero and with the transfer inferred from the flavor-averaged LEP measurements. The statistical reach with the full Run-2, Run-3 and HL-LHC datasets is projected.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Two-loop integrals for $t\bar{t}γ$ production at hadron colliders in the leading-colour approximation
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We complete the calculation of the two-loop Feynman integrals required for the next-to-next-to-leading order QCD corrections to on-shell top--antitop production in association with a photon at hadron colliders, in the leading-colour approximation. The same integrals also enter the subleading-colour corrections to top--antitop production in association with a jet. We construct integral bases that satisfy algebraic differential equations. These are largely in canonical form; the exceptions are a few entries, associated with elliptic curves or nested square roots, that depend at most quadratically on the dimensional regulator $ε$. We solve the differential equations in terms of a tailored set of special functions, which will enable the analytic extraction of the two-loop finite remainder. We evaluate these functions by numerically solving the differential equations they satisfy, and show that the resulting routine is fast and stable enough in the physical region for phenomenological applications.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Bootstrapping a Higher-Derivative Cosmological Collider: Borel-Laplace Resummation and Stokes Phenomena
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We develop a higher-derivative cosmological bootstrap for massive spectators with quartic dispersion, $ω^2\propto k^4$, revealing a new boundary-value problem for inflationary correlators. The exchange equation becomes fourth order, and the collapsed limit becomes an irregular singular point, where collider and WKB branches coexist and exhibit Stokes phenomena. Since the folded configuration is now an ordinary point, the relativistic criterion of Bunch--Davies regularity at the folded singularity is no longer available. We instead impose an asymptotic boundary condition that removes the WKB branches and matches the surviving collider branches to Schwinger-Keldysh data. We also construct a convergent Borel-Laplace particular solution that resums a factorially divergent expansion and satisfies both bootstrap equations simultaneously; its leading collapsed-limit behavior is reproduced by direct in-in integrals. In the bispectrum, the squeezed-limit collider signal retains its mass-dependent frequency, while its amplitude and phase depend on the dispersion scale; near the equilateral configuration, the full shape is also sensitive to this scale and can change sign. Our results expose a new analytic structure of non-relativistic cosmological correlators and signatures beyond the squeezed limit.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Running cosmological constant in light of recent CMB-BAO data
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We revisit single-field slow-roll inflation driven by a running cosmological constant, i.e. a cosmological constant receiving a logarithmic radiative correction, in light of the latest CMB-BAO data. The relative radiative correction $δ$ is treated as a free parameter of the model and allowed to be positive or negative. For positive $δ$, the predictions interpolate between a logarithmic regime and a linear inflation one. Compatibility with CMB-only data is confined to a narrow stripe near the $2σ$ border where $δ$ is relatively large. On the other hand, the predictions fit easily within the constraints including BAO data in a wide range of parameters. For negative $δ$, the slow-roll approximation breaks down at small field values and the predictions are excluded by data. However, once the effective mass contribution inside the logarithmic correction is taken into account, the negative $δ$ potential develops a local maximum and behaves like a hilltop model, achieving compatibility with CMB-only data, while agreement with CMB-BAO data is possible only at $2σ$.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 15 pages, 5 figures, corrected experimental constraints, updated discussion

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Neutrino Oscillation in a Static Dihole Geometry
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate neutrino flavor oscillations in the static equal-mass Majumdar-Papapetrou dihole geometry, restricting the propagation to the symmetry plane. Within the null approximation, we derive the leading contribution to the neutrino phase and numerically evaluate the geodesic integrals. For two neutrino flavors, interference between different trajectories introduces a dependence on the individual neutrino masses and on the neutrino mass ordering for nonmaximal mixing. We analyze the transition probability in different spacetime configurations possessing two light rings, a merged light ring (critical configuration), and no light rings in the equatorial plane. In the weak-lensing regime, the transition probability generally increases with the black holes' individual masses, while variations in the half-separation produce no qualitative change in the transition probability. In stronger-lensing configurations, variations in both the mass and half-separation modify the heights and positions of the extrema, with no monotonic increase or decrease in the transition probability. For the critical and no-light-ring configurations studied, we identify three zero-winding trajectories connecting the source and detector, including one passing near the symmetry axis. The probability remains oscillatory, and its oscillatory pattern depends strongly on the neutrino energy.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Topological Multi-Natural Inflation
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate topological inflation in minimal multi-natural inflation, in which the axion potential consists of two cosine terms. Focusing on the high-scale regime, we perform a systematic parameter scan for representative ratios of the two periods and identify regions consistent with current constraints on the scalar spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio, including those from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope. The interplay of the two harmonics allows departures from the quartic hilltop limit and accommodates the higher spectral index favored by recent cosmological data combinations. We characterize the hilltop and near-inflection-point branches and analyze the associated vacuum structure and domain-wall properties. We also discuss a symmetry-breaking origin of the required domain walls when the inflaton is the angular component of a complex scalar field. We identify regions in which the observational constraints and the adopted criteria for topological inflation are simultaneously satisfied, including regions with a sub-Planckian axion decay constant. Our results show that the observational tension encountered in the minimal quartic double-well model need not extend to topological inflation in a minimal multi-natural axion potential.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Quasi Parton Distribution Functions in Covariant Quark Models
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Quasi parton distribution functions (QPDFs) are defined in terms of QCD fields at spacelike separations evaluated in matrix elements of hadrons moving with velocity $v$. These objects can be studied in lattice QCD. In the limit when $v$ approaches the speed of light, QPDFs converge to PDFs. It is insightful to study QPDFs and their convergence in models. In this work, we first study the QPDFs in a broad class of quark models characterized by one common feature, namely the absence of gauge degrees of freedom. We provide general proofs for the convergence and sum rules of the unpolarized quark and antiquark QPDFs for both choices $γ^0$ and $γ^3$. We choose the Covariant Parton Model (CPM) as an illustration. We derive analytical results for the small-$x_v$ behavior of QPDFs and the energy-momentum tensor form factor $\bar{c}^q(t)$ at zero momentum transfer. These results are of interest as they correspond to a Wandzura-Wilczek-type approximation.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 25 pages, 7 figures, 1 table, typos fixed, published version

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Numerical evaluation of one-loop integrals using quadrature rules
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We introduce a numerical quadrature algorithm with stretched exponential convergence to evaluate one-loop integrals in dimensional regularisation in the causal Loop Tree Dual (cLTD) representation. The key feature that makes this possible is the fact that for Euclidean kinematics all singularities of the cLTD integrand lie on a compact set in loop momentum space. We prove that our algorithm admits a stretched exponential convergence with the number of integrand evaluations, and we illustrate it by evaluating triangle, box and pentagon integrals at selected Euclidean kinematics points. We benchmark our implementation against analytic results as well as results obtained via Monte Carlo integration. We also provide a proof of concept that our algorithm can be extended to physical kinematics after subtraction of threshold singularities.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: The chiral phase transition in the 3D Columbia plot - a scalable HPC workflow
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The nature of the chiral phase transition of QCD continues to represent a fundamental open problem in the study of strongly interacting matter. In recent years, significant progress has been achieved by exploiting systematic variations of theory parameters in regimes free of the sign problem. In this work, an open-source computational framework for large-scale lattice QCD investigations is presented, with particular emphasis on its application to extensions of previous studies at nonzero purely imaginary chemical potential. The framework is not developed specifically for this application: its underlying software components have been successfully employed for more than a decade in large-scale lattice QCD investigations. The focus is placed on the explicit documentation of a reproducible and scalable numerical workflow, covering all stages from data production on HPC systems to statistical analysis and final data interpretation. The presented framework integrates several publicly available software components, including GPU-accelerated simulation codes, automated job orchestration tools, and generic Monte Carlo analysis libraries. By bringing these previously operational components together and documenting their interfaces and interaction in a single framework, this work provides a ready-to-use computational blueprint for future large-scale studies of the QCD phase diagram. The corresponding software stack is fully released and designed to support systematic extensions of existing studies.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures. Version accepted and published in Computer Physics Communications. Manuscript updated to reflect the published article, with minor differences in language conventions and formatting

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Simultaneous Dalitz-plot decomposition of the $e^+ e^- \to J/ψ\, π\, π\, (K \bar{K})$ processes in the 4.13-4.36 GeV region using dispersive final-state interactions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a joint analysis of the processes $e^+e^- \to J/ψπ^+π^-$ and $e^+e^- \to J/ψK^+K^-$ at center-of-mass energies from 4.13 to 4.36 GeV. The amplitudes are constructed using the Dalitz-plot decomposition formalism, with the $e^+e^-$ energy dependence encoded through the $Y(4220)$ and $Y(4320)$ resonant structures together with a nonresonant production mechanism. The scalar $ππ/K\bar K$ final-state interaction is treated dispersively using a coupled-channel Omnès representation. This allows us to describe the measured total cross sections and one-dimensional invariant-mass distributions with a single set of energy-independent parameters. We find that a purely resonant description of the BESIII data is insufficient, requiring a nonresonant term at the amplitude level which undergoes $ππ/K\bar{K}$ rescattering. Within the present isobar model, we extract Breit-Wigner parameters for the $Z_c(3900)$, $Y(4220)$, and $Y(4320)$ states, and determine the corresponding subprocess cross sections.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 15 pages, 12 figures, 5 tables. v2: matches the version published in PRD

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Nucleon Wave Functions from QCD Vacuum Topology
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Instantons, as topologically nontrivial gauge field configurations, provide a microscopic mechanism for chiral symmetry breaking and the $U_A(1)$ anomaly in QCD. Within the instanton liquid model (ILM), instantons generate multi-fermion interactions governed by their density and size. Using this framework, we develop a microscopic description of the nucleon based on instanton-induced quark--quark correlations. We derive the diquark interaction kernels arising from single instantons and instanton--anti-instanton molecules, revealing a strong attraction in the scalar channel and weaker correlations in the spin-one channels. Embedding these interactions in a covariant, permutation-symmetric Bethe--Salpeter--Faddeev equation yields a nucleon mass $m_N=939.53~{\rm MeV}$, with a predominantly scalar-diquark component ($98\%$) and a small axial-vector admixture ($2\%$) around the mass pole. Despite its small weight, the small admixture generates substantial spin--isospin interference, yielding an axial charge $g_A=1.265$, close to experiment. The resulting covariant amplitude is analytically continued to the light front to obtain the leading three-quark wave function. The corresponding unpolarized, helicity, and transversity parton distributions, along with their QCD-evolved moments, provide a direct connection to lattice QCD calculations and global-fit analyses. Our results show that the topology of the QCD vacuum organizes not only the nucleon mass and spin structure, but also its leading valence partonic content, providing a microscopic foundation for a more complete description including confinement and higher Fock components.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Sterile neutrino dark matter in conformal Majoron models
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study sterile neutrino dark matter (DM) in a classically conformal U(1)' extension of the Standard Model with three right-handed neutrinos and a Majoron-like singlet scalar that generate the observed pattern of active neutrino masses and mixing via the type-I seesaw mechanism. Working in the regime of strongly suppressed active-sterile mixing, we show that the observed DM abundance can be produced through freeze-in from feeble interactions mediated by the heavy Z' and the conformal scalar. We solve the Boltzmann equation for the nonthermal phase-space distribution and confront the scenario with Lyman-$α$ and strong gravitational lensing data by computing the matter power spectrum. For keV-mass sterile neutrinos we identify the viable parameter space consistent with the inferred relic density and structure-formation and X-ray bounds, including regions compatible with a tentative 3.5 keV line. If a second sterile state is long-lived, late decays can realize a two-component setup that alleviates the $S_8$ tension. However, explanations of the 3.5 keV line and the $S_8$ tension are incompatible with the strong-lensing limit from JWST if the neutrinos saturate the relic abundance. In a highly fine-tuned variant of the model, the 220 PeV KM3NeT event can also be explained by invoking the decay of a superheavy sterile neutrino.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 23 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Version to appear in PRD

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Primordial black holes and gravitational waves from aligned axion inflation
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study the production of primordial black holes (PBHs) and scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) in aligned axion inflation through the transition between two stages of inflation. The first stage proceeds along a metastable trajectory and ends when this trajectory loses stability, causing the fields to turn towards the attractor of the second inflationary stage. During the transition, coupled adiabatic--entropy evolution produces a localized enhancement of the curvature power spectrum. We compute the PBH abundance from this spectrum assuming Gaussian primordial curvature perturbations and using the nonlinear compaction-function formalism with a spectrum-dependent collapse threshold and critical collapse. Representative benchmark solutions yield asteroid-mass PBHs with a potentially significant dark-matter abundance, together with an associated SIGW background.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Unitarity Methods for Magnus Amplitudes
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Magnus amplitudes refer to the matrix elements of the logarithm of the $S$-matrix. Modern unitarity methods construct cut-constructible parts of scattering amplitudes without directly invoking Feynman diagrams, offering an efficient way of obtaining loop integrands for scattering amplitudes. A procedure is proposed that adapts unitarity methods to the computation of Magnus amplitudes by modifying the $i0^+$ prescriptions of scattering amplitude integrands. A sufficient condition for applying the procedure at the level of master integrals is identified.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: v2) details of normalization conventions included (end matter). expanded abstract for a better representation of the main text and minor edits for clarity; 7+2 pages, 14 figures. v1) 7+2 pages, 14 figures

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Double diffraction production for dipole-dipole scattering at high energies
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: This paper is a first attempt to describe double diffractive production in dipole-dipole scattering within high energy QCD. Our approach is based on summing large BFKL Pomeron loops, which generate two clusters of hadrons separated by a rapidity gap. Unlike in the BK framework, our approach allows both clusters to carry large masses. We derive the cross section for the production of two such clusters and show that it exhibits geometric scaling. Testing this scaling behaviour against data from high-energy colliders such as the LHC will be a crucial step in establishing whether large Pomeron loops play a major role in high energy QCD dynamics, and in particular in the unitarization of the scattering amplitude.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Color transparency effects on the deuteron spin observables in the hard $pd \to ppn$ reaction
High Energy Phenomenology.summary:
The pionless breakup of a deuteron induced by 15 GeV/$c$ beam proton is considered theoretically in the kinematics
  where both outgoing protons are fast and the neutron is slow in the rest frame of the deuteron.
  Significant influence of color transparency on the deuteron vector and tensor analyzing powers is expected.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, Contribution to the proceedings of the International conference "Particle Physics at Medium and High Energies", June 2-5, 2026, Protvino, Russia

High Energy Phenomenology.title: The Phenomenology of the Dark Dimension and Non-Supersymmetric Strings
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Swampland principles, combined with the smallness of dark energy $Λ$, lead to the dark dimension scenario, with one extra dimension of micron size. We review this scenario and its predictions: KK graviton dark matter (or the KK tower of the quintessence field into which the gravitons convert), neutrino masses tied to $Λ^{1/4}$ via a bulk $B-L$ gauge symmetry, QCD axion decay constant $f_a\sim Λ^{1/12}\sim 10^9-10^{10}$ GeV at the 5d Planck scale $M_5$, connecting electroweak hierarchy to $Λ^{1/6}$, and a relation between the GUT and weak scales with $M_5$ as the geometric mean. The dark dimension also provides a concrete realization of an evolving dark sector: the evolution of its diameter correlates the variation of dark energy with that of the dark matter mass, fitting the recent DESI DR2 (+CMB+supernovae) data while avoiding the phantom crossing that the $w_0w_a$CDM parametrization would suggest---the apparent phantom behavior instead arises from the evolving dark matter mass. The fits suggest that the dark energy field sits in the interior of moduli space, near an unstable critical point. Motivated by this, we review recent progress on non-supersymmetric string vacua: isolated critical points protected by duality symmetries, in non-geometric flux compactifications and in Scherk--Schwarz compactifications of M-theory, and an emerging duality web for non-supersymmetric strings. This note is based on two talks given by the author at String Phenomenology 2026 (Paris) and Strings 2026 (Shanghai).
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 20 pages, based on talks at String Phenomenology 2026 (Paris) and Strings 2026 (Shanghai)

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Complex potential and the thermal width of quarkonium in quark-gluon plasma
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study the complex heavy quark anti-quark potential in lattice 2+1 flavor QCD at non-zero temperature. We point out a close relation between the imaginary part of the potential and the thermal quarkonium width. Using this relation, we estimate the thermal width of charmonia and bottomonia at high temperatures, which are not yet accessible with direct lattice QCD calculations of the quarkonium correlation functions and compare these to the results of the T-matrix analysis. For some of the excited quarkonia states, our estimates of the thermal width are smaller than the ones obtained in the T-matrix analysis.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Meson-baryon final-state interactions in the $ψ(3686)\to pK^-K_S^0\barΞ^0$ decay
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study the decay $ψ(3686)\to p K^- \bar K^0 \barΞ^0$, treating the $ψ(3686)$ as a $c\bar c$ state and therefore as a singlet under SU(3) transformations in the light-quark sector. We consider all possible combinations of a baryon, an antibaryon, and two pseudoscalar mesons that form an SU(3) singlet, retaining the terms that can lead to the $p K^- \bar K^0 \barΞ^0$ final state through $S$-wave final-state interactions. Three independent SU(3)-singlet structures are identified and assigned different weights. We also include the contribution of the $Λ(1520)$ in the meson-baryon $D$-wave. A fit to the data provides a good description of all six invariant-mass distributions. In addition to the $Λ(1520)$ contribution, we find a small contribution from the $Λ(1670)$ in the $K^-p$ invariant-mass distribution, generated by final-state interactions, and a contribution from the $Σ(1430)$, which produces a significant distortion of the $\bar K^0p$ invariant-mass distribution relative to phase space. This study demonstrates the value of investigating charmonium decays into a baryon-antibaryon pair and two pseudoscalar mesons, complementing the more commonly studied decays into a baryon-antibaryon pair and a single pseudoscalar meson.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Addendum: Production of $π^{+} π^{-}$ pairs in diffractive photon-proton and in proton-proton collisions revisited, in particular concerning the Drell-Söding contribution
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We update our analyses concerning the non-resonant (Drell-Söding) contribution to the reaction $γ^{(*)} p \to π^{+} π^{-} p$, now including general vertex functions for the coupling of pomeron, $f_{2 \mathbb{R}}$, and $ρ_{\mathbb{R}}$, to pions. This takes into account the off-shellness of the pions. We present a comparison of our tensor-pomeron model, including our new Drell-Söding and $ρ$, $ω$ vector-meson contributions, with data for the $γp \to π^{+} π^{-} p$ reaction measured by the ZEUS and H1 Collaborations. We find very good agreement of our theory with the experimental data for the $π^{+} π^{-}$ invariant mass ($M_{ππ}$) and for angular distributions. Here we restrict our analysis to the region $M_{ππ} \lesssim 1.2$ GeV. For higher values of $M_{ππ}$ we will have to consider production of higher-mass mesons. The purpose of the present article is to show that our tensor-pomeron model gives a very good fit to the so-called skewing of the $ρ$-resonance contribution in photoproduction. In fact, it is an old problem/puzzle to understood the difference of the shapes of the $M_{ππ}$ distributions in the region of the $ρ(770)$ resonance in $e^{+} e^{-}$ annihilation and photoproduction. We think that with our results we have obtained for this problem a solution which is very satisfactory from the Quantum-Field-Theory point of view. Our results are also relevant for central-exclusive $π^{+} π^{-}$ production in ultraperipheral $pp$, A$p$, and AA collisions at the LHC and for photo- and electroproduction of $π^{+} π^{-}$ at future electron-proton/ion colliders, EIC and LHeC.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: New topological phase transitions in $κ$-deformed $φ^4$ lattice models
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $κ$-deformed $φ^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/α^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: An approximate separation of the electron and positron degrees of freedom in the Dirac-Heisenberg-Wigner formalism
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Here we study the quantum relativistic phase-space description of the Dirac field referred to as the Dirac--Heisenberg--Wigner (DHW) formalism. By applying a systematic expansion procedure in weak electromagnetic fields (compared to the Schwinger critical field) and slow temporal and long spatial scales (compared to the Compton scales), the 16 scalar phase-space functions of the DHW equations can be reduced to 8 scalars. By making a further change of variables, the equations can be interpreted as four evolution equations for the electron degrees of freedom and four for the positron degrees of freedom. We refer to these equations as the weakly coupled electron-positron (WCEP) limit of the DHW equations. Unlike the case after a Foldy--Wouthuysen transformation has been made, the electron and positron degrees of freedom remain weakly coupled. Naturally, further approximations can be made on the 4+4 equations so that only 4 equations for one particle species remain. Importantly, the expansion scheme can be carried out to all orders, in which case the reduced 4+4 model, contrary to other reduced models, will cover most quantum relativistic effects. Specifically, this includes vacuum polarization, a phenomenon that otherwise has been added phenomenologically, but here appears naturally as a feature of the general expansion scheme.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Prospects for Direct Detection of Ultralight Dark Matter candidates in deci-Hz Band with IndIGO-D
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate the sensitivity of IndIGO-D, a proposed space-based decihertz gravitational-wave interferometer, to different classes of ultralight dark matter. IndIGO-D will probe the $\sim0.01$--$10~\mathrm{Hz}$ frequency band between those accessible to current ground- and future space-based gravitational-wave interferometers, providing access to ultralight dark-matter masses beyond the reach of existing instruments. We consider two complementary signatures: interferometric displacements induced by coherently oscillating scalar (dilaton), vector (dark-photon, $U(1)_B$ and $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge groups), and tensor fields with masses $m_{\rm DM}\sim10^{-17}$--$10^{-14}~\mathrm{eV}$; and changes in laser polarization induced by pseudoscalar axion dark matter at higher masses, around $m_a\sim10^{-12}~\mathrm{eV}$. For the dilatons, dark photons and tensors, we compute the expected sensitivities using two pipelines -- cross-correlation and BSD excess-power -- assuming L-shaped and triangular interferometer layouts and three representative noise power spectral densities (S1, S2, S3), each for two years of continuous observation. We find that the projected sensitivities agree to within a factor of order unity across the search pipelines and interferometer geometries. In particular, we show that IndIGO-D could open previously unconstrained coupling parameter space for vector and tensor dark matter across $m_{\rm DM}\sim10^{-16}$--$10^{-14}~\mathrm{eV}$, bridging the sensitivity of space- and ground-based experiments. For axion dark matter, we demonstrate that a complementary detection for laser light polarization shifts, limited primarily by photon shot noise, could probe the axion-photon coupling $g_{aγ}$ at masses around $m_a\sim10^{-12}~\mathrm{eV}$ at a level potentially better than that of other future experiments without degrading sensitivity to gravitational waves.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: Matches the accepted version in Physical Review D

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices in the oscillating axion background
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate the effect of an oscillating axion background on thermally induced vortex-antivortex production in the Abelian-Higgs model. Through its coupling to the gauge field, the axion sources an electromagnetic response in the presence of vortex magnetic flux, modifying the dynamics of the vortices. We study this system using Langevin lattice simulations with dissipation and stochastic noise. It is shown that the phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices, namely the pair creation of vortex and antivortex under thermal fluctuations, can be significantly modified in the oscillating axion background. We find that the axion background shifts the rapid increase in the vortex density to lower temperature. In particular, this transition temperature becomes smaller as the oscillation frequency of the axion increases. The temperature dependence of the correlation length is also modified. These features provide a new experimental approach for the axion dark matter using superconducting devices.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Probing the Energy Evolution and Hadronic Cascade Time Dependence of Forward-Backward Multiplicity Correlations in pp Collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 0.9$--$13.6$ TeV with AMPT
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Forward-backward (FB) multiplicity correlations are studied in proton--proton collisions at centre-of-mass energies of $\sqrt{s} = 0.9$, $2.76$, $5.02$, $7$, $13$, and $13.6$~TeV using the AMPT model in its default (DF) and string melting (SM) configurations. The coefficient $b_{\rm corr}$ is obtained for windows separated in pseudorapidity and azimuth, and its variation with the pseudorapidity gap, window width, collision energy, transverse momentum interval, and hadronic cascade time $τ_{\rm HC}$ is investigated. The simulated results are compared with the available ALICE measurements, and the model is validated against experimental pseudorapidity densities and charged-pion transverse momentum spectra. The correlation strength is found to decrease gradually with increasing pseudorapidity gap while retaining a substantial pedestal, to rise non-linearly with the window width, and to increase substantially with collision energy. The DF configuration yields systematically larger values of $b_{\rm corr}$ than the SM configuration, while the SM configuration provides the better description of the ALICE data at $0.9$ and $2.76$~TeV and the DF configuration at $7$~TeV. In the lowest transverse momentum intervals the deviations from the data are largest for both configurations. The hadronic cascade time is varied within the SM configuration over $τ_{\rm HC} = 0.6$, $5$, $15$, and $30$~fm/$c$. A monotonic reduction of $b_{\rm corr}$ with increasing $τ_{\rm HC}$ is observed at all energies and for all window widths, with the ordering of the curves preserved throughout. The effect is modest but statistically significant. These results indicate that the FB correlation strength is primarily imprinted at the partonic stage and only mildly diluted by the subsequent hadronic evolution.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a lattice-QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in isospin-symmetric QCD. We employ the gauge configurations generated by the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with $N_f = 2 + 1 + 1$ flavors of Wilson-clover twisted-mass quarks at four lattice spacings and at values of the quark-mass parameters matching the definition of isospin-symmetric QCD given in the FLAG review 2024 and in the 2025 edition of the Muon $g-2$ Theory Initiative White Paper (WP25). After retuning the simulation parameters to precisely match these two definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD, and after carrying out an extrapolation to the continuum limit based on the data at lattice spacings $a \simeq 0.049, 0.057, 0.068$ and $0.079$~fm, and spatial lattice sizes up to $L \simeq 7.7$~fm, we obtain $a_μ^{\rm HVP, FLAG}(\rm{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9) \times 10^{-10}$ and $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso}) = (714.8 \pm 7.4) \times 10^{-10}$. Our results, which have a relative uncertainty of about $1 \%$, agree well with the corresponding determinations by other lattice groups. After adding to our determination of $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso})$ the leading isospin-breaking corrections provided in the WP25, namely $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}({\rm IB}) = 0.1(3.4)\times 10^{-10}$, we obtain for the full HVP the value $a_μ^{\rm HVP}= (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$. This result translates into a Standard Model prediction for the muon anomalous magnetic moment that is fully consistent with the latest result by the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment and strengthens the tension between lattice QCD and data-driven (pre-CMD3) dispersive determinations.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Partial Next-to-Next-to-Leading-Order Corrections to the $B \to π$ Form Factors from Light-Cone Sum Rules
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: By incorporating the available leading-power results at $\mathcal{O}(α_s)$ and next-to-leading-power corrections at tree level, we compute the $\mathcal{O}(α_s^2β_0)$ contribution to the $B\toπ$ form factors in the large-recoil region using the light-cone sum rule approach with $B$-meson light-cone distribution amplitudes. We find that the QCD corrections at $\mathcal{O}(α_s^2β_0)$ contribute approximately $+6.1\%$ compared to the tree-level result. Combining the light-cone sum rule predictions in the large-recoil region, lattice QCD results in the small-recoil region, we perform a combined fit for the $B\toπ$ form factors across the full kinematic range. Utilizing these form factors, we update the branching ratios, lepton-flavor-universality ratio $R_π$, forward-backward asymmetry $\mathcal{A}_{\rm FB}$, flat term $\mathcal{F}_{\rm H}$ and polarization asymmetry $\mathcal{A}_{λ_\ell}$ of $B\toπμ\barν_μ$ and $B\toπτ\barν_τ$ decays. We also extract the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix element $|V_{ub}| = 3.73(14) \times 10^{-3}$. We find that the resulting shifts are generally small and remain within the uncertainties of previous analyses.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Hadronic Molecules: Theory
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Since the turn of the century it becomes evident that the naive quark model is not capable to describe the rich phenomenology of hadrons, especially in the doubly heavy sector. For a large number of those states a molecular structure appears to be a natural description. In these proceedings I review the theory of hadronic molecules, how they can be described systematically in effective field theories and what imprint this structure leaves in observables. On two examples I explain non-trivial predictions emerging from the molecular hypothesis that can be tested in future experiments and lattice QCD calculations, promising deep insights into the inner workings of QCD.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 11 pages, 3 Figures, Invited talk presented at MESON2026, Cracow, June 2026

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Quantum Popcorn: the shape of a phase transition bubble
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: A quantum tunneling event in field theory is usually depicted as the materialization of a spherical bubble of true vacuum. The bubble appears at rest, and its profile is the time-symmetric slice of Coleman's bounce, the Euclidean solution that controls the decay rate. However, the bubble is spherical only in the leading semiclassical approximation: at the next order the configuration is a Gaussian ensemble of fluctuations around the bounce. We derive the wave functional of the field on the nucleation slice from the half-bounce path integral, and use it to compute the root-mean-square quadrupole moment of a bubble at nucleation. The relative deformation of the bubble wall radius $R$ is $δR/R\sim(\hbar/S_b)^{1/2}$, with $S_b$ the bounce action. Thus $δR/R\sim0.1$ for a typical cosmological phase transition with $S_b/\hbar\sim100$.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Probing dark sector with decihertz gravitational wave observations of compact binary inspirals in IndIGO-D
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate the potential of decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) observations of compact-binary inspirals to probe atomic dark matter (aDM) and its interactions through an ultralight massive dark photon. We consider a scenario in which neutron stars accumulate DM charged under a dark Abelian massive vector mediator, leading to an additional long-range Yukawa interaction between compact objects and associated dipolar radiation. In this framework, the GW waveform acquires characteristic corrections parameterized by the Yukawa coupling strength $α$, the dipole-radiation parameter $γ$, and a parameter related to the mediator mass $μ$. These corrections include a leading $-1$ post-Newtonian dipole contribution and finite-mediator-mass effects. We relate the aDM corrections to existing parameterized tests of general relativity and perform Bayesian parameter-estimation analyses for simulated binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) systems incorporating the modified binary inspiral in a proposed space-based decihertz detector, named IndIGO-D. For a GW170817-like BNS with nonzero aDM couplings chosen near current observational bounds, we find that the dark-photon rest energy can be inferred with a $90\%$ credible uncertainty of $O(10^{-20})\,\mathrm{eV}$, conditional on a detectable dark-sector contribution. Analyses with weaker dark-sector interactions $(α\lesssim O(10^{-8}))$ show that the mediator mass remains unconstrained when both the Yukawa coupling and dipole-radiation contribution are negligible, but can be measured even for a negligible Yukawa coupling if the dipole-radiation contribution is sufficiently strong. Our results demonstrate that future decihertz GW observatories can serve as powerful laboratories for testing dark-sector physics and probing dark matter interactions in compact binaries through precision GW measurements.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Enhanced Cosmic-Ray Cooling in AGN from Dark Matter Deep Inelastic Scattering
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The diffusion of high-energy cosmic rays (CRs) through the dark matter (DM) spikes of active galactic nuclei entails significant energy loss via interactions with DM. While previous studies of sub-GeV DM have focused on elastic scattering, this process becomes insufficient at higher proton energies and DM masses. In this work, we investigate the CR-DM deep inelastic scattering (DIS) as mediated by a vector portal. We calculate the DIS contribution to the CR energy loss rate and derive stringent exclusion limits on the CR-DM scattering cross-section for DM masses between $10^{-6}$ GeV and $1$ GeV. For higher CR energies and mediator masses, the resulting CR cooling timescales are reduced by orders of magnitude after involving the DIS contribution, producing stringent constraints that surpass most of current experimental limits.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 12 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Radiative decays of $J/ψ,\,ψ(2S)\rightarrowγη^{(\prime)}$ in perturbative QCD with relativistic corrections
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present the first calculation of the radiative decays $J/ψ,ψ(2S)\rightarrowγη^{(\prime)}$ in perturbative QCD that includes the order-$q^{2}$ relativistic corrections in all three short-distance contributions, namely the quark-antiquark, two-gluon, and QED contributions. The amplitudes are found to be remarkably insensitive to the light-cone distribution amplitude and to the light-quark mass, a robustness that persists through order $q^{2}$ and makes the predictions correspondingly reliable. The relativistic correction enhances the $J/ψ$ branching ratios by roughly a factor of 2, narrowing their shortfall from experiment, whereas for the $ψ(2S)$ it is about twice as large as for the $J/ψ$ and the low-order expansion converges poorly. In two representative $η$--$η^{\prime}$ mixing schemes, the ratio $\mathcal{R}_{1S}=\mathcal{B}(γη^{\prime})/\mathcal{B}(γη)$ proves sharply sensitive to the mixing angle and favors the smaller of the two. The predicted $ψ(2S)$ rates lie well above the data in both channels, already at leading order, and most severely for the anomalously small $γη$ channel. Such a discrepancy suggests that a mechanism beyond the hard perturbative process is at work. As a physically motivated attempt, we explore the $η_{c}$-mixing contribution, which adds coherently to the perturbative one and is comparable to it in the $γη$ channel, and find that the interference can bring the $ψ(2S)$ rates into agreement with the data, although its extraction is limited by a strong sensitivity to the mixing parameters.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Gravitational form factors of the pion in light-front holographic QCD
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Understanding the internal structure of the pion-particularly the energy-momentum distributions of quarks and gluons and the internal mechanical properties encoded in its gravitational form factors-is a fundamental challenge in quantum chromodynamics (QCD). In this work, we study the gravitational form factors using light-front QCD (LFQCD), combined with the holographic QCD. Our main innovation is the introduction of an effective light-front wave function, with its five-dimensional component obtained from holographic QCD, which is then employed, within the light-front QCD framework, to calculate the pion's gravitational form factors $A(Q^2)$ and $D(Q^2)$ as well as its radius. Our computed pion gravitational form factors show agreement with lattice QCD results, providing nontrivial support for the viability of our phenomenological model.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Searching for Ultra-Light Axions with Twisted Cavity Resonators of Anyon Rotational Symmetry with Bulk Modes of Non-Zero Helicity
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Möbius-ring resonators stem from a well-studied geometrical structure with a one-sided topology, the Möbius strip, and have been shown to exhibit fermion rotational symmetry with respect to an untwisted ring resonator, which exhibits boson rotational symmetry [1]. Here, we present twisted hollow resonators with equilateral triangular cross-sections, leading to cavities with anyon rotational symmetry. Unlike conventional cavity resonators, these structures permit bulk resonant modes with a non-zero complex electromagnetic overlap $\mathcal C_p=\int_V\mathbf{E}_p\cdot\mathbf{B}_p^*\,dτ$. The real and imaginary parts of this overlap couple to different observable quadratures. Although the negative-frequency component of a real axion field is immaterial for haloscopes employing a static DC magnetic field, it must be retained for a pumped resonator because the complex forms of Maxwell's equations differ for positive and negative frequencies and produce distinct upper and lower mixing branches. Retaining both branches shows that the real overlap produces amplitude-modulated sidebands, whereas the imaginary helicity of the modes studied here produces phase-modulated sidebands through the axion-photon chiral anomaly. A sensitive ultra-light dark-matter experiment may therefore be realised with an ultra-stable oscillator and a phase-sensitive readout. The sensitivity curves calculated here require the assumed noise floor to be interpreted as phase-modulation noise rather than amplitude-modulation noise, and consequently require sufficiently low residual oscillator phase noise at the axion Fourier frequency. The scheme removes the usual requirement for an external magnetic field and permits superconducting resonators with reduced surface loss and enhanced axion sensitivity.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: An erratum has been submitted to Physical Review D; this is the corrected article. Correctly treating both axion frequency components gives AM for real field overlap and PM for imaginary overlap (helicity). Sensitivity curves are numerically unchanged if the assumed noise is interpreted as phase noise, requiring sufficiently low residual oscillator and readout phase noise

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Properties of the $D_{s0}^*(2317)^\pm$ in hot and dense nuclear matter
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate the properties of the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^\pm$ in hot and dense nuclear matter using a coupled-channel molecular model built on next-to-leading-order heavy meson chiral perturbation theory. In-medium modifications to the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ stem from changes to the $DK$ channel within the coupled $DK$-$D_s η$ system. As nuclear density increases, the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ quasiparticle peak shifts toward lower energies and broadens, tracking the behavior of the $D$-meson spectral function. As for temperature effects, those are milder, with the thermal smearing of the Fermi surface and the melting of $Σ_c N^{-1}$ excitations in the $D$-meson spectral function shifting the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ peak back toward its free-space mass while narrowing it. Conversely, the behavior of the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$ is governed by the $\bar D \bar K$ channel and its medium behavior is driven by the $\bar K$ spectral function. With increasing temperature, the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$ also approaches its free-space mass, but its width broadens before saturating at high temperatures. Incorporating explicit medium dependencies into the interaction kernel, driven by density and/or temperature variations in the pion decay constant, further shifts the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ mass lower and narrows its width with temperature. As for $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$, its mass also drops with temperature but its width increases. These contrasting medium behaviors offer a promising pathway to constrain the internal structure of these exotic states.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D. Numerical data are available as ancillary files

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Dark axion portal at $Z$ boson factories
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Dark axion portal connects an axion-like-particle (ALP), which can be the QCD axion, with the SM by the coupling to a photon and a dark photon, leading to a rich and distinct phenomenology related to dark matter, astrophysics, and cosmology. We note that due to the gauge invariance, the $Z$ boson-dark photon-ALP coupling should also be generated with sizable strength, and we study its phenomenological consequences at $Z$ boson factories: LEP, FCC-ee, and forward physics detectors at the LHC and FPF@FCC - FASER and MATHUSLA. Due to the large number of $Z$ bosons produced, DAP particles can be efficiently produced and detected by semi-visible displaced decays of the heavier DS species to $γ$+inv. or $f^+ f^-$+inv., and via missing energy signature with zero or one photon. Because of the complementarity of the two approaches, we find great prospects in exploring both short and long-lived lifetime regimes of DAP, especially when the heavier dark species has mass above $0.1\,$GeV.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Application of flavor moonshine
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In our previous paper [1], we presented the application of Moonshine to the flavor physics based on the work of Cohn and Deutsch and Bagger and Wess [2], J. Conway and S. Norton [3] and T.Eguchi, H.Ooguri and Y.Tachikawa [4] laid down the mathematical basics. We present here the extension of our previous paper [1] by including the supersymmetry in addition to the modular symmetry [1], [4]. We calculate all the lepton masses and the quark masses and their super partner masses by using the one input particle mass for each family. The two valued modular function is defined in equation (3.7). We define the two valued modular function of degree K in equation (3.2). We use K = 1 two valued modular function for the charged leptons and K = 2 two valued modular function for the neutrino and for the up quarks, and K = 3 two valued modular function for the down quarks, where 2K is the level of the two valued modular function. We emphasize that we have three particle masses which can be measured by the existing accelerators such as KEK B factory or CERN LHC. One is super electron mass "M_{e,s} = 24.73MeV", which is approximately 25 times that of electron. The Super d, s and b quark masses are 0GeV, 89.165GeV, and 2964.7GeV. Super down quark mass is 0 and super strange quark mass can be measured both in KEKB and in CERN LHC. The super bottom quark mass can be measured only in LHC.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Updated $Σ_{c}$ excitation spectrum including the $2P$- and $1F$-wave fine structures
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In order to study the new $Σ_{c}$ baryons observed by the LHCb collaboration recently, we update the previously predicted $Σ_{c}$ excitation spectrum by extending the excited states up to the highly excited $2P$- and $1F$-wave states. The calculation is performed in the framework of the relativized quark model and Gaussian expansion method by considering the mixing effect. The radially and orbitally excited states in the calculation are determined by the truncation convention proposed in this work and the mechanism of the heavy-quark dominance. The contribution of each Hamiltonian term to the energy levels is precisely calculated by using the two-step Gaussian expansion method. Then, the concerned $Σ_{c}$ states are obtained and the $Σ_{c}$ excitation spectrum including the $2P$- and $1F$-wave fine structures is established. Based on these, several important topics are discussed and analyzed, including the root-mean-square radii, off-diagonal matrix elements, mixing effect, fine structures and assignments of the newly observed $Σ_{c}(2800)^{0}$, $Σ_{c}(2900)^{0}$ and $Σ_{c}(3200)^{0}$ states. Meanwhile, it is found that the approximate decoupling phenomenon emerges in different $nL$-wave groups. This implies the reasonability of the truncation convention and is of great significance for further improving the calculation scheme for all the baryon spectra. Moreover, it is demonstrated that in the very high-lying $nL$-wave groups such as the $1F$-wave group, the energy level gaps become small even degenerate, and each of the baryon states has a big radius and therefore a loosely bound structure. In addition, by examining the experimental and calculated data, we suggest more precise experiments to search for more $Σ_{c}$ baryon states in the predicted $1P$- and $2P$-wave fine structures whose central energies are around 2822 and 3210 MeV, respectively.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: HWF Analysis of TRN Black Holes
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We extend the horizon wave-function (HWF) formalism to a spherically symmetric, charged, spinless quantum source in $\mathcal{D} + 1$ dimensional spacetime geometry and construct the HWFs associated with inner- as well as outer-horizons of the Tangherlini--Reissner--Nordström (TRN) black hole. The corresponding black hole formation probabilities, $P_{\rm BH}^{\pm}$, are also calculated and their sensitivities due to various source parameters including charge, mass, and $\mathcal{D}$ are analysed as well. Our analysis reveals that the ratio of inner- to outer-horizon probabilities, $P_{\rm BH}^{-}/P_{\rm BH}^{+}$, changes drastically from being unity as the source departs away from being in the extremal limit defined by $α$ ($\to 1$ for extremal case). Furthermore, black hole formation probabilities are found to be highly suppressed for higher values of $\mathcal{D}$, particularly for the source mass, $m \lesssim Λ_{\mathcal{D}}$, e.g., for $α= 0.5$, the ratio, $P_{\rm BH}^{+}(\mathcal{D} = 5)/P_{\rm BH}^{+}(\mathcal{D}=10)$ turn out to be approximately $2.95\times10^3$, $117$, and $3.35$ respectively for $m/Λ_{\mathcal{D}} = 0.5, 1$ and $2$, with $Λ_{\mathcal{D}}$ being the reduced gravity scale associated with $\mathcal{D}$ spatial-dimensions.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Neutrino mass predictions with metaheuristic optimization under $A_4$ modular symmetry
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The current research aims to conduct an exhaustive investigation of the neutrino mass model based on $A_4$ discrete non-abelian modular symmetry, specifically in the context of the linear seesaw mechanism, where the conventional type I seesaw mechanism is extended, with particular attention given to the optimization of the parameters using incomprehensible but intelligible-in-time logics optimization algorithm (ILA), a metaheuristic optimization. Unlike other approaches to discrete flavor symmetry, the modular approach to flavor dynamics is found to significantly reduce the number and complexity of flavon fields required to give realistic textures to fermion masses. The key predictions include neutrino masses, $U_\text{PMNS}$ matrices, effective neutrino masses for neutrinoless double beta decay, beta decay, Dirac and Majorana CP violation phases for normal (NO) and inverted mass ordering (IO), offering testable implications. The working efficiency of the ILA optimization technique is also estimated. The optimized neutrino oscillation parameters are well consistent with recent experimental data. Our analysis also aligns with Planck cosmological constraints on the sum of neutrino masses $0.06<Σm<0.12\ \text{eV}$.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Nonthermal coalescence parameter of light nuclei production in pp collisions at LHC energies
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study the light nucleus production in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=7$ and $13$~TeV reported by the ALICE Collaboration within the color string fragmentation framework. We adopt the Schwinger mechanism with string tension fluctuations as the particle production mechanism describing the $p_T$ spectrum. The approximately thermal behavior observed in the light-nucleus spectra motivates the use of a perturbative series expansion of the $q$-Gaussian string tension fluctuations around $q=1$. The resulting $p_T$ spectrum is expressed as a perturbative series expansion around the thermal distribution with nonthermal corrections given by Gamma distributions, providing closed forms for the effective temperature, moments, and cumulants. In the superstatistical framework, the associated temperature fluctuations show that the medium in which light nuclei are produced is out of equilibrium. Additionally, we derive closed formulas for the coalescence parameter at arbitrary order, which agree well with experimental data. Our results also show that the mass--temperature relation ($T_N/m_N \approx AT_A/m_A$) between the nucleons and nuclei is not preserved in the coalescence process.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Toward a Three-Body Holonomy Standard Model
High Energy Phenomenology.summary:
We propose a phenomenological framework toward a Three-Body Holonomy Standard Model in which the number three is selected by the minimal primitive cyclic structure of a democratic many-body interaction network. The resulting threefold holonomy information is assumed to survive in $(3+1)$ dimensions as an internal three-state space.
  A Lorentz-invariant six-fermion interaction provides a candidate microscopic origin of the internal cyclic correlations, with their matching to Wilson holonomy left as a dynamical requirement. The parity-related holonomy sectors of the underlying $(1+1)$-dimensional Dirac system motivate left- and right-handed internal structures and a trinification-like $SU(3)_C\times SU(3)_L\times SU(3)_R$ gauge completion.
