We then examine physical observables that change prominently between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes. In particular, we calculate the evolution of the physical-electron spectral function and identify characteristic signatures in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. We find a pronounced contrast in low-energy spectral weight between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes without requiring conventional symmetry-breaking order. Our results establish finite-temperature orthogonal-metal physics as a possible mechanism for pseudogap-like behavior in three-dimensional and quasi-two-dimensional layered materials with non-negligible interlayer hopping, which may be applied to the recent experiments in $\mathrm{Sr_2 VO_3 Fe As}$.

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Collective Modes of Fractional States Beyond Landau Levels
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: Collective modes provide a powerful probe into the properties and stability of topologically ordered and strongly interacting phases of matter, such as fractional quantum Hall states. Yet, the description of fractional-state excitations away from the Landau-level limit remains a formidable challenge. We develop a framework for describing collective excitations in the strong-coupling regime of coupled-wire constructions and show that they emerge as solitons and breathers of effective sine-Gordon theories. This approach provides a systematic route to studying collective modes in a broad class of fractional states. Applied to a coupled-wire construction of the fractional quantum Hall effect, the framework captures key features of the magnetoroton branch. It naturally extends to fractional Chern insulators, demonstrating that magnetoroton-like collective modes persist well beyond the Landau-level limit. We find that the magnetoroton gap increases as the Fubini-Study metric approaches the ideal (trace-condition) limit, highlighting the important role of quantum geometry in the stability of fractionalized phases and their collective excitations. The same trend favors the stability of the long-wavelength quadrupolar mode associated with the chiral graviton. Together, these results identify a distinct interplay between fractionalization and quantum geometry, and provide an analytical framework for studies of collective excitations in fractional topological matter.

Nuclear Theory.title: Effects of Competing Reactions on $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ on Abundance Distributions in Type I X-Ray Bursts
Nuclear Theory.summary: The composition of X-ray burst ashes affects the thermal transport properties of the neutron star crust, as well as heating and cooling through weak interaction processes. Reaction-rate uncertainties can produce secondary peaks separated from the main peak in final abundance distributions. Using STARLIB reaction rates and their temperature-dependent uncertainties in the K04 one-zone post-processing model, we combine four sets of Monte Carlo calculations with XGBoost classification, SHAP analysis, and reaction-flow analysis to investigate the origins of these secondary peaks. We find that the competing $(p,α)$ and $(p,γ)$ reaction pairs on $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ are primarily responsible for secondary peaks outside the central 68\% confidence interval in all 44 isotopes examined. Fixing both pairs at their median rates reduces the fractions of samples in the secondary-peak regions by 96\%--100\%, while the bounds of the central 68\% interval remain largely unchanged for most mass numbers. The $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ pair has the larger effect. Enhanced recycling limits the supply of material to heavier isotopes and accelerates proton consumption, while earlier proton exhaustion further suppresses subsequent proton captures. These changes alter the balance between isotope production and destruction, leading to high- or low-abundance secondary peaks over a broad mass range beyond the Ni--Cu and Zn--Ga cycles. These results identify $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}(p,γ)^{60}\mathrm{Zn}$ and the two competing channels on $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ as priorities for further nuclear-physics constraints to improve XRB abundance predictions.

Nuclear Theory.title: Extracting Meson Distribution Amplitudes from Nonlocal Euclidean Correlations at Next-to-Next-to-Leading Order
Nuclear Theory.summary: We present the first complete result for the next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) hard matching kernel indispensable for a precision extraction of light meson distribution amplitudes from lattice calculations of equal-time nonlocal Euclidean correlation functions. The results are given in both coordinate and momentum space, with the renormalization and matching accomplished in a state-of-the-art scheme. Our results can be used in both large-momentum effective theory and short-distance factorization approaches. Notably, our coordinate space kernel is directly applicable to nonsinglet quark unpolarized and helicity generalized parton distributions as well. We also illustrate the numerical impact of the NNLO matching, using the pion distribution amplitude as an example.
Nuclear Theory.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures. Supplementary Mathematica notebook (Matching_coefficient.nb) is included

Nuclear Theory.title: Exact factorization of finite-range three-body matrix elements between Gaussian wave packets and its application to the $0^+$ states of $^{12}C$
Nuclear Theory.summary: We introduce finite-range three-body interactions into the $β-γ$-constrained generator coordinate method of antisymmetrized molecular dynamics. These genuine operators give saturation without an additional prescription for the projection, but require $O(A^6)$ complex exponentials at every node of the projection grid. With the graph Laplacian of the ranges, as in spectral clustering widely used in machine learning, we factorize the exponential factor of a Gaussian three-body kernel exactly into pairwise tables of $O(A^2)$ exponentials. A cofactor expansion rewrites the remaining contraction as complex matrix-matrix products. For $^{12}C$, the factorization reduces the time of the kernels with the three-body term from $530$ to $24$ times that of the two-body kernels. We apply the method to the $0^+$ states of $^{12}C$ with the Volkov, Tohsaki F1, and Kanada-En'yo--Akaishi F3B interactions, restricting the intrinsic states to time-reversal-invariant ones. Without the three-body terms of F1 and F3B, $^{12}C$ collapses far below the three $α$ threshold, whereas with them the ground state lies close to its experimental position below the threshold. When we adjust the Majorana parameter to this position, the Hoyle state lies within 0.6 MeV of experiment for all three interactions.

Nuclear Theory.title: Jet quenching and its substructure dependence due to color decoherence
Nuclear Theory.summary: Motivated by color coherence and decoherence effects in the QCD medium, we propose a theoretical framework that combines vacuum-like emissions and medium-induced radiation to study jet quenching and its dependence on jet cone sizes and substructure. In our approach, a jet produced at a hard scale $Q$ first undergoes vacuum-like evolution, as described by the well-established generating-function method in the double logarithmic approximation. These vacuum-like emissions generate subjets at an infrared momentum scale $Q_0$. Each subjet then experiences medium-induced energy loss as described by the BDMPS-Z formalism. By modeling the QCD bulk medium using OSU (2+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamics and treating $Q_0$ together with the jet-quenching parameters at the initial proper time of the hydrodynamic evolution as free parameters, our approach provides a very good description of the inclusive jet modification factor $R_{AA}$ for large-radius jets and its dependence on jet substructure in 0-10% PbPb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\rm{TeV}$, as measured by the ATLAS experiment.

Nuclear Theory.title: Numerical study of the three-boson bound-state problem in partial-wave and vector-variable formulations
Nuclear Theory.summary: We present a systematic benchmark of the three-boson bound-state problem in momentum space, comparing one-dimensional (1D) spectator-amplitude, two-dimensional (2D) partial-wave, and three-dimensional (3D) vector-variable formulations. The benchmark controls the interaction representation by embedding the same finite partial-wave interaction space in each formulation, so that discrepancies reflect discretization, interpolation, and quadrature errors. This enables direct 1D--2D--3D comparisons for separable interactions, controlled 2D--3D tests for local interactions, and comparison with the full local interaction in the 3D vector-variable formulation. Binding energies agree at the $10^{-6}$~MeV level for the separable interactions. For the local interactions at $l_{\rm max}=12$, the 2D--3D differences are $2.2\times10^{-6}$~MeV for MT-V and $5.3\times10^{-5}$~MeV for MT-IV. The 2D and 3D equations are also solved in both $t$-matrix-driven and bare-potential-driven forms, whose agreement validates the permutation geometry, quadrature, and interpolation. Fourier transforms to coordinate space yield consistent norm decompositions and spatial observables, providing an independent check of the momentum-space solutions.

Nuclear Theory.title: Symmetry energy effect on hot nuclear matter and proto-neutron stars
Nuclear Theory.summary: We examine the effects of symmetry energy on proto-neutron stars (PNSs) by employing equation of state (EOS) described by the relativistic mean-field (RMF) model. The thermal properties of dense matter and the bulk properties of PNSs are investigated under the assumptions of isothermy, isentropy, and fixed lepton fractions. The polytropic index is calculated at finite temperature, revealing a negative correlation with the PNS maximum mass that the EOS can support. The properties of PNSs during the heating and cooling stages along their evolution line are explored under different combinations of lepton fraction and entropy. We investigate the correlation between the symmetry energy slope $L$ and the properties of PNSs. As $L$ increases, the PNS radius also increases; however, this effect diminishes with a growing lepton fraction for the isentropic case. These results indicate that the nuclear symmetry energy and its density dependence play crucial roles in determining the properties of PNSs and their evolution stages.

Nuclear Theory.title: Higher-Order Symmetry Energy Effects on the Properties of Neutron Stars
Nuclear Theory.summary: We study the effects of the symmetry-energy curvature $K_{\rm sym}$ on the equation of state (EoS) and neutron-star properties within the relativistic mean-field (RMF) framework. We construct controlled families of RMF parametrizations based on the TM1 and IUFSU models by varying $K_{\rm sym}$ while keeping the symmetry energy $J$ and its slope $L$ fixed at saturation density. We find that, although a larger $K_{\rm sym}$ leads to a lower symmetry energy at suprasaturation densities and a reduced proton fraction in $β$-equilibrated matter, it results in a stiffer EoS and a higher sound speed. The maximum neutron-star mass is weakly affected, whereas the canonical radius $R_{1.4}$ exhibits a nearly linear dependence on $K_{\rm sym}$.

Nuclear Theory.title: Accounting for correlations in the $ωπ$ spectral function and its implication on the leading model dependent contribution to the $τ^- \to π^-π^0 ν_τγ$ decay
Nuclear Theory.summary: The $ωπ$ spectral function, measured in the decay $τ^- \to π^-ων_τ$ by the CLEO Collaboration, is described in the vector meson dominance approach. We sample the parameter space using a Metropolis Monte-Carlo algorithm and generate a set of parameters of the corresponding form factor, explicitly accounting for the correlation among them. We show the improvement in the uncertainty region of the spectral function with respect to neglecting correlations. We test the conserved vector current hypothesis by showing the agreement of the spectral function with the expected from the measurement of the cross section of $e^+e^- \to ωπ$ by the SND experiment, and the consistency of the branching ratio of the $τ^- \to π^-ων_τ$ decay with the value reported by the Particle Data Group. As an application, we consider the $ω$-channel of the $τ^- \to π^-π^0ν_τγ$ process, the leading model dependent contribution in the vector meson dominance approach. We compute the contribution to the long distance electromagnetic correction function $G_\text{EM}(t)$, of the pure $ω$-channel and its interference with the structure independent part. We show that the uncertainties, using the set of correlated parameters, are largely reduced with respect to neglecting correlations. The implication on the isospin symmetry breaking correction to the muon magnetic dipole moment estimation from tau data is found to be consistent with previous results but with improved precision.

Nuclear Theory.title: Chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in flavor branes
Nuclear Theory.summary: We investigate the chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in the chiral symmetry broken phase of the holographic D3/D7 model with massless quarks, where the axial charge in the flavor sector can relax through transfer to the adjoint sector in the probe limit. We find that the dispersion relations of the quasi-normal modes are well described by the phenomenological expression for the chiral magnetic wave when the relaxation rate is small. We then determine how this rate depends on vector charge density and the chiral condensate. At higher temperatures, it increases with charge density and decreases with increasing condensate, while these dependences become non-monotonic at lower temperatures. These results show that the phenomenological description of the chiral magnetic wave also applies in the chiral symmetry broken phase in the quasi-hydrodynamic regime.

Nuclear Theory.title: Solar axions from nuclear transitions
Nuclear Theory.summary: We investigate the possibility of detecting 14.4~keV and 9.4~keV solar axions and axion-like particles that could be produced in the M1 nuclear transitions of $^{57}\mathrm{Fe}$ and $^{83}\mathrm{Kr}$, respectively. To do so, we used data from soft X-ray observations of the quiet Sun collected by the Solar X-ray Monitor (XSM) on board India's Chandrayaan-2 lunar mission. We observe that although the effective axion-nucleon couplings for $^{83}\mathrm{Kr}$ and $^{57}\mathrm{Fe}$ differ only slightly, their fluxes differ by nearly three orders of magnitude. Consequently, the limit on $|g_{aN}^{\rm eff} \times g_{aγγ}|$ and only $g_{aγγ}$ vs. $m_a$ provide more than one order of magnitude stronger constraint for Fe than for Kr.
Nuclear Theory.comment: 22 pages, 8 figures, 1 table. Updated to the version published in JCAP

Nuclear Theory.title: From wave-function to fireball geometry: the role of a restored broken symmetry in ultra-relativistic collisions of deformed nuclei
Nuclear Theory.summary: Monte Carlo (MC) Glauber models for high-energy nuclear collisions conventionally treat deformed nuclei as classical rotors, encoding deformation in the one-body distribution of a single intrinsic state. The physical nuclear ground state, however, is rotationally invariant and describes a quantum rotor: a coherent superposition of intrinsic states at different orientations, with shape information encoded in many-nucleon correlations. For axially deformed even-even nuclei, we develop a modified MC Glauber sampling procedure consistent with this rotational symmetry. The model retains information off-diagonal in the basis of orientations through an angular overlap function and a generalized thickness function. We provide a practical prescription for computing both quantities and show that the rotational symmetry of the nuclear ground state is important in central collisions involving light, strongly deformed nuclei: for ${}^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$, the elliptic eccentricity is reduced by approximately $10\%$ level relative to the classical-rotor treatment. These results highlight the importance of incorporating quantum-mechanical constraints when relating intrinsic nuclear deformation to the QGP geometry in relativistic nuclear collisions.
Nuclear Theory.comment: 15 pages, 3 figures. Still under review, but some updates are important and will be used for a coming long paper

Nuclear Theory.title: Convergence of many-body truncations in the in-medium similarity renormalization group
Nuclear Theory.summary: The in-medium similarity renormalization group (IMSRG) is a leading \textit{ab initio} method for describing atomic nuclei. Most applications truncate the flowing operators at the normal-ordered two-body level, neglecting induced higher-body terms. Convergence with increasing operator rank remains poorly understood, particularly in strongly correlated systems. We systematically assess the many-body truncation hierarchy in the single-reference and multi-reference IMSRG, retaining normal-ordered operators through the four-body and three-body levels, respectively. Using an exactly solvable pairing-plus-particle-hole model, we quantify successive higher-body corrections over a broad range of interaction strengths, spanning weakly to strongly correlated regimes. The multi-reference formulation exhibits faster and more robust convergence than its single-reference counterpart, with the advantage becoming most pronounced at strong coupling. In this regime, higher-rank irreducible density matrices play an essential role in achieving convergence of the many-body expansion.

Nuclear Theory.title: Simultaneous $αβ$ Decay: A New Mode of Nuclear Instability
Nuclear Theory.summary: We propose simultaneous $αβ$ decay as a novel mode of nuclear instability that involves the strong and weak interactions in a single quantum transition. We develop a theoretical framework to predict its branching ratios and $α$-energy spectra, establishing exclusive and inclusive criteria based on whether the individual $α$ and $β$ channels are closed or open. A global survey of the nuclear chart identifies five exclusive $αβ^-$ candidates, all predicted to be experimentally inaccessible, and ranks the leading inclusive candidates for both the $αβ^-$ and $αβ^+$ modes. Remarkably, six of the top $αβ^+$ candidates coincide with known $β$-delayed-$α$ precursors. The observed $α$ spectra are naturally accounted for by simultaneous $αβ^+$ emission without additional assumptions, indicating a substantial and possibly dominant direct component. Our findings establish simultaneous $αβ$ decay as a distinct radioactive process and a sensitive probe of the interplay between the strong and weak interactions.

Nuclear Theory.title: Examining the accessibility of the compressibility of nuclear matter from nuclear experiments
Nuclear Theory.summary: The most accurate approach to determine the compressibility of nuclear matter remains the one based on microscopic Energy Density Functionals (EDFs). Recent analyses yield a value for nuclear incompressibility modulus $K_\sat=240\pm 20$~MeV, defined in nuclear matter as the second derivative of the energy per particle at saturation density. However, we demonstrate that the compressibility modulus can be reduced to values shifted by four times the suggested uncertainty, i.e., $K_\sat\approx 160$~MeV, by providing examples based on models where the second derivative ($K_\sat$) and third derivative ($Q_\sat$) of the energy per particle at saturation density can be independently varied, while the experimental binding energies, charge radii, and ISGMR data in $^{120}$Sn and $^{208}$Pb are enforced. The present work suggests a new methodology to access the compressibility of nuclear matter from nuclear experiments, still based on microscopic models, but using EDFs containing more flexibility than the ones employed up to now. Consequences of our results for nuclear matter at supra-saturation density are also discussed by exploring the quarkyonic cross-over. We predict that, for our models with low values for $K_\sat$, the quark onset density has to be low for neutron stars to exist.

Nuclear Theory.title: Proton GTMDs and Wigner Distributions in the Chiral Quark Soliton Model: Orbital Angular Momentum and Spin-Orbit Correlation with Sea Quarks
Nuclear Theory.summary: We calculate the leading-twist vector and axial-vector quark generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) of the proton in the chiral quark soliton model, including both the discrete valence level and the regularized Dirac sea. We consider the isosinglet and isotriplet combinations of GTMDs at zero and nonzero skewness. At zero skewness, we construct Wigner distributions and resolve the orbital angular momentum (OAM) and spin-orbit correlation (SOC) densities in transverse position and momentum space, separately for quarks and antiquarks. This provides a phase-space picture of the sea-quark and sea-antiquark contributions, displaying OAM aligned with the proton spin and anti-aligned with the partons' own spin.
Nuclear Theory.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables, v2: references added

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Higgs boson decays into gauge bosons: theoretical predictions in RNS
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We discuss recent results on the loop-induced decays $h\to Zγ$, $h\toγγ$, and $h\to gg$ in the Radiatively Natural Supersymmetry (RNS) framework. These processes are sensitive to contributions from particles beyond the Standard Model and provide complementary probes of supersymmetric effects. We evaluate the decay amplitudes and partial widths for parameter points consistent with a Higgs boson mass near the measured value of 125 GeV, and examine their dependence on the model parameters. Across the parameter space, the predicted $h\to Zγ$ width can reach about 7.5 keV, while the $h\toγγ$ and $h\to gg$ widths remain close to their Standard Model predictions. We compare the $h\to Zγ$ predictions with the available ATLAS and CMS measurements and discuss the prospects for distinguishing RNS from the Standard Model with improved experimental precision.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Extrapolation and explainability in hadron mass predictions with machine learning
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In this work, we study the predictive performance of four machine learning (ML) models for hadron masses, with particular attention to extrapolation beyond the conventional hadrons represented in the training data. Calculations are performed using a multilayer perceptron (MLP), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and Gaussian process regression (GPR). ML models are trained on conventional hadrons, using features that describe valence quark content and quantum numbers. Then, we evaluate their performance on test sets and on a separate extrapolation set of 39 states, including exotic candidates and heavy baryons, none of which appear in the training or test sets. We find that the MLP achieves the lowest extrapolation Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) on the $30$ states with measured masses at $294.2 \pm 57.9$~MeV, roughly one-third that of the other models. We also show that the MLP reproduces the overall mass scale of nine unobserved doubly heavy baryons predicted by theoretical calculations, although it underestimates the doubly bottom masses. We use SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis and show that heavy quark content is the most significant factor in the MLP's mass predictions, with the remaining features contributing differently across hadron types. Our results quantify the extrapolation accuracy of ML models for hadron masses and identify the features that drive the MLP predictions.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Expanding Coulomb field
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We briefly discuss vector field theories that allow for electric charge non-conservation and focus on the modified version of the classical Maxwell theory, where the Lagrangian density has the same structure as in the Gupta-Bleuler theory with an external current-vector field coupling. Within this framework, we study the causal dynamics of the field configuration following the sudden creation of an electric charge modeled by an external current. The resulting solution describes an expanding Coulomb field, which is an inherently dynamical object featuring a shockwave-like front propagating at the speed of light (the Coulomb field is confined to the volume swept out by this front). We obtain intriguing results for the energy of the studied field configuration and for the energy carried by the shockwave-like front. General results on the dynamics following the sudden onset of an otherwise static external current are given. The field equations are solved in an unconventional way by means of a quantum-to-classical mapping. An energy-based argument against charge non-conservation in the Maxwell theory is presented.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Reinforcement Learning in High-Energy Physics: A Survey from Accelerator Control to Theory Exploration
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a machine learning paradigm in which an agent learns a decision-making policy by interacting with an environment, guided by a scalar reward rather than explicit supervision. Supervised and unsupervised learning have become indispensable tools in high-energy physics (HEP), but they learn from fixed datasets, whereas many HEP tasks are closed-loop decisions: the data an algorithm observes depend on its choices, the feedback is sparse or delayed, and the objective is often measured on a real machine or in a stochastic simulation, not by a differentiable model. This survey reviews the application of RL to such tasks: accelerator control and feedback, data quality monitoring, jet grooming, clustering, and representation, charged particle tracking, beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) and string model building, detector design, trigger control, analysis, and formal quantum field theory computation. It provides a self-contained introduction to the underlying RL methods, from model-free and model-based to multi-agent, offline, inverse, and bandit approaches, reviews each domain against its traditional methods, and summarizes the head-to-head comparisons. The applications range from policies deployed on real accelerators and evaluated on recorded collision data to exploratory studies in formal theory. RL is most advantageous for repeated tasks with a fast simulator, decisions inside fast control loops, operation under faults and corrupted measurements, physics-based rewards in place of labels, and sequential discrete constructions with a reusable policy, while Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms, and differentiable methods remain competitive elsewhere. We conclude with the open challenges that recur across domains, including reward design, sim-to-real transfer, safety, the lack of shared benchmarks, and the statistical validity of policy-driven decisions.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Topological Defect Statistics in a Weakly First-Order Phase Transition
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The celebrated Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM) characterizes the nonequilibrium dynamics of second-order phase transitions and predicts universal scaling of the average number of defects with the quench time. However, the KZM is not directly applicable to first-order phase transitions, where defect formation is instead governed by nucleation processes. Here, using a Ginzburg-Landau model, we investigate the defect-number statistics in a weakly first-order phase transition. We show that the resulting statistics contain signatures of both Kibble-Zurek dynamics and nucleation, revealing the interplay between these two defect-formation mechanisms. In particular, we find that the defect-number distribution evolves from approximately Gaussian to nearly Poissonian across the crossover from the KZM regime to nucleation-dominated defect formation. While the first two cumulants are well described by a simple additive estimate of the KZM and nucleation contributions, the third cumulant exhibits a plateau and an enhancement beyond this estimate, providing a sensitive probe of the interplay between the two defect-formation mechanisms.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Electroweak-Scale Cosmic Magnetism: Magnetogenesis, Baryogenesis, Phase Transitions and Gravitational Waves
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Magnetic fields, the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, and stochastic gravitational waves provide complementary probes of physics in the early Universe. Near the electroweak scale, these phenomena are not necessarily independent. The electroweak anomaly allows hypermagnetic helicity to exchange charge with chiral fermions, sphalerons can change baryon and lepton number, and first-order phase transitions in extensions of the Standard Model can drive plasma motion, magnetogenesis, and gravitational waves. In this review, we explain these connections and examine the literature needed to make quantitative predictions. We begin with the properties of primordial magnetic fields and the electroweak plasma, then discuss the mechanisms that produce magnetic fields, the conversion between helicity and baryon number, magnetic backreaction, and the evolution of the field to the present day. We also review the observational constraints and recent developments, including gauge-invariant descriptions of magnetic flux through the crossover and reconnection-controlled field evolution. Particular attention is given to the assumptions behind commonly used formulas and to the distinction between established results and model-dependent estimates. We argue that the most useful way forward is to predict the baryon abundance, present-day magnetic-field spectrum, and gravitational-wave signal from the same microscopic model, with consistent treatment of the intervening plasma dynamics.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Boundedness from below in the real Weinberg three-Higgs-doublet model
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study the boundedness-from-below (BFB) conditions of the quartic potential in the real Weinberg three-Higgs-doublet model (3HDM). Unlike an analysis restricted to neutral Higgs fields, a complete stability test must also allow for charge-breaking directions. We show that the problem can be reduced to a finite set of 28 stationary configurations, 14 neutral and 14 charged, each of which can be treated using a linear system of size at most four. The main simplification comes from the one-dimensional kernel of the Gram matrix for charged configurations, while the phase equations reduce to two possibilities: aligned phases or phases forming a closed triangle. We further show how to deal exactly with singular choices of the couplings by introducing an auxiliary deformation and taking an algebraic limit. For rational couplings, the normalized minimum is rational and an attaining field configuration can be constructed algebraically. We discuss analytical examples, exact checks, and comparisons with numerical minimization and StableWein. Our result applies to arbitrary real quartic couplings; it does not cover complex phase coefficients or settle the full-potential stability problem when the quartic is flat.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Momentum entanglement at colliders: the $H \to WW,ZZ$ case
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We address momentum entanglement in Higgs decays to weak boson pairs, $H \to WW,ZZ$, by discretising momentum space. The momenta of the two weak bosons are entangled, as well as the degrees of freedom in momentum and spin spaces. For $H \to ZZ$ in the four-lepton final state, we also estimate the statistical sensitivity of entanglement measures at the Large Hadron Collider and future upgrades. The discretisation method introduced here is broadly applicable, offering a framework for studies of momentum entanglement at the energy frontier.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: LaTeX 9 pages. Added caveats and explanations. Final version to appear in PRD

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Gravitational form factors of the baryon octet and flavor dependence in an NJL quark--diquark model
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We calculate the gravitational form factors of the baryon octet in a proper-time-regulated Nambu--Jona-Lasinio quark--diquark model using the total energy--momentum tensor. The momentum, angular-momentum and stress form factors reveal different flavor dependences, and the momentum and stress slope radii follow distinct hierarchies. With the diquark pole inputs taken from the hadron-spectrum calculation, the $Σ$ is more compact than the nucleon in its momentum response but more extended in its normalized stress response; it also has the smallest magnitude of the forward stress form factor. This combination of weaker forward strength and larger normalized extent persists under separate variations of the scalar and axial-vector diquark couplings. Along a self-consistent flavor-breaking path the initially degenerate radii split, and the sampled $Σ$--nucleon stress-radius ordering changes while the momentum ordering does not. The metric continuation and external pole inputs further change these hierarchies. Together, the octet form factors show how flavor breaking and scalar and axial-vector correlations affect momentum and stress differently.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Flavor from Consistency: Qualified-Axion, Anomaly Cancellation, and Emergent Unification
High Energy Phenomenology.summary:
We present a framework for flavored grand unification theory (flavored-GUT) in string-derived supergravity based on $G_{\rm SM}\times SL(2,\mathbb{Z})\times U(1)_X\times U(1)_{B-L}$, where gravity is intrinsically incorporated. We show that anomaly cancellation and Standard Model gauge coupling unification act as fundamental consistency conditions that determine the flavor structure, rather than treating flavor as an independent input. Mixed $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$, $U(1)_{X}$, $U(1)_{B-L}$, and gravitational anomalies are shown to vanish, with the anomalies induced by K{ä}hler transformations matched by those from chiral rotations of gauginos. For nontrivial $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ transformations of SM fermions, the anomaly-free conditions impose strong constraints on the quark and lepton flavor structures while leaving the strong CP phase unchanged. Quark and lepton mass hierarchies, mixing patterns, and the flavored Peccei-Quinn sector emerge from the same underlying structure. The consistency conditions fix the $U(1)_X$ breaking scale, identified with the Froggatt-Nielsen cutoff scale, thereby determining the QCD axion decay constant and predicting the axion mass $m_a=3.35\times10^{-8}$ eV, while simultaneously constraining the supersymmetry-breaking scale of ${\cal O}(10)$TeV and the seesaw scale.
  We show that the moduli are stabilized and that gauge-invariance-induced quantized nonperturbative indices are constrained by vacuum stability. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the fundamental consistency conditions dynamically realizes a qualified QCD axion. Our results establish a predictive framework connecting flavor physics, anomaly cancellation, SM gauge coupling unification, neutrino mass generation, gravitational dynamics, and axion physics, without invoking a conventional simple unified gauge group.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: Revised the scalar potential and Qualified-QCD axion, a compelling motivation for SM gauge-coupling unification. Added 11 plots

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Jet quenching and its substructure dependence due to color decoherence
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Motivated by color coherence and decoherence effects in the QCD medium, we propose a theoretical framework that combines vacuum-like emissions and medium-induced radiation to study jet quenching and its dependence on jet cone sizes and substructure. In our approach, a jet produced at a hard scale $Q$ first undergoes vacuum-like evolution, as described by the well-established generating-function method in the double logarithmic approximation. These vacuum-like emissions generate subjets at an infrared momentum scale $Q_0$. Each subjet then experiences medium-induced energy loss as described by the BDMPS-Z formalism. By modeling the QCD bulk medium using OSU (2+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamics and treating $Q_0$ together with the jet-quenching parameters at the initial proper time of the hydrodynamic evolution as free parameters, our approach provides a very good description of the inclusive jet modification factor $R_{AA}$ for large-radius jets and its dependence on jet substructure in 0-10% PbPb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\rm{TeV}$, as measured by the ATLAS experiment.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: EEXICC: An event generator for doubly heavy baryon production at $e^+e^-$ colliders
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present EEXICC, a Monte Carlo event generator designed to simulate the production of doubly heavy baryons ($Ξ_{cc}$, $Ξ_{bc}$, and $Ξ_{bb}$) via $e^+e^-$ annihilation. Based on nonrelativistic QCD effective theory, the generator calculates the process $e^{+}+e^{-}\rightarrow Ξ_{QQ'}+\bar{Q}'+\bar{Q}$ using an improved trace technique at the amplitude level, which greatly improves numerical efficiency compared with traditional squared-amplitude methods. EEXICC uses a modular Fortran implementation for hard-process generation and a C++ interface to the bundled PYTHIA 8.317 library, enabling convenient integration into complete event simulation workflows. The program supports both weighted and unweighted event generation, and its numerical reliability has been verified against existing theoretical results. EEXICC provides a flexible and robust tool for studying the properties of doubly heavy baryons at future high-luminosity and high-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders such as the CEPC and FCC-ee.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: A General Manifestly Covariant Construction of Partial-Wave Amplitudes in the Rarita-Schwinger Formalism
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We propose a new set of functions, named Relative Spin Wave Functions (RSWFs), defined via covariant pure boosts to a common rest frame. RSWFs separate spin transport from orbital-spin coupling while preserving the conventional partial-wave angular structure in a manifestly covariant form. Within the Rarita-Schwinger formalism, this approach generates explicit, covariant on-shell partial-wave amplitudes for two-body decays of massive particles of arbitrary spin, with definite orbital angular momentum and total final-state spin. This general framework provides a foundational Lorentz basis for hadronic reaction studies and $LS$-organized operators in theoretical investigations, such as Lattice QCD and QCD sum rules.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Chiral-odd structure of the $N \to Δ$ transition: transverse multipoles from QCD light-cone sum rules
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The matrix element of the tensor current between the nucleon and the $Δ(1232)$ is described by six form factors, which organize into transverse multipoles of rank zero to three. The rank-three term, an octupole, has no counterpart in the diagonal tensor matrix elements of the nucleon or in the electromagnetic $N \to Δ$ transition. We study the isovector chiral-odd transition within QCD light-cone sum rules, constructing the sum rules from light-cone projections of the correlation function rather than from individual Lorentz structures and removing the contributions of spin-$1/2$ states of both parities explicitly. At leading and next-to-leading power in the light-cone expansion the spin-$1/2$-free sum rules form an overdetermined system that determines four combinations of the form factors, among them the transverse dipole, quadrupole and octupole; the monopole and the longitudinal form factor $F_1$ are not accessible at this level. Conventional sum rules built on single Lorentz structures that measure the same combination of form factors differ by up to a factor of two while being equally stable in the Borel parameter, and we show that these structures receive no contribution of leading or next-to-leading power. With the $Δ$ coupling and the continuum threshold taken from the $Δ$ two-point sum rule and two sets of nucleon distribution amplitudes, we obtain the quadrupole for $1 \leq Q^2 \leq 6$~GeV$^2$ and the octupole for $Q^2 \gtrsim 2$~GeV$^2$, with Borel and threshold variations of at most about ten percent, and the dipole, whose magnitude depends strongly on the distribution amplitudes. The model of the distribution amplitudes is the dominant source of uncertainty, and the results do not determine an extrapolation to $Q^2 = 0$.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. v3: substantially revised. Isovector channel only; sum rules constructed from light-cone projections with spin-1/2 contributions removed

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Quark Number Susceptibilities and Conserved Charge Fluctuations in $(2+1)$-flavor QCD with Möbius domain-wall fermions (MDWF)
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We calculate second- and selected fourth-order conserved-charge fluctuations in $(2+1)$-flavor QCD using Möbius domain-wall fermions (MDWF) along a line of constant physics. Gauge ensembles were generated for two light-to-strange quark-mass ratios, $m_l/m_s=1/10$ and $1/27.4$, corresponding to heavier-than-physical and physical pion masses, respectively. For $m_l/m_s=1/10$, calculations were carried out on lattices with temporal extents $N_τ=12$ and $16$, enabling an assessment of lattice-spacing effects at heavier pion mass. For $m_l/m_s=1/27.4$, calculations were performed at $N_τ=12$, allowing us to study the light-quark-mass dependence down to the physical point. Below the pseudocritical temperature, second-order electric-charge, strangeness, and off-diagonal conserved-charge fluctuations are consistent with QMHRG2020 hadron resonance gas calculations. Across the crossover region, these observables rise rapidly and tend toward their Stefan--Boltzmann limits. Selected fourth-order cumulants were also computed at the physical pion mass. Although these observables are statistically more demanding, several channels with controlled uncertainties permit a first comparison with hadron resonance gas calculations.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Heavy-meson molecules with dynamical pions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate heavy-meson molecules by treating the pion as a dynamical degree of freedom. We construct an energy-independent Hamiltonian that couples the two- and three-body Fock spaces. The two-body sector contains a pseudoscalar meson and a vector meson $H_1H_2^{*}$, while the three-body sector consists of two pseudoscalar mesons and a pion $H_1H_2 π$. The $H^*$ self-energy, the $H_1H_2^{*}$ pion-exchange interaction, and the $H_1H_2π$ three-body propagation are consistently generated through the coupling between the two Fock sectors. We use the Gaussian expansion and complex scaling methods to solve the coupled Schrödinger equation. Previous approaches usually reduce three-body effects to energy-dependent two-body kernels and solve the equations iteratively. Our approach obtains the poles by solving a single linear generalized eigenvalue problem. The eigenvectors also provide explicit wave functions in both Fock sectors, allowing a qualitative analysis of channel weights and spatial structure. We benchmark the framework in $T_{cc}^{+}$ and $X(3872)$. The benchmark results are consistent with the current experimental pole determinations. We then apply this formalism to the $BBπ$, $B\bar{B}π$, $DBπ$ and $D\bar{B}π$ systems. We predict one isoscalar bound state in each of these systems. The $DBπ$ and $D\bar{B}π$ systems also contain resonances lying below and above their three-body threshold, respectively. We propose complementary searches for these resonances through $DB^*\to DBγ$ and $D\bar Bπ$. This coupled Fock-space framework can be readily extended to other few-body systems in which unstable constituents can decay and change the particle number.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Accounting for correlations in the $ωπ$ spectral function and its implication on the leading model dependent contribution to the $τ^- \to π^-π^0 ν_τγ$ decay
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The $ωπ$ spectral function, measured in the decay $τ^- \to π^-ων_τ$ by the CLEO Collaboration, is described in the vector meson dominance approach. We sample the parameter space using a Metropolis Monte-Carlo algorithm and generate a set of parameters of the corresponding form factor, explicitly accounting for the correlation among them. We show the improvement in the uncertainty region of the spectral function with respect to neglecting correlations. We test the conserved vector current hypothesis by showing the agreement of the spectral function with the expected from the measurement of the cross section of $e^+e^- \to ωπ$ by the SND experiment, and the consistency of the branching ratio of the $τ^- \to π^-ων_τ$ decay with the value reported by the Particle Data Group. As an application, we consider the $ω$-channel of the $τ^- \to π^-π^0ν_τγ$ process, the leading model dependent contribution in the vector meson dominance approach. We compute the contribution to the long distance electromagnetic correction function $G_\text{EM}(t)$, of the pure $ω$-channel and its interference with the structure independent part. We show that the uncertainties, using the set of correlated parameters, are largely reduced with respect to neglecting correlations. The implication on the isospin symmetry breaking correction to the muon magnetic dipole moment estimation from tau data is found to be consistent with previous results but with improved precision.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Solar axions from nuclear transitions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate the possibility of detecting 14.4~keV and 9.4~keV solar axions and axion-like particles that could be produced in the M1 nuclear transitions of $^{57}\mathrm{Fe}$ and $^{83}\mathrm{Kr}$, respectively. To do so, we used data from soft X-ray observations of the quiet Sun collected by the Solar X-ray Monitor (XSM) on board India's Chandrayaan-2 lunar mission. We observe that although the effective axion-nucleon couplings for $^{83}\mathrm{Kr}$ and $^{57}\mathrm{Fe}$ differ only slightly, their fluxes differ by nearly three orders of magnitude. Consequently, the limit on $|g_{aN}^{\rm eff} \times g_{aγγ}|$ and only $g_{aγγ}$ vs. $m_a$ provide more than one order of magnitude stronger constraint for Fe than for Kr.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 22 pages, 8 figures, 1 table. Updated to the version published in JCAP

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Holographic study of the scalar meson $K_0^*(1430)$ with dynamical longitudinal confinement
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Within the framework of light-front holographic QCD, where transverse confinement is inherently realized through holography, the structure and mass spectrum of the light scalar meson $K_0^{*}(1430)$ are investigated by employing the invariant mass ansatz and enhancing the model with a longitudinal confinement potential (specifically, the 't Hooft equation and the analytically solvable LMZV potential). The combined transverse and longitudinal confinement dynamics lead to more reliable calculations of key observables, including decay constants, parton distribution function, $ξ$-moments, and twist-$2$ and twist-$3$ distribution amplitudes. Transition form factors for the semileptonic decay $B \rightarrow K_0^{*} \ell^+ \ell^-$ are computed from these amplitudes, yielding predictions for differential branching ratios and longitudinal lepton polarization asymmetries as functions of $q^2$. The results are compared with other theoretical models, offering valuable insights into the non-perturbative dynamics of QCD. The predicted observables provide theoretically motivated benchmarks for future experimental investigations of $B\rightarrow K_0^*(1430)\ell^+\ell^-$ decays at LHCb and Belle II.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Heavy-quark limit of $B$-meson distribution amplitudes in light-front holography with longitudinal confinement
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The heavy-quark limit of light-front holographic wave functions for heavy--light mesons is investigated, with particular emphasis on the leading-twist $B$-meson light-cone distribution amplitude, $φ_B^+(ω)$. Two prescriptions for incorporating finite quark masses are compared: the invariant mass ansatz (IMA) and the longitudinal confining framework based on the Li--Maris--Zhao--Vary (LMZV) potential. In the IMA, although the peak of the distribution amplitude remains at a soft spectator momentum, its characteristic width decreases as $Δω\propto m_B^{-1/2}$ in the heavy-quark limit, causing the longitudinal distribution to collapse asymptotically to $δ(ω-m_q)$. Accordingly, the inverse moment approaches the finite limit $λ_{B,\mathrm{IMA}} \to m_q = \mathcal{O}(Λ_{\mathrm{QCD}})$. In contrast, the LMZV framework approaches a finite leading-power (LP) profile with a stable width of order $\mathcal{O}(Λ_{\rm QCD})$ and a stable inverse moment, $λ_{B,\mathrm{LMZV}}^{\mathrm{LP}} = m_q + σ/2 = \mathcal{O}(Λ_{\mathrm{QCD}})$, which is independent of the heavy-quark mass. The heavy-quark scaling of $f_B$ is also examined using the local axial-vector current at zero transverse separation. While the LMZV longitudinal wave function has a non-singular heavy-quark limit, the bare light-front current does not reproduce the canonical heavy-quark effective theory scaling $f_B \propto m_B^{-1/2}$: the decay constant scales as $f_B \propto m_B^{-1}$ in the LMZV framework and as $f_B \propto m_B^{-5/4}$ in the IMA. Thus, a non-singular heavy-quark limit of the longitudinal wave function is necessary but insufficient to ensure the correct heavy-quark scaling of local current matrix elements without systematic current matching.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Precision determination of $B_c$ and $B_c^*$ meson decay constants from lattice QCD
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a lattice QCD study of heavy-heavy meson decay constants using the HISQ gauge ensemble generated by the MILC Collaboration. Employing the HISQ action for both charm and bottom valence quarks tuned to their physical masses, we determine pseudoscalar, vector, and tensor decay constants for heavy quarkonium and $B_c$ systems. Preliminary results are presented for the decay constants of the $B_c$, $B_c^*$, $η_c$, $η_b$, and $Υ$ mesons.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 9 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables, contribution to the 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (LATTICE2026), July 26 - August 1, 2026, College Park, MD, USA

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Electroweak Thermal Histories in the Minimal Type-II Seesaw Model with a Renormalization Group-Improved Effective Potential
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study electroweak thermal histories in the minimal type-II seesaw model with a renormalization group-improved finite-temperature effective potential. The commonly used criterion $v_c/T_c>1$, with $v_c$ the broken-phase field at the critical temperature $T_c$, applied to every first-order degeneracy of the neutral-field phase structure in our survey, does not identify a strong electroweak phase transition. Treating those degeneracies as completed transitions would assign them a gravitational-wave signal they have not been shown to produce. Transitions that do nucleate, percolate and complete are found for the model. They are weak and fast, too weak on the standard sphaleron estimate to protect a baryon asymmetry from washout. Their sound wave spectra lie far below the sensitivity of planned space detectors. Their properties depend strongly on the renormalization group improvement and on the renormalization scale.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Topological Geometry of Neutrino Mass and Mixing
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: This work presents an analytical, parameter-free derivation of the lepton mixing matrix and active neutrino mass spectrum from an icosahedral $A_5$ flavor manifold coupled to the three-generation Iwahori-Hecke algebra $H_3(q)$. Partitioning the icosahedral vertex curvature across the six fundamental Weyl chambers of $H_3(q)$ fixes an elementary angular defect $Δ_{AD} = π/18$, unifying ultra-high-energy mass generation and low-energy flavor mixing as dual realizations of a single geometric invariant. At the topological braiding threshold $μ\sim M_0$, the right-handed Majorana scale $M_0$ breaks scale invariance and drives the five-dimensional Temperley-Lieb quotient into its hyperbolic regime with loop modulus $d'_{AD} = 2\coshΔ_{AD}$, where Quantum Yang-Baxter Baxterization projects the algebraic roots onto a hierarchical heavy spectrum $M_1 > M_2 > M_3 > 0$. Integrating out and inverting these states via a flavor-isotropic Seesaw mechanism Type-I locks in the normal mass hierarchy with $m_1 \approx 3.64$ meV, $\sum_i m_i \approx 63.5$ meV, and $m_β\approx 9.45$ meV. Simultaneously, probability conservation requires analytic continuation onto the compact unitary circle, factorizing the mixing matrix into the $A_5$ Golden Ratio baseline, a unitary boundary twist generated by the longest Coxeter involution, and a discrete Majorana parity matrix. This geometry yields $θ_{13} = 8.49^\circ$, $θ_{12} = 32.11^\circ$, $θ_{23} = 45^\circ$, and maximal Dirac CP violation, $δ_{CP} = \pm π/2$, while discrete $SO(3)$ parities quantize the relative Majorana phases, $α_{13} = -π, α_{23} = 0$, preventing $0νββ$ decay cancellation, $m_{ββ} \approx 1.14$ meV, and suppressing renormalization group drift to $\dotθ_{ij} \sim 10^{-7}$ rad.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 29 pages (main text) plus four Appendices. Improves the underlying algebra, updates the main results accordingly, and corrects typos from the previous version

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Resolving the Two-Fold Ambiguity in Tau Momentum Reconstruction via a Self-Consistent Weighting Method
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The reconstruction of $τ$ lepton momenta in $e^{+}e^{-} \to τ^{+}τ^{-}$ processes suffers from a two-fold kinematic ambiguity due to undetected neutrinos. We show that the common practice of retaining both solutions with equal weight systematically biases the extracted angular coefficients: the bias grows with the size of the $\cos^{2}θ$ modulation of the production distribution $f(\cosθ)$, but remains resolvable even in the nearly uniform QED limit at the $ψ(2S)$ threshold. We propose a self-consistent weighting method based on a fixed-point theorem: assigning normalized weights $w_{i} = f(\cosθ_{i})/[f(\cosθ_{1})+f(\cosθ_{2})]$ yields a weighted distribution $h(x) = f(x)[1+\varepsilon(x)]$ with $\varepsilon(x) \ll 1$ under a detailed balance condition. Monte Carlo simulations at $\sqrt{s}=3.686$~GeV and $4.8$~GeV show that the fixed-point iteration converges to the true angular coefficient $α$ within statistical uncertainty, providing a robust framework for angular analysis without event-by-event ambiguity resolution.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Fully charmed tetraquarks on the Lattice with controlled errors
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We introduce the lattice quark potential model (LQPM), which discretizes the nonrelativistic quark potential model on a periodic cubic lattice and diagonalizes the resulting many-body Hamiltonian exactly. Unlike variational approaches, which provide only upper bounds on the energy, LQPM removes this variational bias, and its remaining finite-volume uncertainty is removed by extrapolation. Formulated directly in coordinate space, the method is indifferent to the specific form of the potential and accommodates arbitrary interactions, such as including three-body forces and spin-orbit and tensor couplings, that are difficult to treat in conventional few-body approaches. As a benchmark, the charmonium and $Ω_{ccc}$ spectra are reproduced within a few MeV of experiment. For the fully charmed tetraquark $cc\bar{c}\bar{c}$, we obtain three resonances $J^P = 0^+, 1^+,$ and $2^+$ ground states above the $η_c η_c$, $η_c J/ψ$, $J/ψJ/ψ$ thresholds, respectively. Our results establish exact lattice diagonalization as a controlled, systematically improvable, and broadly applicable route to multiquark spectroscopy, providing a quantitative benchmark for the strong interaction and valuable guidance for future experimental searches for exotic hadrons.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: In this revised version the potential parameters are refitted at a=0.2 fm, and the tetraquark masses and thresholds are evaluated at the same spacing. Results from the method, i.e. its benchmarks and its finite-volume analysis, are unchanged. The three tetraquark states are now found to be resonances lying 12-30 MeV above their thresholds, in agreement with most of the recent model calculations

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Electroweak baryogenesis from charged current anomalies in $B$ meson decays
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We demonstrate for the first time that new physics explaining the long standing charged $B$ meson anomalies, $R(D^{(*)})$, can be the source of CP violation that explains the observed baryon asymmetry of the universe (BAU). We consider the general two Higgs doublet model with complex Yukawa couplings and compute the BAU in the semiclassical formalism, using a novel analytic approximation for the latter. After imposing constraints from both flavor observables and the electron electric dipole moment (eEDM), and assuming the occurrence of a sufficiently strong first order electroweak phase transition, we find that the observed BAU can be generated for benchmark points within the region favored by the global flavor fit. Reaching the observed BAU relies on optimized values of the phase transition parameters, which we treat as inputs. These scenarios, which explain both $R(D^{(*)})$ and the BAU, can be probed with future eEDM experiments and Higgs factories measurements.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Proton GTMDs and Wigner Distributions in the Chiral Quark Soliton Model: Orbital Angular Momentum and Spin-Orbit Correlation with Sea Quarks
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We calculate the leading-twist vector and axial-vector quark generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) of the proton in the chiral quark soliton model, including both the discrete valence level and the regularized Dirac sea. We consider the isosinglet and isotriplet combinations of GTMDs at zero and nonzero skewness. At zero skewness, we construct Wigner distributions and resolve the orbital angular momentum (OAM) and spin-orbit correlation (SOC) densities in transverse position and momentum space, separately for quarks and antiquarks. This provides a phase-space picture of the sea-quark and sea-antiquark contributions, displaying OAM aligned with the proton spin and anti-aligned with the partons' own spin.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables, v2: references added

High Energy Theory.title: An Amplitudes Approach to Spinning Black Hole Scattering
High Energy Theory.summary: The detection of gravitational waves has opened a new era of precision studies of gravity, demanding advances in our understanding of compact binary dynamics. Scattering amplitudes provide a powerful framework for studying these systems using methods from high-energy physics. In this thesis, we study classical black hole scattering, systematically including spin---an important feature of real astrophysical systems---to describe Kerr black hole dynamics. We model Kerr black holes as massive point particles in finite-spin representations and compute their scattering dynamics perturbatively. We resolve an ambiguity mixing classical and quantum contributions using our spin interpolation method, obtaining a classical amplitude for Kerr black hole scattering through quartic order in spin at third post-Minkowskian order. From this amplitude, we extract the gauge-invariant radial action, enabling the computation of classical non-aligned-spin observables---such as the linear and angular impulses---using covariant Dirac brackets. The amplitude exhibits spin-shift symmetry, remaining invariant under a shift of the black hole spin by the momentum transfer. Motivated by this property, we study the conserved quantities governing the scattering process and show that the dynamics of a probe black hole remains integrable at asymptotic infinity through quartic order in probe spin. Finally, we show that the quartic-in-spin radial action for a probe black hole in a Kerr background, at any order in perturbation theory, is completely fixed by the aligned-spin dynamics, provided that it satisfies asymptotic integrability and spin-shift symmetry.

High Energy Theory.title: Projective relativistic dynamics from a quantum Lorentz algebra: time-dependent deformed Hamiltonians on (anti-)de Sitter spaces
High Energy Theory.summary: A (non-standard) quantum deformation of the Lorentz algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ is used to construct novel time-dependent Hamiltonian systems on the (anti-)de Sitter spacetimes in $(1+1)$-dimensions. The specific deformation considered here contains, among others, the non-standard quantum deformation of $\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{R})$ and that of the `book' algebra $\mathfrak{b}_{2}$ as quantum subalgebras. The guiding idea is to apply the theory of Poisson--Hopf deformations of Lie--Hamilton systems to the Lorentz deformation, giving rise to a broad family of time-dependent deformed systems that share the same deformed Poisson--Hopf Lorentz algebra symmetry. In particular, this approach provides Hamiltonian vector fields expressed in terms of certain projective canonical variables, which, in turn, are related to the usual Beltrami variables via a canonical transformation. Under this construction, it is shown that the underlying Lorentizan spaces possess constant curvature $κ$ and the quantum deformation parameter $z$ can be identified with $κ$, such that the cosmological constant is $Λ=-z\equiv -κ$. Therefore, we deal with the anti-de Sitter, de Sitter and Minkowskian spaces for $z>0$, $z<0$ and $z=0$ (the undeformed case), respectively. Finally, as applications, we study time-dependent deformed oscillators on the (anti-)de Sitter spaces in detail, as well as time-dependent deformed Bateman and generalised coupled Caldirola--Kanai Hamiltonians.

High Energy Theory.title: The entanglement membrane in 2d CFT: reflected entropy, RG flow, and information velocity
High Energy Theory.summary: The time evolution of entanglement entropy in generic chaotic many-body systems has an effective description in terms of a minimal membrane, characterised by a tension function. For 2d CFTs, a degenerate tension function reproduces several results regarding the dynamics of the entropy; this stands in contrast to higher dimensions where the tension is non-degenerate. In this paper we use holography to show that, in order to correctly capture the reflected entropy in 2d CFT, one needs to add an additional degree of freedom to the membrane description. Furthermore, we show that the conventional non-degenerate membrane tension function emerges upon introducing a relevant deformation of the CFT, dual to a planar BTZ black hole with scalar hair and with an interior Kasner universe. Finally, we also study the membrane description for reflected entropy and information velocity arXiv:1908.06993 in higher dimensions.
High Energy Theory.comment: 39 pages + appendices, 39 figures. v2: matches published version

High Energy Theory.title: Comments on Celestial CFT and $AdS_{3}$ String Theory
High Energy Theory.summary: In a recent work, Ogawa et al. (2024) proposed a model for celestial conformal field theory (CFT) based on the $H_{3}^{+}$-Wess-Zumino-Novikov-Witten (WZNW) model. In this paper, we extend the model advanced by Ogawa et al. (2024), demonstrating how it can holographically generate tree-level MHV scattering amplitudes for both gluons and gravitons when analytically continued to the ultra-hyperbolic Klein space $\mathbf{R}_{2}^{2}$, thereby offering an alternative to celestial Liouville theory. We construct a holographic dictionary in which vertex operators and conformal primaries in celestial CFT are derived from their worldsheet counterparts in Euclidean $AdS_{3}$ (bosonic) string theory. Within this dictionary, we derive the celestial stress-energy tensor, compute the two- and three-point functions, and determine the celestial operator product expansion (OPE). Additionally, we derive a system of partial differential equations that characterises the celestial amplitudes of our model, utilising the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) equations and worldsheet Ward identities. In the Appendix, we provide a concise introduction to the $H_{3}^{+}$-WZNW model, with emphasis on its connection to Euclidean $AdS_{3}$ string theory.
High Energy Theory.comment: This version has been accepted for publication in The European Physical Journal C. In this revision, we have included a comment clarifying the difference in physical interpretation between the central charge associated with the boundary-spacetime Virasoro algebra and the central charge of the physical celestial stress-energy tensor. I have also reviewed WZNW theory relevant to our dynamical model

High Energy Theory.title: Time Evolution of Multi-Party Entanglement Signals
High Energy Theory.summary: We study the real-time dynamics of multi-party entanglement signals in chaotic quantum many-body systems including but not necessarily restricted to holographic conformal field theories. We find that scrambling dynamics generates multiparty entanglement with rich structure including: (a) qualitatively different dynamical behaviours for different signals, likely reflecting different dynamics for different kinds of entanglement patterns, (b) discontinuities indicating dynamical phase transitions in the entanglement structure, (c) transient and non-monotonic multiparty entanglement, and (d) periods during which the extensive entanglement of some regions is entirely multipartite. Our main technical tool is the membrane theory of entanglement dynamics.
High Energy Theory.comment: 34 pages + appendix, 23 figures. v2: improved discussions on the saturation of reflected entropy in finite adjacent intervals, added references. v3: matches published version

High Energy Theory.title: Detection times are not local observables in quantum field theory
High Energy Theory.summary: Detection times are routinely recorded in quantum experiments. We show that, under natural covariance and consistency requirements, the observables describing these times cannot be algebraically localized in any bounded spacetime region, even when the records themselves are localized. This challenges the identification of algebraic localization with the physical localization of measurements and shows why microcausality alone does not establish non-signalling for measurements in quantum field theory.

High Energy Theory.title: Dimensionally Regulated Graviton Self-Energy from Gravitons on de Sitter
High Energy Theory.summary: The graviton self-energy $-i [\mbox{}^{μν} Σ^{ρσ}](x;x')$ is the 1PI 2-point function of quantum gravity. It can be used to quantum-correct the linearized Einstein equation in order to infer quantum corrections to gravitational radiation and to the force of gravity. As long as the two points are non-coincident, the graviton self-energy does not need regularization at 1-loop order, however, solving the 1-loop effective field equations requires integrating $[\mbox{}^{μν} Σ^{ρσ}](x;x')$ over ${x'}^μ$, including ${x'}^μ = x^μ$. To facilitate this we employ dimensional regularization and BPHZ renormalization to compute the 1-loop contribution to the graviton self-energy, in pure quantum gravity, on de Sitter background, in the simplest gauge. We then solve the effective field equations to derive 1-loop corrections to the plane wave mode functions of gravitational radiation, and to the Newtonian potential. Although it seems possible to renormalize in such a way that the mode function shows no secular growth, the Newtonian potential grows like the third power of the number of e-foldings.

High Energy Theory.title: Finite N Black Holes through the Brick Wall
High Energy Theory.summary: In AdS/CFT at finite $N$, black holes are described by ordinary quantum systems with finite entropy and discrete spectra, while semiclassical bulk effective field theory treats the near-horizon region as an ideal continuum. We reconsider the brick-wall model as a simple effective description of the finite $N$ departure from the semiclassical near-horizon continuum in AdS/CFT. A Dirichlet wall is reflecting; however, once the regulated near-wall modes are replaced by interacting stretched-horizon degrees of freedom, the exterior simple sector can look absorptive and black-hole-like. If these degrees of freedom are thermally populated while the exterior incoming modes are in their vacuum, they radiate as ordinary hot matter, and this gives Hawking radiation. Furthermore, we show that finite $N$ prevents the near-horizon sector from being an ideal continuum absorber; the brick-wall model is a simple effective representation of this limitation, where the failure of perfect absorption appears as residual reflection or echoes. Such return effects appear on the echo time scale $κ^{-1}\log S_{\rm BH}$ and are not expected to be suppressed as $e^{-S_{\rm BH}}$, although their detailed amplitude is model-dependent. We also discuss brick-wall-like models in which the effective inner boundary arises dynamically from a regular matter core rather than from an imposed boundary condition.
High Energy Theory.comment: v2: 39 pages. Revised version; discussion of finite N evolution clarified, near-extremal throat analysis reformulated, references added

High Energy Theory.title: Black Hole Love Numbers with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
High Energy Theory.summary: We develop and validate a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for computing the tidal Love numbers of black holes directly from their perturbation equations. We consider static perturbations of the Kerr black hole, whose exact hypergeometric solutions provide a controlled benchmark for both the numerical solver and the extraction of the physical response. The framework combines exact enforcement of the horizon boundary conditions with an $H^2$-Sobolev loss that incorporates derivatives of the differential-equation residual. The Love number is then obtained by extracting the asymptotic coefficients of the learned solution, without using the analytic connection formula. Across the tested scalar, vector, and tensor perturbations, the method recovers the finite dissipative response with relative errors below $10^{-5}$. Controlled comparisons show that the higher-derivative loss terms improve solution accuracy by orders of magnitude, while independent tests of the extraction procedure distinguish solver errors from errors in recovering the response coefficients. The conservative response, which vanishes analytically, is constrained by the numerical error floor. These results demonstrate that PINNs can accurately compute black-hole tidal response and establish a validated framework for future extensions to frequency-dependent and non-separable perturbation problems.

High Energy Theory.title: Holography for an $\AdS_5$ to Hyperscaling-Violating Flow via Dimensional Reduction from 8d Einstein-Matter Gravity
High Energy Theory.summary: We construct a classical eight-dimensional Einstein--matter model whose reduction on a three-torus admits an $\AdS_5$ ultraviolet vacuum and a hyperscaling-violating infrared solution. Neutral scalar winding maintains the ultraviolet vacuum, while its disappearance allows the infrared geometry to become locally $\AdS_8$. The same reduction fixes the running gauge coupling, charged scalar mass and interactions. We derive the vacuum conditions, the radial evolution equations and the infrared spectrum. Scalar and vector superfluid orders are then compared using exact ultraviolet zero modes and analytic infrared eigenvalue identities. The scalar and vector instabilities in the infrared coincide at a unique scalar mass above the Breitenlohner--Freedman bound. Their nonlinear competition is governed by a quartic free energy that includes electric response and the change between fixed chemical potential and fixed density. For the interpolating geometry, we identify the conditions under which the two orders can appear together and form a locally stable phase.

High Energy Theory.title: Canonical Forms as Dual Volumes
High Energy Theory.summary: We study dual volume representations of canonical forms for positive geometries in projective spaces, expressing their rational canonical functions as Laplace transforms of measures supported on the convex dual of the semialgebraic set. More generally, for hyperbolic positive geometries the inverse Laplace transform is naturally understood as a distribution supported on the closed dual cone. When this distribution is a non-negative measure, we term the geometry completely monotone, reflecting the property of its canonical function. We identify a class of positive geometries with hyperbolic algebraic boundary for which this cone-supported distribution exists. In particular, simplex-like minimal spectrahedra are completely monotone, with representing measures governed by the Riesz--Wishart theory of the cone of positive semidefinite matrices and admitting integral descriptions over spectrahedral slices and lower-rank strata. We explicitly compute these measures for positive geometries in the projective plane bounded by lines and conics or by a nodal cubic, revealing periods evaluating to transcendental functions. This dual volume perspective replaces logarithmic differential forms by dual measures in the completely monotone case, forging new connections to hyperbolic differential operators, convex optimization and algebraic statistics.
High Energy Theory.comment: 36 pages, 14 figures, Revised version addressing referee comments, with clarifications to the discussion, improved notation, and corrections of minor errors and typos

High Energy Theory.title: New horizons for inhomogeneous quenches and Floquet CFT
High Energy Theory.summary: A fruitful avenue in investigating out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is to abruptly change their Hamiltonian and study the subsequent evolution of their quantum state. If this is done once, the setup is called a quench, while if it is done periodically, it is called Floquet driving. We consider the solvable setup of a two-dimensional CFT driven by Hamiltonians built out of conformal symmetry generators: in this case, the quantum dynamics can be understood using two-dimensional geometry. We investigate how the dynamics is reflected in the holographic dual three-dimensional spacetime and find new horizons. We argue that bulk operators behind the new horizons are reconstructable by virtue of modular flow.
High Energy Theory.comment: 34 pages + appendices, 14 figures. v2: matches published version

High Energy Theory.title: Entanglement Bounds on Cardy Growth in Higher Dimensions
High Energy Theory.summary: We propose bounds relating thermal entropy to entanglement in unitary conformal field theories: $f\le4π^2a$ in four dimensions and $f\le2.99830949\ldots\,F$ in three dimensions. Here $f$ is the dimensionless coefficient of the cosmological constant term in the thermal effective action, $a$ is the Euler anomaly coefficient, and $F$ is the sphere free energy. These bounds arise naturally as the high-temperature limits of proposed inequalities for spherical Rényi entropy that extend the conformal collider bound in four dimensions and an analogous conjecture in three dimensions. To verify this proposal, we formulate a stronger conjectural inequality common to both dimensions, expressed in terms of the stress-tensor three-point function and saturated by every free theory. We establish this inequality in controlled regimes of weakly coupled gauge theories, large-$N$ vector models, and holographic CFTs. Finite-$N$ numerical results provide additional support. Our proposal suggests that the equality between the universal coefficients governing the Cardy formula and entanglement entropy in two-dimensional CFTs extends to higher dimensions in the form of a universal inequality.

High Energy Theory.title: Quasinormal Modes Criticality across Black Hole Extremality
High Energy Theory.summary: We investigate the extremal solution branch to nonextremal branch transition in Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg anti-de Sitter black holes, where the nonlinear electromagnetic parameter $λ$ governs the existence of the extremal branch solution. At fixed pressure and charge, extremal black hole only exist for $λ\leqλ_c$. For $λ>λ_c$, the lowest Hawking temperature keeps nonzero. Near this threshold, the lowest temperature follows a linear critical scaling, $T_{\min}\propto(λ-λ_c)^{α_T}$. We investigate the corresponding dynamical behavior by computing the quasinormal modes of a massless scalar perturbation along the lowest-temperature black hole branch. As the critical threshold is approached, two complex-frequency quasinormal modes branches collide on the imaginary axis and reorganize into distinct purely imaginary branches. Then the imaginary parts of these modes, together with higher overtones, reach zero at the critical threshold, described by $Γ_n\propto(λ-λ_c)^{α_n}$, with $α_n\simeqα_T$. The resulting zero-damped modes become increasingly localized near the event horizon, and their relative damping rates closely follow the overtone spacing predicted by the near-horizon AdS$_2$ spectrum. Our results show that the thermodynamic and dynamical critical behavior remain closely connected even when extremal black hole solutions cease to exist, providing further evidence for the relevance of near-extremal spectral behavior in this distinct critical regime.

High Energy Theory.title: Gravitational Faraday rotation, gravitational spin Hall effect, and spin-refined causality analysis from Magnusian matrix in effective field theories of gravity
High Energy Theory.summary: The effects of black hole's spin in effective field theories (EFTs) of gravity are explored through observables of wave scattering on black hole backgrounds in the geometric optics approximation. The considered observables are polarisation rotation angle, wavenumber kick (or deflection angle), and (Shapiro/Wigner--Smith) time delay, each of which are related to gravitational Faraday rotation, gravitational spin Hall effect, and infrared causality. The observables are computed from scattering amplitudes through the Magnusian formalism, where the Magnusian is promoted to a matrix to account for helicity information. It is found that (1) the gravitational spin Hall effect in EFTs of gravity are qualitatively different from that of general relativity due to "noncommutative" wavenumber kicks, and (2) black hole's spin slightly enhances the causality constraints on EFT coefficients.
High Energy Theory.comment: v2) version accepted by JHEP; added references and minor improvements for clarity including explicit SSC choice for (2.2); conclusions unchanged v1) 35 pages, 22 figures
