If $M$ is null-bordant, $Z(M)$ is obtained from an explicit, state-independent finite family of multi-invariants, up to a power of $Z(S^d)$ which is fixed to be $Z(S^d)^{χ(M)/2}$ for even $d$ and can be removed for odd $d$. Conversely, the obstruction is measured by a quotient of the group of "residues" of colored graphs which receives a surjective map from the oriented bordism group, with kernel precisely the torsion subgroup as far as smooth manifolds are concerned. In $d=4$ the obstruction is the signature: $Z(M)/Z(S^4)^{χ(M)/2}$ can be extracted if and only if $σ(M)=0$. This is due to the fact that the first Pontryagin class $p_1$ has a local expression and thus $e^{iθσ(M)}=e^{\frac{i}{3}θ\int_M p_1}$ cannot be separated from the non-universal factors. Torsion invariants, in contrast, are not obstructed: for the ground state of the $4+1$-dimensional invertible phase with partition function $(-1)^{\int w_2w_3}$ we compute the multi-invariants exactly, and two graphs with identical local data, encoding the Dold manifold and $\mathbb{CP}^2\times S^1$, give opposite signs.

High Energy Theory.title: Ising anyons in the $SU(2)_2$ Chern--Simons theory
High Energy Theory.summary: Ising anyons and $SU(2)_2$ Chern--Simons theory share the fusion rules and $F$-symbols, and their $R$-symbols agree up to braiding orientation and an overall phase. The quantum-group description, $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at $q = e^{iπ/4}$, is nevertheless not semisimple: tensor powers of the fundamental representation contain an additional spin-$3/2$ representation and reducible indecomposable representations, all of zero quantum dimension. We construct explicit highest-weight bases for up to four strands, compute the Racah and braiding matrices, and show that for four strands changes of fusion basis and braiding mix the physical sector with an indecomposable summand. We prove that this mixing affects neither the braid-closure invariant nor the plat-closure amplitude for any number of strands, so that each braiding matrix can be replaced by its physical block. The full representation theory thus reproduces the Ising-anyon data for all observables relevant to topological quantum computation.

High Energy Theory.title: Dipolar boson stars as static two-body systems: an effective-one-body description
High Energy Theory.summary: Dipolar boson stars consist of two scalar-field lumps held in static equilibrium by the balance between gravitational attraction and scalar repulsion. The repulsion stems from a $π$ phase difference between the harmonically varying complex scalar field sourcing each lump. We construct sequences of these configurations numerically and describe them analytically as bound states of two boson stars within the effective-one-body (EOB) formalism. We map the EOB potential previously derived for the scattering of two boson stars onto an energy-dependent Schwarzschild-like radial potential. We find that the EOB-based analytical prediction for the binding energy of the system agrees remarkably well with the numerical values. The analytical prediction for the critical gravitational coupling beyond which no static equilibrium exists is also consistent with the numerical results.

Materials Science.title: Longitudinal and Transverse Thermoelectric Properties in Topological Quantum Materials
Materials Science.summary: Thermoelectric materials can be topologically trivial or non-trivial, enabling reversible interconversion of heat and electricity using a solid-state technology. Incidentally, few of the first experimentally discovered 3D topological materials, namely, Bi, Sb, Sn and Pb-based chalcogenides, were long known as good thermoelectric materials. In these compounds, the heavy atoms that give rise to strong spin-orbit coupling often become essential for band inversion and non-trivial band topology. They lead to low lattice thermal conductivity, linearly dispersing Dirac-like bands induce high electrical mobility, and a band-inverted electronic structure with multiple band extrema gives rise to high Seebeck coefficients. In materials, where the applied temperature gradient induces electrical voltage (Seebeck effect) in the same direction, they are termed as longitudinal thermoelectrics. On the other hand, when the generated electrical voltage and applied thermal current remain orthogonal to each other, the materials are termed as transverse thermoelectrics. The transverse response can be driven by an additional external magnetic field (ordinary Nernst effect), intrinsic remanent magnetisation, or non-zero Berry curvature of a material, which arises from their non-trivial topology (anomalous Nernst effect). We discuss another class of quantum materials, known as goniopolar materials, that exhibit axis-dependent conduction polarity and hence transverse thermoelectric effects, which are based on mechanisms of longitudinal thermoelectric properties. In this review, we cover both types of thermoelectricity, focusing on materials that possess non-trivial topological order. We make connections between their structures, topology and transport properties and suggest tunability of thermoelectric properties going beyond conventional mechanisms such as electron-phonon interactions.

Materials Science.title: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials
Materials Science.summary: Grain growth during heat treatment strongly affects the microstructure of polycrystalline materials and, consequently, their mechanical properties. Although numerical methods such as front-tracking or front-capturing simulations can accurately describe grain growth, their high computational cost limits their use for long or non-isothermal thermal cycles. In previous work, grain growth was successfully predicted under isothermal conditions by treating grain size distributions as time series and forecasting their evolution using recurrent neural networks, allowing complete grain growth trajectories to be generated in seconds rather than through costly PDE-based simulations. In the present work, this forecasting framework is reformulated to handle non-isothermal conditions by explicitly incorporating thermal information into the model architecture. Grain size distributions are encoded using a convolutional neural network, thermal descriptors are embedded through a dedicated multilayer perceptron, and temporal evolution is predicted using a recurrent network. Instantaneous temperature and thermal rate are provided at each time step, allowing the model to adapt its predictions to changing thermal conditions. The framework is trained and evaluated on datasets generated from validated front-tracking simulations across a wide range of non-isothermal thermal paths. The results show that the thermally conditioned model accurately reproduces grain growth dynamics under complex thermal histories, achieving, in k-fold cross-validation over all simulations, mean relative errors of 2.99% (one-hour cycles) and 4.51% (four-hour cycles) with coefficients of determination exceeding 0.99, and mean relative errors between 1.91% and 14.66% on ten simulations following four unseen thermal histories of increasing complexity.

Materials Science.title: Strain-Glass Dynamics in the Superionic Conductor Na$_3$PS$_4$
Materials Science.summary: Ionic conduction in solid-state electrolytes is conventionally described by mobile cations migrating through a static host lattice. Yet the fastest conductors are often the most disordered, and how disorder enhances transport remains unresolved at the mesoscale, inaccessible to ensemble-averaged probes. We use Bragg X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy to measure nanoscale structural dynamics of a single ball-milled Na$_3$PS$_4$ particle. We find that the cubic phase behaves as a strain glass: a frustrated configuration of three degenerate tetragonal variants with short-range order. Its domain-wall motion is stress-driven, crossing over irreversibly to thermally activated dynamics on annealing as residual milling stress is depleted. Rearrangements follow scale-free avalanche statistics, matching ferroelastic martensites but without external driving. The tetragonal polymorph shows none of these features and relaxes fifty times more slowly. These dynamics occur on timescales comparable to estimated ionic diffusion across the particle, indicating the host structure cannot be assumed static on transport-relevant timescales.
Materials Science.comment: Main text: 25 pages, 5 figures; Supplementary Materials included

Materials Science.title: High temperature Jahn-Teller distortion and short-range order in CsCuCl$_3$
Materials Science.summary: CsCuCl$_3$, chiral and Jahn-Teller distorted at room temperature, takes a more symmetric structure above 423 K. Describing this 'simpler' high temperature structure is far from simple and has been the subject of many, sometimes contradicting, studies. Here we reinvestigate the high temperature structure of CsCuCl$_3$, its thermal stability, and its effect on room temperature chirality. In situ pair distribution function data from powder neutron diffraction confirms that CsCuCl$_3$ is Jahn-Teller distorted both below and above $T_\mathrm{c}$, and provides a quantitative view of short-range order in the high temperature structure. In situ powder x-ray diffraction shows that CsCuCl$_3$ does not undergo any additional structural changes above 423 K and is congruently melting. In situ single crystal x-ray diffraction experiments reveal that the phase transition induces domains of mixed handedness in originally homochiral crystals. These findings contribute to a better understanding of phase transitions in Jahn-Teller distorted compounds, and highlight the potential use of phase transitions to control chiral domains.

Materials Science.title: Evolutionary Design of Interpretable Spatial Descriptors for Structure-Property Relationship Discovery
Materials Science.summary: Structure property prediction is a classical task in machine learning, ranging from molecular activity and materials properties to local functional responses measured in microscopy. For image-based regression, two choices define the information available to the predictor: the size of the image neighborhood and the spatial resolution retained within it. A small neighborhood can omit relevant surrounding structure, whereas a large, finely sampled neighborhood can introduce redundant or irrelevant information. Here, we develop a framework for constructing spatial descriptors for prediction of local spectra and hysteresis loops. We benchmark regression models, use SHAP maps to examine their spatial attribution, and explore the effect of the patch size and compression to establish the relationship between predictive accuracy and descriptor dimensionality. We then use a genetic algorithm to optimize spatial partitions and the assignment of mean, minimum, and maximum pooling operations. Each retained region contributes an explicit measurement of the image, allowing the search to balance prediction error against the number of descriptor values. Cartesian and polar constructions provide complementary ways to organize this information. The resulting descriptors make it possible to examine where spatial detail is needed, where regional summaries are sufficient, and how these choices depend on the predictor and the measured response. The same approach can be used for molecules and solids once the genetic algorithm rules for these are established.

Materials Science.title: Correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets for copper solids from material-constrained atomic optimization
Materials Science.summary: Correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets are central to systematic molecular quantum chemistry, but their direct use in periodic solids is often limited by severe linear dependence from diffuse atomically optimized primitives. This problem is particularly acute for metallic and metal-containing systems, where reliable complete-basis-set (CBS) extrapolation is needed for correlated-wavefunction benchmarks. We introduce material-constrained atomic optimization (MCAO), a basis-set optimization framework that preserves the atomic and correlation-consistent character of Gaussian basis sets while penalizing large overlap-matrix condition numbers in representative solids. As a proof of concept, we generate Dunning-style MCAO-cc-pVXZ basis sets (X = D, T, Q) for Cu with all-electron, scalar-relativistic all-electron, effective core potential (ECP), and pseudopotential treatments. The resulting basis sets remain numerically stable for Cu solids and surfaces while reproducing molecular Cu dimer energetics and plane-wave reference properties of bulk Cu. CBS-extrapolated random-phase approximation calculations further enable a controlled assessment of pseudopotential, relativistic, and basis-set errors in bulk Cu and CO adsorption on Cu(111), providing scalar-relativistic all-electron Gaussian-basis benchmarks for the CO adsorption puzzle.

Materials Science.title: Millikelvin magnetometry up to 30~T using a multi-cross micro-Hall sensor
Materials Science.summary: We report a multi-cross micro-Hall sensor fabricated from an MBE-grown GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure for high-sensitivity magnetometry. The device enables dc magnetization measurements at temperatures down to $\sim$15~mK and in dc magnetic fields up to 30 T. Bulk samples with dimensions ranging from 100~$μ$m to 1~mm can be measured with a resolution better than 1$~μ$T with a 1~$μ$A excitation at 13.77 Hz. Test-of-performance measurements were carried out by probing the field-dependent magnetization plateaus of the triangular-lattice quantum magnet K$_{2}$Co$_{2}$(SeO$_{3}$)$_{3}$ at 20~mK, the antiferromagnetic transition of K${_3}$GdTe${_2}$O${_9}$ near 220 mK via temperature-dependent magnetization, and the quantum oscillations in a ruthenium single crystal. A simple and reliable sample-mounting setup that ensures reproducible magnetic measurements is provided.
Materials Science.comment: To appear in Chinese Physics B

Materials Science.title: First-principles study of the formation of Group-IV--vacancy color centers in diamond
Materials Science.summary: $XV$ ($X$ is Si, Ge, Sn, or Pb, and $V$ is the carbon vacancy) color centers are promising platforms for quantum computing and quantum information science due to their favorable optical and spin properties. They are commonly fabricated by ion implantation, which inevitably introduces vacancies and carbon self-interstitials (C$_i$) into the lattice. However, the microscopic formation mechanism remains unclear, limiting the yield and stability of $XV$ centers. Here, first-principles calculations are conducted to systematically investigate the roles of $V$ and C$_i$ in $XV$ formation. We find that $XV$ formation is energetically favorable, with large binding energies and low diffusion barriers. Nevertheless, $XV$ readily captures C$_i$ to form substitutional defect $X_s$, or captures an additional $V$ to form the complex $XV_2$. Charge transition levels show that oppositely charged reactants never meet in these reactions, and that Coulomb repulsion blocks them only when both reactants carry charges of the same sign, which for the capture of C$_i$ requires strongly n- or p-type conditions. These competing defect reactions destabilize the split-vacancy configuration and could account for the low formation yield of $XV$ centers, so that they appear at concentrations well below those expected from the implanted dose. Our results elucidate the microscopic origin of this intrinsic instability and suggest that Fermi-level control may suppress defect conversions and stabilize the split-vacancy configuration.

Materials Science.title: Anomalous thermal transport in isotope-enriched germanium carbide
Materials Science.summary: Advances in modern electronics demand the dissipation of heat fluxes approaching 1000 W cm$^{-2}$, which drives an urgent need for materials with thermal conductivity ($κ$) exceeding 1000 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. Here, by solving the Boltzmann transport equation considering both three- and four-phonon interactions, we observe that isotopically pure cubic germanium carbide (GeC) exhibits a remarkable $κ$ of 1018 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, which is further corroborated by state-of-the-art machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations. Two unique mechanisms underlie this anomalously high $κ$: a remarkably strong isotopic enhancement effect (289%) and a surprisingly modest suppression due to four-phonon scattering (22%)-despite the presence of a wide acoustic-optical phonon gap. Moreover, we find that GeC defies the conventional Leibfried-Schlomann formula and exhibits a non-monotonic variation of $κ$ with external hydrostatic pressure at elevated temperatures. Our findings establish isotope-enriched GeC as a material of ultrahigh $κ$ and an ideal platform for exploring exotic phonon physics.

Materials Science.title: Ta-based S-I-S junctions for integrated superconducting electronics
Materials Science.summary: In this work, we have presented S-I-S Josephson junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ barrier. We grew base and top $α$-Ta electrodes using seed layer engineering, showing both Nb and ${\rm TaN}_x$ are viable seed layer choices, and particularly emphasize that at room temperature a re-seed layer is required to nucleate $\rmα$-Ta for the top electrode. However, we note that the choice of seed layer can have subtle implications on the electrical tunneling behavior of the junctions. We used room-temperature probing of variable junction areas, combined with Ambegaokar-Baratoff physics, to characterize the wafer scale critical current densities. For 0.4 $μ$m$^2$ junctions, we found junction spreads as low as 2.0% across the 20 x 20 mm chip relevant for device performance. The entire process was carried out using standard industry foundry processing using 150 mm wafer tooling, which is an important step towards proving that Ta-based junctions can be implemented at scale. We have successfully fabricated and tested junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ insulating tunnel barrier, demonstrating that this is a material platform which merits further investigation and studies for potential application in classical and quantum superconducting technologies.
Materials Science.comment: 26 pages, 12 figures, to be submitted to Physical Review Applied, authors listed alphabetically

Materials Science.title: Explicit pore pre-conditioning and inverse design of amorphous nanoporous carbon
Materials Science.summary: Porous carbons store energy, capture gases and purify water, and their performance depends strongly on the geometry of their pores. Atomistic models mostly simulate their synthesis by molecular dynamics, with results that depend on the interatomic potential, and return the pore network as an output rather than as a specification. Here we show that the pore network can be an input: pores drawn from a target size distribution fill a prescribed volume fraction, carbon is grown around them by stochastic ring placement, and a particle swarm recovers the construction parameters from a structural fingerprint. The search reproduces the density, surface area and pore volume of a carbon produced by quenched molecular dynamics within about 5 %, together with its pore size distribution. As a stress test, it also recovers a bimodal distribution, and the search history reveals which parameters the targets constrain and flags a failed search. A short anneal completes the network, recovering the coordination of the reference while the pore size distribution keeps its shape. Molecular dynamics still supplies the local chemistry, but the pore geometry becomes a design variable for a given application.

Materials Science.title: Free electrons unveil nanolaser physics at the sub-picosecond and nanometer scale
Materials Science.summary: Semiconducting nanowire lasers (NWLs) constitute nanoscale modular and tunable light sources, essential components for integrated optoelectronics. However, advancing NWL operation requires characterization of their near-field and dynamics at the nanometer scale, which is hampered by the diffraction limit of light. Here, we show a non-perturbative measurement of the absolute number of photons in a GaN/InGaN nanowire nanolaser cavity above the lasing threshold with sub-picosecond resolution and maps of the lasing mode spatial profile at the nanoscale. For this we use photon-induced near-field electron microscopy while simultaneously measuring the photons far-field, unraveling the key nanoscale and time-resolved characteristics of a NWL in operation. With this technique, we observed lasing with a pump-power-dependent time offset of 0.5-1 ps that reflects carrier thermalization and spontaneous emission, and a pulse duration of 500 to 700 fs. From the spatial maps of the lasing mode, we observe TM-polarized azimuthal whispering gallery modes along the nanowire circumference, as well as two distinct Fabry-Perot modes along the nanowire length. These spatial maps allow us to understand which of the multiple complex cavity modes available in the nanowire are responsible for lasing paving the way for their practical application into devices.

Materials Science.title: Dynamically Reentrant Skyrmion Phase in Oscillating Magnetic Fields
Materials Science.summary: We address a central open question in driven topological matter by investigating the nonequilibrium response of a two-dimensional magnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions subjected to a periodically oscillating magnetic field. Using extensive Monte Carlo simulations, we uncover a dynamically reentrant skyrmion phase that emerges within a finite window of field amplitudes and bias fields, sandwiched between the conventional skyrmion and polarized ferromagnetic phases. This phase has no equilibrium counterpart and originates from an imbalance between skyrmion creation and annihilation over a single field cycle, leading to a reversal of the period-averaged topological charge. We show that the re-entrant phase exists only in the dynamic response regime where the system can follow the drive, and is suppressed at higher driving frequencies. Our results establish periodic driving as a nonequilibrium control parameter for stabilizing and reversing skyrmion topology.

Materials Science.title: Helium States in a CAS(2,2) Subspace Inspired by Quantum Photonics
Materials Science.summary: We present a four-mode Fock-state photonics implementation of the variational quantum deflation (VQD) algorithm to calculate the ground-state and excited-state energies for the neutral helium atom in a CAS(2,2) Subspace. Its CAS(2,2) electronic Hilbert space is encoded into a bosonic Fock-space representation and subsequently optimized using a continuous-variable quantum circuit. The circuit architecture under study is constructed of single-mode phase shifts, beam splitters, and cross-Kerr interactions. The variational circuit is initialized in the Fock state $\ket{1100}$ and its performance is benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the active-space configuration-interaction (CASCI) Hamiltonian. We also extend the method to optimize from the first to three excited states of the helium atom with the aid of the variational quantum deflation $(VQD)$ method in a CAS(2,2). We then investigate the performance of this circuit architecture as a basis for implementing the VQD method. In the ideal noiseless simulation setting, we see that the survival probability of the ground and the excited states within the target $CAS$ subspace is unity, because the total photon number and the photon number in the two spin sectors $α$ and $β$ are preserved. We demonstrate that the proposed approach enables the determination of the ground and excited-state energies within the CAS(2,2) electronic Hilbert space using a continuous-variable quantum circuit and the variational quantum deflation ($VQD$) algorithm, while satisfying the orthogonality conditions with negligible errors.

Materials Science.title: Hydrogen sublattice in LaH$_{12}$: structural stability and possible ordering motifs
Materials Science.summary: Lanthanum polyhydrides, synthesized under extreme pressure, exhibit near-room-temperature superconductivity. Finding a precise arrangement of the hydrogen sublattice that is critical for understanding the strong electron-phonon coupling remains experimentally unresolved due to the small X-ray scattering form factor of hydrogen atoms. In this work, we attempt to computationally reconstruct hydrogen sublattices of the LaH$_{12}$ at 100-200 GPa combining unconstrained evolutionary searches and structure generation with fixed lanthanum sublattice. By implementing a similarity metric, we screen the computationally generated configurations against experimental powder X-ray diffraction data. We specifically identify the trigonal $R\bar{3}$-LaH$_{12}$ and pseudo-hexagonal $C222_1$-La$_2$H$_{24}$ phases, which demonstrate close agreement with the experimental X-ray diffraction data. First-principles calculations confirm the metallic and superconducting nature of these hydrides. Crucially, our lattice dynamics analysis using the stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation (SSCHA) indicates that these structures are dynamically stable. We reveal the presence of molecular H$_2$ units and soft phonon modes in the trigonal LaH$_{12}$ that suppresses superconductivity ($T_c \ge 30$ K), while the hydrogen clathrate network in the $C222_1$ phase drives strong electron-phonon interactions, yielding the coupling parameters of $λ\approx 1.83$, $ω_{\log} \approx 87.5$ meV and transition temperature of $T_c\approx 150$ K at 150 GPa.

Materials Science.title: Electrical Control over Volatile Mott Switching through Non-Volatile Memory Effects
Materials Science.summary: Vanadium Dioxide (VO2) and Vanadium Sesquioxide (V2O3) are Mott insulators that undergo an Insulator-to-Metal Transition (IMT) at ~340K and ~160K, respectively, manifested as an orders-of-magnitude reduction in their electrical resistance. These transitions provide the physical basis for their Volatile Resistive Switching (VRS) behavior, making them promising candidates for threshold-switching devices. Here, we show that the volatile switching in these materials can be strongly affected by non-volatile processes associated with the creation and annihilation of the conducting filament. These processes give rise to pronounced memory effects in which the initial switching voltage substantially exceeds that of subsequent cycles. We identify two distinct mechanisms underlying this behavior in different thermal regimes. In the phase-coexistence regime, a memory effect is observed in V2O3, arising from the spatial redistribution of metallic and insulating domains. Well below the hysteresis regime, an additional electroforming-like memory effect is observed in both VO2 and V2O3 which is attributed to the formation and/or migration of defects under the influence of a high electric field and a current surge associated with the IMT-driven switching. Using a protective internal resistor and a multi-step writing protocol, this normally destructive process can be harnessed to tune the switching voltage and power over a wide temperature range. These results demonstrate a route toward controlled programming of switching parameters in IMT-based resistive switching devices.
Materials Science.comment: 22 pages, 8 figures, 12 supplementary pages, 7 supplementary figures; Acknowledgements section updated

Materials Science.title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
Materials Science.summary:
We analyze the unusual microstructure resulting from the cubic to orthorhombic phase transformation in the shape-memory alloy ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$. This seems to represent an approximate experimental realization of a deformation having a finite number of incompatible deformation gradients, which has been known to exist only as a theoretical possibility. Because the middle eigenvalue $γ$ of the transformation strain is very close to 1, the phase transformation in this alloy takes place via nucleation of exact austenite-martensite interfaces rather than, as usual for other alloys, by classical austenite-martensite interfaces separating the austenite from a finely-twinned laminate of martensite. According to the moving mask approximation of Della Porta this leads to the question whether a microstructure can be formed from the set $H$ of the twelve matrices ${\mathbf V}_i$ on the martensite energy wells that are rank-one connected to the identity, even though these matrices are mutually incompatible.
  We show that when $γ=1$ and the transformation is volume preserving, such a microstructure is possible that does not deform the grain boundary. This is a consequence of $H$ forming a degenerate $T_{12}$ configuration in the sense of Kirchheim. In fact there are such microstructures supported on just 8 of the 12 matrices in $H$. However there is no deformation satisfying the same boundary condition whose gradient belongs to $H$ almost everywhere. An additional prediction, confirmed experimentally, is that the macroscopic deformation gradient equals the identity everywhere. We also analyse the approximate compatibility of the ${\mathbf V}_i$. Although mutually incompatible, they are nearly compatible, with some pairs much more nearly compatible than others, these pairs corresponding to interfaces that are more frequently observed.

Materials Science.title: Why Ammoniated Lithium Borohydrides Liquefy and Resolidify?
Materials Science.summary: Ammonia (NH$_3$) absorption drives LiBH$_4\cdot x$NH$_3$ through a re-entrant ``solid--liquid--solid'' transition: LiBH$_4\cdot$NH$_3$ is a well-defined solid ammoniate, compositions near LiBH$_4\cdot 2$NH$_3$ are liquid-like or partially liquefied, whereas LiBH$_4\cdot 3$NH$_3$ returns to a more rigid non-liquid ammoniate state. However, the microscopic origin of this unintuitive response remains a long-lasting mystery. Here, we uncover its mechanism. Cross-database analysis identifies borohydrides as a particularly state-diverse and composition-responsive material family. Structure prediction and ab initio molecular simulations reveal that increasing NH$_3$ loading increases the direct Li--N coordination number while progressively decreasing BH$_4^-$-associated contacts in the local Li environment. Near $x \approx 2$, these contributions are most balanced among the simulated compositions, and the sampled Li--N/N$\cdots$B coordination landscape is broadest. Further ammoniation produces Li--N-dominant coordination and slower BH$_4^-$/NH$_3$ contact renewal, accompanying recovery of a more rigid ammoniate state. Pressure--composition isotherm, $^1$H and $^{11}$B nuclear magnetic resonance, and Raman measurements support this non-monotonic state evolution and associated BH$_4^-$/NH$_3$ reorganization. These findings transform ammonia-induced liquefaction from an empirical phase anomaly into a competition between native-network disruption, mixed-coordination frustration, and ligand-built network reconstruction, providing a framework for chemically switching between transport-favouring fluidity and stability-favouring rigidity in hydrogen-rich materials.

Materials Science.title: Oxygen-nonstoichiometry-driven phase transition in $\mathrm{Sr}_{1-x}\mathrm{Nd}_{x}\mathrm{CoO}_{3-δ}$ ($x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3$) perovskites
Materials Science.summary: We report a systematic study of the interplay between oxygen nonstoichiometry, crystal structure, and magnetic/electrotransport properties in $\mathrm{Sr}_{1-x}\mathrm{Nd}_{x}\mathrm{CoO}_{3-δ}$ ($x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3$). High-resolution neutron powder diffraction combined with synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction reveals that increasing the oxygen content induces a structural transition from a layered $I4/mmm$ ($2a_p \times 2a_p \times 4a_p$) to an oxygen-deficient orthorhombic $Pmmm$ ($a_p \times a_p \times 2a_p$) phases with preferential oxygen-vacancy occupation. This transition is accompanied by a crossover from G-type antiferromagnetic with a weak ferromagnetic component to a ferromagnetic state, and a drastic decay in resistivity. The evolution of the magnetic and transport properties is discussed in terms of changes in the Co spin state, enhanced Co $3d$ - O $2p$ orbital overlap upon oxygen uptake, and a magnetically inhomogeneous ferromagnetic state associated with residual oxygen vacancies and mixed $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}/\mathrm{Co}^{4+}$ valence. Our findings experimentally confirm that the stabilization of the layered "314" structure is driven by the presence and ordering of oxygen vacancies rather than A-site cation ordering, whereas the oxygen-deficient oxidized compounds represent an intermediate orthorhombic state preceding fully stoichiometric phases.

Materials Science.title: Tunneling spectroscopy of topological insulator Josephson junctions
Materials Science.summary: In the seminal proposal by Fu and Kane, the superconducting proximity effect is used to realize topological superconductivity in the topological surface state (TSS) of a 3D topological insulator (TI). In a Josephson junction made on the TI surface, the spin-momentum locking of the TSS guarantees the existence of spin nondegenerate, perfectly transmitted Andreev modes. These modes lead to gap closing as a function of the superconducting phase difference $\varphi$. Here, we report the observation of highly transmissive Andreev modes in a TI Josephson junction, probed via tunnel contacts and $\varphi$ controlled by a flux loop. Within our experimental resolution, they could indicate a gap closing and reopening. This phenomenon is observed for a wide range of chemical potentials, supporting its TSS origin. Under an applied magnetic field, highly transmissive modes are observed locally, matching theoretical predictions for Josephson vortices in the TSS. Our results support the fundamental role of spin-momentum locking in the Andreev physics in the TSS.
Materials Science.comment: 45 pages in total, including 5 main text figures and 13 supplementary figues

Materials Science.title: Strain control of magneto-optical properties of ultra-thin Ni-Mn-Ga films grown by magnetron sputtering
Materials Science.summary: Ultra-thin epitaxial Ni-Mn-Ga films, 10-15 nm thick, were grown by magnetron sputtering on MgO(001), either directly on the substrate or on a Cr buffer, and studied by X-ray diffraction, magnetometry, and magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) spectroscopy. The films were austenitic, with the cubic cell tetragonally distorted in opposite directions. The film on bare MgO was stretched in-plane ($c/a=0.989$) and the film on Cr was compressed in-plane ($c/a=1.021$), while their unit-cell volumes differed by less than $0.3\%$. As the thermal expansion mismatch was expected to stretch the films in-plane in both cases, the opposite distortions were attributed to the lattice misfit. The room-temperature magnetization loops of the two films did not show significant differences, but their polar and longitudinal MOKE spectra differed in the amplitude, sign, and energy of the spectral structures over the whole 0.76-5 eV range. Magneto-optical simulations showed that the absence of the Cr buffer accounted only for the stronger low-energy polar MOKE rotation extremum of the film on MgO. We attributed the other changes to the strain-induced change of the electronic structure, consistent with theoretical predictions in which the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ sub-bands of the minority-spin Ni $e_g$ states exchange their order when the distortion changes sign. In parts of the spectrum, the two films showed Kerr rotation or ellipticity of opposite sign, so the choice of the growth template or a dynamically induced distortion can switch the sign of the magneto-optical response at a given photon energy.

Materials Science.title: Ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals: temperature-tunable electrocaloric fluids with large strength at low fields
Materials Science.summary: The electrocaloric (EC) effect offers a promising energy-efficient and clean cooling technology. We present the first direct measurements of EC temperature change in a new family of EC fluids, ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals (FNLCs), demonstrating in two such materials temperature jumps of $|ΔT_j|$ ~ 0.2 K for field changes as low as $ΔE$ ~ 0.1 $V μm^{-1}$. Indirect measurements of adiabatic temperature change $|ΔT|$ confirm that these direct measurements are an underestimate and that $ΔE$ = 2 $V μm^{-1}$ can induce up to $|ΔT|$ ~ 1.6 K, yielding EC strengths $|ΔT/ΔE|$ up to 100% higher than incumbent materials. For temperature spans of 5-10 K, we predict a coefficient of performance of ~21-40. We find $|ΔT|$ ~ 1 K for >100 FNLCs that collectively span all temperatures between $0{^\circ}$C and $100{^\circ}$C. This, together with the new device concepts conceivable with fluid EC materials, offers huge potential for cooling applications.

Materials Science.title: Inverse Chiral Phonon Zeeman Effect in Noncentrosymmetric Crystals
Materials Science.summary: We present a quantized effective theory of the inverse chiral phonon Zeeman effect in noncentrosymmetric crystals. Within micropolar elasticity, coupled translational displacements and microrotations give rise to intrinsically chiral phonons, which generate an elliptically polarized internal magnetic field through dynamical piezoelectricity. Provided that electronic screening is incomplete, this field acts as an effective longitudinal Zeeman field on electronic spins, driving a Floquet response for localized states and a stationary adiabatic band splitting for itinerant electrons, leading to macroscopic spin polarization. In contrast to earlier discussions based on nearly degenerate axial optical modes or externally driven circular lattice motion, the present mechanism relies on finite-wave-number truly chiral phonons whose counter-rotating branches are intrinsically split by crystal chirality. Quantization is introduced to define the single-phonon magnetic-field scale, coherent-state enhancement, and magnetic chirality in a controlled manner. The results establish a purely lattice-driven mechanism for the inverse chiral phonon Zeeman effect in noncentrosymmetric crystals.
Materials Science.comment: v2: 39 pages, 5 figures. Main text with Appendices A-D and Supplemental Material (Secs. S1-S3) in a single file

Materials Science.title: An All-Atom Model of the Resorcinol-Formaldehyde Aerogel Skeleton from DFT and Molecular Dynamics: Validation and Iron Incorporation
Materials Science.summary: Resorcinol-formaldehyde (RF) aerogels are lightweight, ultra-porous thermal superinsulators whose complex amorphous structure has not yet been described at the all-atom level. Here, we build an all-atom model of the RF aerogel skeleton by combining density functional theory (DFT) and classical molecular dynamics (MD), validate it against experimental infrared and density measurements, and use it to study the incorporation of iron dopants. The RF base unit was optimized with Gaussian, DMol$^{3}$ and SIESTA, and its calculated infrared spectrum agreed with experiment. Comparing classical force fields with DFT for branched systems of two to four base units (140-278 atoms) led to the choice of COMPASS II. A 15,012-atom system of 54 branched RF units, not cross-linked to each other, aggregated into a single cluster in the canonical (NVT) ensemble and reached an equilibrium density of 1.296 g.cm$^{-3}$ in the isobaric-isothermal (NPT) ensemble, in agreement with the experimental skeletal density (1.3 g.cm$^{-3}$). Then, 5 wt$\%$ iron (109 atoms) was added to the equilibrated structure: during 1 ns of NPT simulation, the fraction of iron atoms embedded in the skeleton rose from 63$\%$ to 71$\%$, and the Fe-C radial distribution function peaked at 3 Å. The model thus provides an experimentally supported starting point for screening fillers and dopants in RF gels, with prospective application to their thermoelectric functionalization, which we have previously demonstrated experimentally with basalt and PANOX fibres. Future extensions could address skeleton properties relevant to thermal insulation and the pyrolysis of RF gels into carbon and metal-doped carbon aerogels.

Materials Science.title: Quantitatively Probing the Tilt Angle Failures in 4D-STEM Polarisation Analysis
Materials Science.summary: Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) is increasingly used to map polarisation in ferroic textures such as domain walls, vortices, merons and skyrmions. These textures are accompanied by local strain, lattice rotation and misorientation, which also modulate the diffraction features used to infer polar order. Even small deviations from the zone axis can therefore produce contrast that is indistinguishable from a polarisation signal. Here we quantify the tilt sensitivity of two polarisation-sensitive signals, diffraction disc intensity and Kikuchi band intensity, in three ferroelectrics with distinct polar distortions: PbTiO3, BaTiO3 and Cu3B7O13Cl boracite. We find that tilts of only 0.01-0.05 degrees reverse most Friedel-pair disc asymmetries, and even the most robust disc pairs reverse by 0.04 degrees in BaTiO3, 0.14 degrees in PbTiO3 and 0.18 degrees in boracite, producing contrast equal and opposite to that of the polarisation. Kikuchi band contrast is the only signal that reports absolute polarity without knowledge of the specimen thickness, but it does so only up to 0.09 degrees in PbTiO3, 0.015 degrees in BaTiO3 and 0.02 degrees in boracite. From these results we define tilt tolerances for each signal and material, and propose practical criteria for distinguishing polarisation contrast from misorientation. The analysis also applies to scanning electron microscopy-based diffraction, including electron backscatter diffraction.

Materials Science.title: Gauge-covariant theory of the orbital Hall effect: role of itinerant orbital currents and a non-Kubo contribution
Materials Science.summary: The orbital Hall effect is central to the emerging field of orbitronics, yet its first-principles description relies on an atom-centered approximation (ACA) of the orbital angular momentum (OAM) that discards itinerant contributions. Attempts to go beyond it have used off-diagonal elements of the ground-state orbital magnetization formula, which are not gauge covariant and treat the OAM as a fixed operator. Here we construct a gauge-covariant OAM operator in a Wannier basis that is consistent with the modern theory of orbital magnetization for all band pairs. Because this operator depends on the geometry of the Bloch states, an applied electric field modifies the operator itself, giving rise to a non-Kubo contribution to the orbital Hall conductivity (OHC). First-principles calculations for transition metals and monolayer MoS$_2$, which are frequently used in spin-orbitronics experiments, show that OHC contributions originating from the itinerant-circulation of the Wannier functions are often comparable to or larger than those originating from their local-circulation, which is especially evident in Pt and Fe. Separating the OHC instead into local and non-local terms, we find that the former closely resemble the ACA results, while the latter often dominate and reverse the sign predicted by the ACA. Our results call for a reassessment of how orbital currents are identified in experiments.

Materials Science.title: Structural effects of liquid infiltration of 3Y-Zirconia with Sc, Mg and Y
Materials Science.summary: The current work has investigated the effect of co-doping 3Y-Zirconia (3YSZ) with Sc, Mg and Y by liquid infiltration. Pre-sintered porous discs of 3YSZ were immersed in diluted nitric acid solutions containing Sc, Mg or Y, and combinations of the three, trapping liquid within the porosities of the samples. Upon drying, the cations are maintained inside the pellet, making the basis for the co-doping. After sintering, mass increase confirms the co-doping effect. Rietveld refinements of X-ray diffraction data show that the liquid-infiltrated samples contain the tetragonal t, t'' and cubic c-phase in various fractions depending on the doping elements. The phases are compared with 3YSZ and 5YSZ sintered for 0 hours and 2 hours at 1500 °C. To evaluate the material properties in an application-based perspective, the Knoop hardness, translucency and grain size was measured. We conclude that liquid infiltration is a viable route to perform co-doping of Zirconia.
Materials Science.comment: 16 pages, 6 figures, supplementary section included after reference list

Materials Science.title: Spin swapping mediated by spin-orbital textures in centrosymmetric multiorbital materials
Materials Science.summary: Spin swapping converts a primary spin current into a secondary one by interchanging its flow and spin-polarization directions, attributed to spin-orbit scattering or spin-band splitting. Here we uncover a fundamentally distinct route to spin swapping arising from the orbital degree of freedom in the spin pumping to centrosymmetric multiorbital materials \textit{without spin-band splitting}. When the dynamical proximity ferromagnet injects a longitudinal spin current flowing normal to the interface, spin-orbit-entangled orbital textures redirect the injected spins into longitudinal and transverse orbital currents. Their subsequent conversion back to the spin sector generates transverse spin currents with propagation and polarization directions swapped relative to the primary spin current. The swapping efficiency achieves $50\%$ for Ge and Si. Governed by a fourth-rank tensor constrained by crystalline symmetry and without requiring spin-orbit scattering or inversion symmetry breaking, our finding reveals spin-orbital textures as hidden intermediate channels of spin swapping with unexplored material choices and functionalities.

Materials Science.title: Spin State versus Potential of Zero Charge as Predictors of Density-Dependent Oxygen Reduction in M-N-C Electrocatalysts
Materials Science.summary: Metal-site density strongly influences oxygen reduction activity and selectivity in M-N-C electrocatalysts, but the descriptors that predict these trends remain under debate. Here, we compare spin state and the potential of zero charge (PZC) as predictors of density-dependent oxygen reduction behavior in Fe-N-C and Co-N-C catalysts. Using constrained-magnetization calculations combined with Landau analysis, we find that the ground-state magnetic moments vary only weakly across a broad range of metal-site densities, suggesting that magnetic descriptors alone cannot account for the pronounced performance changes. In contrast, explicit-solvent simulations reveal systematic density-dependent shifts in PZC, which alter the interfacial electric field and thereby modulate field-sensitive adsorption energetics of ORR intermediates. Incorporating these PZC shifts into a pH-field-coupled microkinetic model captures the density-dependent activity trends and reproduces the experimentally observed increase in two-electron selectivity at lower site densities under acidic conditions. Experimental PZC measurements further support the predicted trend. Within the investigated Co-N-C and Fe-N-C series, PZC-dependent electrostatics consistently rationalize the density-dependent ORR trends, whereas the examined magnetic descriptors show comparatively weak variation.

Materials Science.title: Colloquium: A critique on van der Waals and two-dimensional magnets
Materials Science.summary: Magnetic two-dimensional (2D) crystals were isolated about a decade ago, triggering a tremendous research activity worldwide. This colloquium raises a stiff question: what is really new about them? At first sight, they seem to be purer implementations of 2D spin models than traditional systems such as ultra-thin films. Yet, they partly realized their promises so far, and whether they give fresh perspectives on long-standing predictions in statistical physics is still an open question. Undoubtedly, they are uniquely amenable to electric-field effect, susceptible to mechanical deformation, and sensitive to moirés, for example. They represent interesting platforms for exploring, challenging, or simply revisiting a wide range of phenomena in condensed matter magnetism. This colloquium intends to offer a critical, yet not necessarily skeptical, overview of the field, clarifying what we believe could be unique with 2D magnets, related quasi-2D van der Waals magnets, and their heterostructures.
Materials Science.comment: 25 pages, 10 figures; published in Review of Modern Physics

Materials Science.title: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of BC8 carbon near terapascal pressures
Materials Science.summary: Whether carbon forms crystalline structures beyond diamond at terapascal pressures remains unresolved. Predicted for nearly four decades, the denser BC8 phase has lacked direct crystallographic evidence. Here we report the first direct crystallographic identification of BC8 carbon, formed as a single crystal from molten carbon during laser-driven decaying-shock compression of [100]-oriented diamond following loading above 1.1 TPa. Using in situ orientation-resolved single-crystal X-ray diffraction, we observe discrete Bragg spots whose spacings and angular relationships are reproduced by a common orientation matrix within each indexed BC8 reflection group, providing constraints beyond powder peak matching. Our single-crystal formation strategy and direct diffraction evidence resolve the decades-long quest for a post-diamond carbon structure, demonstrating how dynamic loading pathways can make predicted high-pressure phases experimentally accessible.

Materials Science.title: Core Reactivity in Cs-Ba-O ternary system under pressure
Materials Science.summary: High pressure can activate Cs $5p$ core electrons for covalent bonding. In this study, we investigate the Cs-Ba-O system at 150 and 250 GPa using first-principles structure searches. CsBa$_3$O$_8$ and CsBaO$_4$ both lie on the static-lattice convex hull at 250~GPa and exhibit mild Cs $5p$-O $2p$ bonding while retaining O$_2$ units with intermediate superoxide-peroxide character. Cs$_2$BaO$_3$ shows substantially stronger bonding but remains metastable with respect to CsO and BaO. A 1:1 Cs$_2$O-BaO$_2$ mixture provides a solid starting composition for investigating this chemistry, with core-reactive CsO among the predicted products at 250~GPa. Calculated Cs $L_3$-edge x-ray absorption near-edge spectra and powder diffraction patterns provide electronic and structural signatures to guide identification of the predicted phases in diamond anvil cell experiments.

Materials Science.title: Symmetry-Selective Shift Current in Polar Multidomain Superlattices
Materials Science.summary: Periodic polar multidomain superlattices can act as symmetry-selective elements for shift-current generation. We demonstrate this using a two-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with prescribed multidomain configurations. The distinct full-supercell symmetries of periodic head-to-head and head-to-tail arrangements impose different constraints on the shift-current tensor and thereby select complementary nonlinear-response channels, as confirmed by numerical calculations. A direct comparison with equal-area averages of the constituent single-domain spectra shows that an independent-domain average does not reproduce the detailed multidomain spectra. A bond-resolved contribution analysis further clarifies the real-space origin of the multidomain response. Widening each domain from one to ten primitive cells leaves the selection rules intact. On the photon-energy grid used here, the allowed head-to-tail response changes sign and grows by about an order of magnitude. These results provide a theoretical framework for the symmetry-based design of anisotropic optical rectification in polar multidomain superlattices.

Materials Science.title: Temperature-Dependent Ion Dynamics in Argyrodite Superionic Conductor Li$_{6}$PS$_{5}$Cl with Fine-Tuned MACE Foundation Model
Materials Science.summary: The rapid growth of machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIP), particularly the foundational models for materials chemistry, such as MACE, has significantly strengthened our capabilities in studying the complex dynamics of materials through statistical sampling. Here, by performing molecular dynamics with a fine-tuned MACE model, that are further combined with essential dynamics analysis, a tool that is commonly applied in (bio)molecular simulations, we examine the temperature-dependent ion dynamics in a prototypical inorganic solid superionic conductor, namely argyrodite Li$_{6}$PS$_{5}$Cl. Our analyses show clear localised phonon-like dynamics for Li$^+$ ions below 500 K with trajectories lying in a low-dimensional manifold that is highly nonlinear, which is opposite to the case in the high-temperature ($\sim$800 K) end. Between 500-700 K, the system exhibit strong competition in the dynamics between the Li$^+$ and framework ions, that are reflected in both the eigenspectrum and the projected low-dimensional embeddings characterising these dynamics not showing a simple monotonic dependency upon rising temperatures, and is further supported by investigations employing Langevin dynamics that systematically examine how damping the framework motions affects the dynamics of the Li$^+$ ions, thanks to the computational efficiency provided by MLIP. This work thus contributes towards the broader theoretical and data-driven framework for studying the lattice dynamics of solids.

Materials Science.title: Deterministic Electrical Switching in Altermagnets via Surface Antisymmetry Groups
Materials Science.summary: A surface antisymmetry group framework is developed to establish design rules for deterministic electrical switching of the Néel vector in a film of a collinear bipartite antiferromagnet. In centrosymmetric altermagnets, where linear current-induced spin-orbit torques vanish in the bulk, staggered effective fields can nevertheless exist as a macroscopic interfacial response, whose allowed tensor form is determined by the surface antisymmetry point group for the given surface orientation. Such effective fields do not require sublattice equivalence to be broken by the surface and can arise via the Edelstein mechanism driven by sublattice-odd interfacial spin-orbit coupling. General symmetry obstructions to bipolar switching that are valid to all orders in torque angular harmonics are also derived. Separately, the structure of the spin conductivity tensor determines which surface orientations allow transverse spin current generation via the nonrelativistic spin-splitter effect. Taken together, these symmetry-enforced properties establish which surface orientations of $d$-wave altermagnets can serve as deterministically switchable spin current sources in spin-torque heterostructures. Because the design rules are based solely on the surface antisymmetry point group, the symmetry-allowed staggered effective fields are robust against averaging over equilibrium surface roughness.
Materials Science.comment: Substantial revision, including new Sections VII and IX and new Table II

Materials Science.title: Maximum-Temperature Theorem for Nanothermometry
Materials Science.summary:
We derive a sharp upper bound on the quasi-steady temperature rise of a sensor of arbitrary shape and known thermometric volume $V_\mathrm{s}$, placed anywhere inside a region enclosed by an isothermal reference surface. The bound also requires the maximum net heat power $\dot Q_{\scriptscriptstyle
  \mathcal S \subseteq \mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}^{\max}$ crossing any closed surface within the region and a lower bound on its thermal conductivity $κ_{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}}$. It is otherwise independent of the heat-source distribution, domain shape, and source-ensor distance. For $\dot Q_{\scriptscriptstyle
  \mathcal S \subseteq \mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}^{\max}=50~\mathrm{pW}$, $κ_{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}} =0.1~\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $V_{\mathrm s}$ equal to the volume of a $60~\mathrm{nm}$-diameter sphere, the theorem permits a maximum temperature rise of approximately $2~\mathrm{mK}$. Neither source localization nor uncertain source--sensor separation can therefore account for reported kelvin-scale intracellular readings under steady-state heat conduction. The result applies to sensors based on
  nanodiamonds, upconversion nanoparticles, fluorescent polymer beads, and core-shell quantum dots.
Materials Science.comment: 9 pages, 3 figures Clarified heat-power definition, notation and the title. Main results are unchanged

Materials Science.title: Ferroelectricity and Peierls transition in MOI$_2$ (M=Ta, Nb): a first-principle analysis
Materials Science.summary: The van der Waals ferroelectric NbOI$_2$ hosts a polar distortion that is commonly attributed to the Peierls dimerization of its Nb chains. Here we show, using first-principles calculations and a Landau-type energy, that the polar instability is in fact a distinct order parameter that does not stem from the Peierls mode condensation and that three main distinct modes are important in the whole MOI$_2$ family. They are a polar mode $P$, an antipolar mode $η$, and a Peierls mode $δ$, whose stabilities and couplings strongly depend on the nature of the $M$ metal element, as evidenced by the fact that the isostructural, TaOI$_2$ system is not polar while possessing Peirls distortions.

Materials Science.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
Materials Science.summary: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. Spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations show that this Si layer opens new channels for phonon transport across the interface. The engineered interface raises the interfacial thermal conductance to 165 MW m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$ -- the highest value yet reported for $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC interfaces. These results offer an effective way to manage heat in $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ devices and point to a general approach for building phonon-bridging interfaces that improve heat dissipation in heterogeneous systems.

Materials Science.title: Barlow Packings All Have Maximum Packing Fraction: Why it is so Hard to Find Barlow Structures Other than fcc or hcp?
Materials Science.summary: We apply lattice theory to periodic Barlow packings $(X_{1}X_{2}\dots X_{N})_{\infty}$ where $X_{i}\in\{A,B,C\}$ and $X_{i}\neq X_{i+1}$, formed by stacking two-dimensional hexagonal close-packed layers, interacting via generalized $(n,m)$-Lennard-Jones potentials. The cohesive energies of all packings lie between those of hexagonal close-packed (hcp, $(AB)$) and face-centered cubic (fcc, $(ABC)$) structure and vary almost linearly with the fcc stacking fraction. The equilibrium lattice constant, bulk modulus, Einstein frequency, and vibrational entropy show similarly near-linear trends. For the standard $(12,6)$ potential, fcc has the highest vibrational entropy and hcp the lowest, with other Barlow packings falling between them, consistent with previous sticky-hard-sphere Monte Carlo simulations and supported by phonon dispersion calculations. These trends imply an approximately linear dependence of free energy on fcc stacking fraction, with hcp and fcc as endpoints. This provides a simple thermodynamic explanation for why intermediate Barlow stackings are rare in nature: near-linearity offers little driving force to favor them. Exceptions may arise when hcp and fcc are nearly degenerate in energy or when many-body interactions, absent from the present model, favor another stacking. Density-functional calculations including dispersion forces for argon Barlow packings with periods $N=2,3,4$, and $12$ corroborate the predicted near-linear cohesive energy dependence.

Materials Science.title: Curvature Potential Formulation for Thin Elastic Sheets
Materials Science.summary: Thin sheets, from graphene to biological membranes, exhibit wrinkling, folding, and thermal deformations driven by geometric nonlinearities. They are treated using weakly nonlinear theories such as the Föppl-von Kármán equations, whose reliance on small slopes and a single-valued height field excludes large-slope and non-graph configurations even at small strain. We introduce a geometric reformulation in terms of scalar stress and curvature potentials that preserves the FvK structure while removing the graph restriction. We show that intrinsic symmetries of these potentials, as opposed to symmetries of the configuration, can persist when none is apparent in the embedding, enabling analytical solutions of boundary-value problems inaccessible to the conventional height-based formulation. Finite-element comparisons validate the predictions under strong confinement. Together, the extended validity and tractability open analytical routes to fluctuating membranes, ribbons, and architected sheets.

Materials Science.title: Data-Driven Modeling of Molten Chloride Corrosion Using Static Test Data
Materials Science.summary: Molten chloride corrosion has been studied for decades, yet reliable prediction across different alloys, salts, and test conditions remains difficult. In this work, 291 static molten chloride corrosion experiments reported in the literature were compiled into a structured dataset and used to develop an interpretable machine-learning framework for corrosion-rate predictions. To better represent the differences in salt condition across studies, a Chloride Salt Preparation Index (CSPI) was introduced to bring the reported salt-treatment method, atmosphere control, and pre-exposure impurity condition on a common numerical scale. A blended tree-based ensemble provided the most consistent predictive performance, achieving a cross-validated \(R^2\) of 0.85 and an MAE of 0.41 mg cm\(^{-2}\) day\(^{-1}\). The graded CSPI retained more useful information than a simple purified/unpurified classification and emerged as the dominant model descriptor. Global sensitivity and SHAP analyses further identified exposure time, temperature, and alloy chemistry as important contributors to the model predictions, with several observed trends consistent with the established molten-chloride corrosion behavior. The conformal prediction intervals were well calibrated, providing an estimate of prediction uncertainty in addition to the point prediction. Overall, the framework demonstrates that historical corrosion data can support quantitative, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware prediction when experimental context is represented explicitly, while also highlighting where more consistent reporting and targeted experiments are needed to improve future molten-salt corrosion models.

Materials Science.title: Hereditary Effective Atom Theory for Large-Scale Atomic Structure Prediction
Materials Science.summary: Predicting the atomic structure of large systems requires simultaneous exploration of atomic positions, species, and, generally, the number of atoms. The combinatorial growth of possible arrangements can make this search difficult even for standard global optimization methods. We introduce Hereditary Effective Atom Theory (HEAT), which integrates Effective Atom Theory (EAT) into a genetic algorithm. HEAT combines EAT's continuous relaxation of atomic positions, species, and population with the global search capabilities of genetic algorithms. Central to the method is a crossover scheme that directly superimposes two parent structures and relaxes the combined structure. HEAT outperforms conventional genetic-algorithm baselines in recovering a missing 240-atom H sublattice, predicting a 364-atom edge-dislocation core, and reconstructing a 1150-atom interior region of twisted-bilayer $\mathrm{WSe_2}$ from experimental ptychographic constraints. These results demonstrate how continuous effective-atom relaxation improves the exploration of large combinatorial structure spaces.

Materials Science.title: Sudden disappearance of a bright exciton in solid helium
Materials Science.summary: Excitons, bound electron-hole pairs, are investigated extensively in optical spectra, where their wave vector is considered to be vanishing. Excitonic spectra as a function of wave vector are much less explored, both theoretically and with measurements of the loss function. Here, we uncover a striking angular dependence of excitonic spectra for the prototypical case of solid helium, where a prominent excitonic peak is completely suppressed for a momentum transfer in certain directions. The effect is entirely due to the electron-hole exchange interaction. This phenomenon leads to a counter-intuitive effect close to Bragg points, where an infinitesimal change of direction of wave vector is sufficient to change the spectrum dramatically. We explain in which way the nature of excitons makes such a scenario possible. We discuss the pressure dependence, point to experimental evidence for our findings, and predict under which circumstances dramatic angular dependencies may also be found in other materials.

Materials Science.title: High-pressure elastic properties of GeO2 polymorphs up to 120 GPa
Materials Science.summary: We systematically investigated the phase stability, pressure dependence of the elastic properties, and elastic anisotropy of four GeO2 polymorphs: rutile-, CaCl2-, alpha-PbO2-, and pyrite-type phases using theoretical calculations based on density functional theory. The elastic constants were calculated at regular pressure intervals within the stability fields of each phase, as determined by static enthalpy calculations. We further employed a strain-coupled Landau free-energy expansion to describe the pressure evolution of the elastic response associated with the rutile- to CaCl2-type transition and elucidate the origin of the elastic softening near the transition. The rutile- to CaCl2-type phase transition is consistent with a Landau-type second-order transition. As the transition is approached, elastic softening develops in the rutile-type phase, resulting in anomalous pressure dependence of the bulk and shear moduli. The calculated elastic-wave anisotropy increases markedly near the transition, primarily due to the rapid reduction in shear-wave velocity, reaching a maximum of approximately 190% at 20 GPa. Following the transition, the anisotropy decreases sharply in the CaCl2-type phase and exhibits discontinuity at the CaCl2-type/alpha-PbO2-type phase boundary. The higher-pressure alpha-PbO2- and pyrite-type phases exhibit comparatively weak pressure dependence of anisotropy, with small discontinuities at their respective phase boundaries. The pyrite-type phase has the lowest anisotropy with AP = 4% and AS = 12% at 120 GPa, consistent with its high-symmetry cubic structure and nearly isotropic elastic-wave propagation.

Materials Science.title: Stability and Relaxation of Electron-Phonon Systems at Strong Coupling
Materials Science.summary: We study the kinetic properties of Migdal-Eliashberg theory (MET) for electron-phonon interactions at strong coupling. Previously, the system was found to be dynamically unstable at large couplings within a Markovian quantum Boltzmann approximation. Using the quasiclassical Kadanoff-Baym equation, we show that this instability is absent when non-Markovian effects are taken into account. We also analyze the long-time relaxation dynamics at strong-couplin, and find a clear imprint of the non-Markovian nature of the dynamics: in an intermediate temperature range between the Debye frequency and the coupling strength, the relaxation rate becomes linear in temperature with Planckian slope, while the leading relaxation mode acquires a large imaginary component, producing strongly oscillatory decay. Our results imply that any instability which preempts superconductivity must arise from effects beyond MET, such as phonon softening or polaronic effects at finite electronic bandwidth. This shows that the characteristic phonon frequency is not a fundamental bound on $T_c$, and leaves open a route to higher $T_c$ in multi-orbital electron-phonon systems.

Materials Science.title: Energy-Based Anisotropic Hysteresis Modeling for Permanent Magnets
Materials Science.summary: Modeling the anisotropic hysteresis behaviour of permanent magnets requires vector hysteresis models capable of representing preferred (easy) magnetization directions. This work extends the energy-based vector play model to anisotropic materials by replacing the spherical pinning region of each particle with an ellipsoid, whose semi-axes represent direction-dependent pinning forces. Special attention is paid to the geometrically consistent adaptation of the update formula for the vector play model. The anhysteretic part of the model is also given an angular dependency. The model is compared to measurements taken from a NdFeB magnet and reproduces the measured loops for field inclinations of up to 30° from the easy axis.
Materials Science.comment: 6 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables, submitted to the 22nd International IGTE Symposium 2026

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Large-Tiny Spin-Stripe SDW Order in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ via $^{139}$La-NQR Spectroscopy: Reconsideration Based on the $Am2m$ Structure
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: The lower-symmetry $Am2m$ structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted $Amam$ structure. Here, we reexamine the crystal structure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and the spin configuration of spin-density-wave (SDW) state via $^{139}$La nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). The observation of two distinct La(2) sites in the NQR spectra is naturally accounted for by the $Am2m$ structure without any special assumptions, whereas it cannot be reconciled within the $Amam$ framework. Within the $Am2m$ framework, we reanalyze the spin configuration of the SDW phase and identify it as a large-tiny spin-stripe structure, arising naturally from two inequivalent Ni sites with large and tiny magnetic moments. These results establish the itinerant nature of the SDW order at ambient pressure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, providing a basis for understanding its relationship to the emergence of high-$T_c$ superconductivity under high pressure.

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Tree tensor network states represent low-energy states faithfully
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: Extending corresponding results for matrix product states [Verstraete and Cirac, PRB 73, 094423 (2006); Schuch et al. PRL 100, 030504 (2008)], it is shown how the approximation error of tree tensor network states (TTNS) can be bounded using Schmidt spectra or Rényi entanglement entropies of the target quantum state. Conversely, one obtains bounds on TTNS bond dimensions needed to achieve a specific approximation accuracy. The result implies that efficient TTNS approximations exist if $α<1$ Rényi entanglement entropies for single-branch cuts obey an area law, as in ground and low-energy states of certain gapped systems on tree graphs.
Strongly Correlated Electrons.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures; corrected typo in Eq. (1), minor improvements; published version

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Simulating a chiral gauge theory
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: Chiral gauge theories underlie the Standard Model, yet none has been simulated nonperturbatively. Lattice constructions that evade the Nielsen-Ninomiya obstruction entail complex fermion measures or infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces. Here we provide a gauge-invariant Hamiltonian lattice regularization of 1+1-dimensional abelian chiral gauge theories built from clock-and-shift qudits with $\mathbb{Z}_N$ gauge fields, in which the global chiral symmetry and its 't Hooft anomaly survive exactly mod $N$. Anomaly cancellation on the lattice lets the Gauss laws be imposed and solved exactly, reducing the theory to an unconstrained qudit chain. Using infinite matrix product states, we simulate the canonical 1+1-dimensional chiral gauge theory, the 34-50 model, and find excellent agreement with analytic predictions, showing that a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space at $N=6$ reproduces the expected infrared physics of the continuum 34-50 model. This provides an efficient and practical solution to the problem of simulating general abelian chiral gauge theories in 1+1 dimensions, both on classical and quantum computers.

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Quantum Tunneling-induced Hybridization and Coherent Dynamics of Jackiw-Rebbi Zero Modes in a Modified Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: We investigate analytically and numerically the tunneling-induced hybridization and coherent dynamics of Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes in a modified Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model. Unlike the conventional SSH model, this modified system possess two bulk gap-closing points, namely the quadratic-type gap-closing point at momenta $k_0=0$ and the Dirac-type gap-closing points at $k_0=\pmπ/4a$. Although the quadratic point does not support a topological domain wall due to the absence of mass inversion, the low-energy Dirac theory around $k_0=\pmπ/4a$ predicts an effective mass that changes sign at two spatially separated domain walls under a kink profile, generating a pair of JR bound states with each states localized at one of those domain walls. We show that the finite spatial overlap between the JR zero modes lifts the zero-energy degeneracy through quantum tunneling, producing symmetric-antisymmetric hybridized states. Using an effective two-level description, we demonstrate that hybridized JR modes undergo coherent tunneling oscillations between the two domain walls, accompanied by periodic transfer of sublattice polarization between the (A,C) and (B,D) sectors. Our results establish a unified framework connecting JR zero modes, quantum tunneling, and coherent dynamics in modified SSH systems, offering a promising platform for controllable topological quantum-state transfer in engineered lattice structures.

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Hidden entropic order of emergent charges in a classical Ampère spin liquid
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: Classical spin liquids are characterized by an extensive number of ground-state configurations. Coulomb spin liquids have, in this ground-state manifold, a divergence-free local constraint, which gives dipolar correlations and pinch points in the structure factor. Recently, models with a complementary ground-state constraint, defined by a zero-circulation constraint (Ampère's law), have been proposed. While classical Coulomb spin liquids forbid emergent charges, their Ampère counterparts leave the charges unconstrained. Here we study an Ising Ampère model on the octochlore lattice. The ground states obey a Gauss law for an antisymmetric rank-two field, i.e., three coupled two-dimensional Gauss laws, which are expected to produce pinch points in the structure factor. Nevertheless, maximal charges, vertices with all six arrows in or out, spontaneously accumulate on one of the two sublattices of the cubic lattice, with disordered signs. This order has a purely entropic origin; it washes out the pinch-point singularities at large scales, produces no magnetic Bragg peaks, and coexists with an extensive entropy. The system enters into this sublattice long-range ordered state through a continuous transition in what seems to be the three-dimensional Ising universality class. Moreover, the state has no magnetic order; it is even under time reversal: it is a hidden, entropic order within the Ampère manifold. Thus, a system whose Gauss law would predict an algebraic spin liquid becomes, through a non-magnetic ordering transition, a partially ordered short-range spin liquid. Our study is based on a combination of the constraint-vector theory, exact bounds and enumeration, and Monte Carlo, Wang-Landau, and parallel-tempering simulations.
Strongly Correlated Electrons.comment: Main text: 7 pages, 5 figures. Supplemental Material: 9 pages, 11 figures

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Cost scaling of MPS and TTNS simulations for 2D and 3D systems with area-law entanglement
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: Tensor network states are an indispensable tool for the simulation of strongly correlated quantum many-body systems. In recent years, tree tensor network states (TTNS) have been successfully used for two-dimensional systems and to benchmark quantum simulation approaches for condensed matter, nuclear, and particle physics. In comparison to the more traditional approach based on matrix product states (MPS), the graph distance of physical degrees of freedom can be drastically reduced in TTNS. Surprisingly, it turns out that, for large systems in $D>1$ spatial dimensions, MPS simulations of low-energy states are nevertheless more efficient than TTNS simulations. With a focus on $D=2$ and 3, the scaling of computational costs for different boundary conditions is determined under the assumption that the system obeys an entanglement (log-)area law, implying that bond dimensions scale exponentially in the interface area of the associated subsystems.
Strongly Correlated Electrons.comment: 13 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables; added discussions of more general class of TTNS (including higher vertex degrees), systems with log-area law entanglement, Renyi parameter, TTNS tensor-operation costs; further minor improvements

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2.
