In addition, we successfully achieved an enhanced gain of $3.2\times 10^4$ without increasing the discharge risk by employing an alternative operation mode.

Nuclear Experiment.title: Analysis of Xe-131 Prompt Gammas
Nuclear Experiment.summary: The prompt gammas of Xe-131 from thermal neutron capture were measured for the first time at the Fission Product Prompt gamma-ray Spectrometer by irradiation of isotopically enriched Xe-130 in a high-purity quartz ampoule. Through gamma-gamma coincidences, 42 new prompt gammas were measured and 14 new nuclear states determined.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Hypersurface covariance in relativistic local equilibrium
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Defining equilibrium typically requires specifying a three-dimensional spacelike hypersurface. While global equilibrium is hypersurface covariant, calculations involving local equilibrium can exhibit hypersurface dependence. In this work, we use polarization in heavy-ion collisions within the Zubarev response approach as an example to show that the hypersurface dependence arising from the local-equilibrium part of the density operator is canceled by an overlooked nondissipative contribution from its so-called ``dissipative part". We establish a hypersurface-covariant Zubarev framework for general geometries by consistently including both nondissipative and dissipative parts, eliminating dependence on the arbitrary hypersurface vector. The remaining frame dependence is physical: it arises from the medium rest frame entering the particle distribution and the time direction of the dissipative process, which usually coincide. This resolves, in principle, the longstanding and widely discussed conceptual disagreement over hypersurface dependence between two influential studies addressing the sign puzzles of $Λ$-hyperon polarization in heavy-ion collisions

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Joint Bayesian Inference for Extraction of Charmonium Long Distance Matrix Elements Using PYTHIA
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a joint Bayesian extraction of the nonrelativistic QCD long-distance matrix elements (LDMEs) for $J/ψ$, $ψ(2S)$, and $χ_c$ production, using short-distance coefficients and feed-down structure implemented in PYTHIA 8.317. Rather than fitting each charmonium state separately, we construct channel-resolved responses that link parent production to daughter feed-down and infer all LDMEs simultaneously from 286 prompt charmonium measurements in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=5.02$-13 TeV at the LHC. The extracted LDMEs provide a good description of the data, with an overall $χ^2/\mathrm{ndf}=1.18$. We also provide a positivity-constrained set that can be used directly as PYTHIA input. Using the extracted LDMEs, we predict prompt $J/ψ$ and $ψ(2S)$ cross sections at high transverse momentum in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=200$ GeV, which can be tested with RHIC data.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Testing the Spin of New Physics with Top Precision Measurements
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Precision measurements can reveal not only the presence of new physics, but also information about the dynamics that generated it. We study this question in top-pair production by comparing three top-philic scenarios: a colored scalar top partner, a colored vector-like fermion, and a spin-one $Z^\prime$ mediator. The first two contribute through loop corrections, while the $Z^\prime$ contributes at tree level. We show that the scalar and vector-like fermion scenarios match onto the same effective operator structure at low energies,making their distinction unfeasible using the EFT approach. However, near or above threshold their full loop amplitudes develop distinct momentum-dependent interference patterns. Using the top transverse momentum spectrum we find that resonant and loop-induced effects are relatively easy to distinguish, whereas separating the scalar and vector-like hypotheses is substantially more challenging. Nevertheless, their different analytic structures leave measurable information in the shape of the distribution. These results illustrate how precision differential measurements can probe the spin and dynamics of virtual new states even when they are not directly reconstructed, and motivate more powerful multidimensional analyses.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 33 pages, 12 figures. The datasets and code used to obtain all the results presented here as well as additional details are available in https://github.com/andlessa/UnfoldingBSMttbar/releases

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Signatures of Neutrinophilic Pion Dark Matter
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study the phenomenology of pion dark matter coupled to neutrinos in a confining sector that dynamically generates both small neutrino masses and dark matter mass from gauge confinement. Dark matter semi-annihilation to active neutrinos or annihilation to light sterile neutrinos can reproduce the observed relic abundance through thermal freeze-out while satisfying constraints from self-interactions. In the first scenario, semi-annihilations of sub-GeV dark matter in the galactic halo produce a flux of antineutrinos which can provide a viable interpretation for the mild electron antineutrino excess reported by the Super-Kamiokande collaboration. We assess the potential of the JUNO detector to test this interpretation. In the second scenario, light sterile neutrinos can leave signatures through displaced vertex searches at accelerator facilities.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Top-Quark Pair Production and Decay in Extended Higgs Sectors
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Extensions of the Higgs sector in the Standard Model address outstanding questions like the first-order electroweak phase transition and also present a rich collider phenomenology. The two-Higgs-doublet model is a minimal extension of the Standard Model with an extra complex $SU(2)_L$ doublet, and consists of an extra scalar, a pseudoscalar and a pair of charged Higgs bosons along with a Standard-Model-like Higgs boson. We present a modified version of the hvq library of the POWHEG-BOX-V2 event generator interfaced with the OpenLoops 2 amplitude generator to obtain predictions for top-quark pair production at NLO accuracy, including top-quark decays with full spin correlations in a framework that extends the SM Higgs sector with an extra heavy scalar and a pseudoscalar. The interference effects between the scalar and pseudoscalar signals, and the Standard Model QCD background are implemented. We include parton showers and hadronisation, and take detector effects into consideration. The status of our work and plans to extend it to future collider projects are discussed.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 6 pages, 2 figures. Prepared for submission to Proceedings of Science (PoS) for the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP 2026)

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Algorithmic Construction of Vector-Valued Modular Forms and Application to an $A_4\times\mathbb{Z}_4$-invariant Model of Leptons
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present an algorithmic procedure that constructs the Vector-Valued Modular Forms (VVMFs) of finite modular groups, as well as its implementation in a companion code. The usual method consists in building the first few VVMFs, whose tensor products then generate the others. We address the difficulty of systematically finding the minimal set of VVMFs that suffices to produce all higher-weight ones, and we propose a method to identify it that makes use of the Burnside-Brauer theorem. For any given group, whose basic group-theoretic and representation-theoretic description is provided by the user, the code determines the minimal set of VVMFs, explicitly builds it using general results of the theory of such functions, then performs the tensor products that generate any other VVMF. Importantly, it automatically takes into account all caveats that might arise during the study of new groups. Our approach reproduces the known results for the finite modular groups explored in the recent phenomenological literature on modular flavor symmetries, and works for additional groups which we tested. We illustrate our algorithm and the working of our code by studying a model of leptons based on the unexplored finite modular group $A_4\times\mathbb{Z}_4$.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Dark Energy Crosses the Line: Quantifying and Testing the Evidence for Phantom Crossing
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Combinations of the most recent CMB, BAO, and SNeIa datasets, when analyzed using the CPL parametrization, $w(a) = w_0 + (1 - a) w_a$, exclude $Λ$CDM at $\gtrsim\!3σ$ in favor of a dark energy equation of state (EoS) parameter that crosses the phantom divide. We confirm this behavior and show that it persists when DESI BAO data are replaced by SH0ES $H_0$ measurements, despite the known tension between these probes in the presence of CMB data. In both cases, the constraints favor a transition from an early-time phantom-like phase to a late-time quintessence-like phase, with the crossing occurring at different redshifts depending on the dataset combination. The probability that a phantom divide line (PDL) crossing does not occur within the expansion history is excluded at significance levels ranging \mbox{between $3.1σ$\,--\,$5.2σ$.} To investigate whether the apparent PDL crossing is a genuine feature preferred by the data or an artifact of the linear form of the CPL parametrization, we isolate the PDL crossing feature by introducing two modified versions of CPL that explicitly forbid it: CPL${}_{>a_\mathrm{c}}$ and CPL${}_{<a_\mathrm{c}}$. These models are physically motivated in that they phenomenologically capture the behavior of thawing and freezing scalar field scenarios. While previous studies have primarily considered thawing quintessence as a non-crossing alternative, we find that a freezing phantom-like model is the only one capable of performing comparably to CPL--and only in a few cases. Nevertheless, across all dataset combinations considered, the standard CPL model consistently provides the best fit, strongly indicating that the data genuinely favor a PDL crossing.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 12 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D

High Energy Phenomenology.title: FCC-μe: High Energy, High Luminosity Muon-Electron Collider & Neutrino Factory at CERN
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The concept is presented of making at the FCC-$ee$ (or CEPC) facility $μ^+e^-$ collisions at the centre-of-mass energy between 1 and 2 TeV and the average luminosity above $10^{34}$cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, concurrently to the $e^+e^-$ collisions. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including the exciting prospect of measurements of the Higgs boson self-interaction, and is followed by a presentation of the FCC-$μe$ layout -- from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations are also given regarding the machine-detector interface and the performance of the FCC-$μe$ and associated neutrino factory. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying relevance of such anti-muon beams for any future high energy storage ring as well as for neutrino science.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: To be published in $Acta~Phys. Polon. B$ - contribution to the proceedings of Workshop on "Ultra-cold Muons for the LHC", Sep 24-26, 2026, at AGH University of Kraków - 7 pages, 1 figure and 2 tables; with modified baseline parameters and extended discussion of performance, including the LEP3 case

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Landau's Leviathans
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a new method together with a proof-of-concept implementation for determining the Landau singularities of Feynman integrals, read off directly from where the Euler characteristic of the associated integral drops. Working over finite fields makes the requisite elimination tractable for multi-scale integrals at the multi-loop frontier. The algorithm returns the genuine and complete set of singularities, subject to a set of conditions which are practically testable. We apply these methods to classes of Feynman integrals beyond the reach of current methods, including non-planar six-point diagrams at two loops, as well as a fully massive three-loop envelope graph. Several of the newly found singularities, both in $d$- and 4-dimensional external kinematics, are of unexpected complexity when compared to previously known singularities for these examples.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Searching for Cosmological Collider in the Planck CMB Data II: collider templates and Modal analysis
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Signatures of massive particles during inflation are highly informative targets for cosmological experiments. With recent progress on both theoretical and observational frontiers, we have reached the point where these novel signals of primordial non-Gaussianities (PNG) can be systematically tested with increasingly precise data. In this paper, we present the results of improved CMB data analysis for cosmological collider signals using Planck CMB data. To set the stage, we first construct a set of simplified but characteristic collider templates which are accurate over a broad range of particle masses, spins and sound speeds. In order to break degeneracies with single-field PNG, we propose an orthogonalization scheme such that the collider templates are uncorrelated with the highly constrained equilateral and orthogonal shapes. On this basis, we deploy the Modal bispectrum estimator for the Planck analysis and perform a systematic scan of parameters to search for the most significant collider signal. The maximum signal-to-noise ratio is found to be $2.35σ$ for an orthogonalized massive spin-0 exchange after taking into account the look-elsewhere effect. In addition, we cross-validate the Modal analysis with the CMB-BEST pipeline, which demonstrates the consistency of results across the benchmark examples of collider templates. Given the low signal-to-noise ratio regime we find at the current stage of PNG observations, we believe the orthogonalization procedure provides an optimized strategy for future tests of the cosmological collider signals.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Ultra-High-Energy Tau Neutrinos as Probes of Lorentz Invariance
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Neutrino telescopes have detected astrophysical neutrinos with energies up to ${O}(100)$ PeV. Several current and proposed experiments aim to observe neutrinos at even higher energies, with the goal of detecting cosmogenic neutrinos. This increase in neutrino energy makes tests of Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) particularly appealing, since the effects of higher-dimension LIV operators on neutrino propagation grow rapidly with energy. In this work, we investigate the potential of the upcoming experiments GRAND and POEMMA to probe LIV in the neutrino sector through the detection of ultra-high-energy tau neutrinos. We generate the cosmogenic neutrino flux using SimProp and interface it with a calculation of neutrino flavor transition probabilities in the presence of LIV effects. Deviations from standard flavor transition probabilities manifest as changes in the expected tau neutrino event rates at GRAND and POEMMA. We first consider the case with a single nonzero LIV operator of various dimensions, and find that the projected sensitivities exceed existing limits from lower-energy probes by orders of magnitude. We then explore scenarios with multiple nonzero LIV parameters and show that their interplay can significantly modify the sensitivities compared to the single-parameter case. Overall, we find that upcoming observations of ultra-high-energy tau neutrinos will place some of the most stringent constraints on LIV.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 19+2 pages, 8+1 figures, matches published version. Code available at https://github.com/samiur06/cosmogenic_neutrino_LIV

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Has Quarkyonic Matter Been Seen in Lattice Simulations?
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Quarkyonic Matter refers to the dual state of matter between confined hadrons and quasi-free quarks. This duality leads to a robust constraint on the behavior of the distribution functions. After a comprehensive review of Quarkyonic Matter based on the distribution functions, we discuss recent lattice data for two-color QCD in $(1+1)$ and $(3+1)$ dimensions at finite baryon number density and QCD in $(3+1)$ dimensions at finite isospin density, as well as the astrophysically inferred equation of state. Taken together, these results reveal a coherent picture consistent with the emergence of Quarkyonic Matter in lattice simulations. Future lattice calculations of baryon and gauge-invariant quark momentum distributions at high density would provide a more direct test of this interpretation.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Analytic parametrisations of the scale dependence of proton parton distributions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) are non-perturbative inputs whose scale dependence is governed by the Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) equations. Their numerical evaluation commonly relies on interpolation of tabulated grids. We discuss an analytic representation of collinear proton PDFs in $(x,Q^2)$, obtained by promoting the parameters of a standard $x$-space parametrisation to functions of the scale. The coefficients are reconstructed from the HERAPDF2.0 NLO set using machine-assisted fitting techniques, with sampling in $10^{-4}\le x\le 0.65$ and scales up to 1 TeV. The resulting ML-PDFs reproduce integrated distributions at the sub-percent level for most flavours, with deviations reaching about 1.5% for the strange quark at the highest scales. They satisfy valence and momentum sum rules at the percent level and reproduce representative $pp\toπ$ and $pp\toγπ$ cross sections within approximately 2% and 5%, respectively, in the kinematic regions studied. Compared with grid interpolation through LHAPDF, direct evaluation of the analytic expressions reduces the total Monte Carlo run time by about 11% and 30% in these two applications.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 1 table, contribution to the proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP 2026), 30 July - 5 August 2026, Natal, Brazil

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Leptogenesis with sub-electroweak-scale reheating temperature
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study the generation of the baryon asymmetry of the Universe via leptogenesis during the post-inflationary reheating epoch, considering reheating temperatures below the temperature of sphaleron freeze-out. Within the framework of a monomial inflaton potential during reheating, we analyze three perturbative reheating scenarios in which the inflaton decays into (i) a pair of Standard Model (SM)-like bosons, (ii) a pair of SM-like fermions, or (iii) exclusively into a pair of heavy right-handed neutrinos, which eventually decays into the SM final states after briefly dominating the energy density of the Universe. For each case, we identify the regions of parameter space that successfully reproduce the observed baryon asymmetry consistently tracking the sphaleron interaction rate during reheating, while satisfying existing cosmological constraints. We also highlight the potential of future primordial gravitational wave observations to probe this class of scenarios.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 43 pages, 20 captioned figures, improved calculations, figures updated, matches the version accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. D

High Energy Phenomenology.title: DIS-secting the universe with high-energy neutrinos
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We revisit the impact of electroweak (EW) radiative corrections on the kinematic distributions of charged leptons in neutrino-induced charged-current (CC) deep inelastic scattering (DIS). These corrections are particularly relevant for observables sensitive to collinear photon radiation, such as the energy spectrum of high-energy muons detected in neutrino telescopes. To study these effects, we implement full next-to-leading order (NLO) EW corrections to CC DIS in a flexible Monte Carlo framework, supplemented with higher-order logarithmically enhanced final-state QED radiation and coherent scattering contributions. We compare our results to exclusive NLO QCD plus parton shower (PS) predictions obtained with an existing $\texttt{POWHEG-BOX}$ event generator, examining different PS models and settings. Based on this comparison, we provide recommendations for the use of the $\texttt{POWHEG-BOX}$ event generator in experimental analyses. We further assess the impact of radiative corrections on the correlation between the observed muon energy and the incoming neutrino energy, and on the mean inelasticity averaged over a realistic neutrino flux. These corrections can exceed $10\%$, and above about $10^4\,{\rm GeV}$ they receive sizeable contributions from photon-initiated and coherent $W$-boson production, which are not included in the event generator.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Defining a Minimum Resolution for Unbinned Analyses
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Collider analyses combine rigorous statistical techniques with state-of-the-art Machine Learning models. However, when the latter are used directly to estimate the likelihood function of the background, hard to quantify systematic effects may bias the estimation of the relevant signal parameters. To address this problem, we present the Minimum Resolution Likelihood (MRL) method, which defines a Fiducial Signal Region that aims to turn systematic effects into statistical uncertainties. We show with examples that the resulting signal strength estimation has a reduced bias, with the effect depending on the sample size and type of signal considered. We consider both toy examples and a realistic application based on the HI-SIGMA technique applied to di-Higgs searches.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 22 pages + references and 10 figures. Updated version to be resubmitted to SciPost Physics. The figures and text have been modified to reflect a corrected seeding procedure in the code and slightly modified toy background and signal models. Comments welcome!

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Quantum Fourier integration of decay rates at next-to-leading order
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We discuss the use of quantum neural networks (QNNs) as a tool for integrating decay rates at next-to-leading order (NLO) in perturbation theory. Data-encoding quantum circuits admit a truncated Fourier-series representation, enabling a trained QNN to approximate a target integrand and provide the coefficients subsequently integrated with Quantum Fourier Iterative Amplitude Estimation (QFIAE). The causal-unitary formulation of the Loop-Tree Duality (LTD) combines virtual and real contributions into locally finite integrands suitable for this representation. We consider $H\to q\bar q(g)$, $γ^*\to q\bar q(g)$ and $Φ\toφφ(φ)$, comparing quantum-simulator and quantum-hardware results with analytic NLO predictions. The study illustrates the potential of Fourier-based QNN integration for high-energy physics.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, Contribution to the proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP 2026), 30 July - 5 August 2026, Natal, Brazil

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Light Primordial Black Holes from a First-Order Phase Transition near the End of Inflation: Baryogenesis and Gravitational Wave Signatures
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate the formation and cosmological consequences of light primordial black holes (PBHs) from vacuum bubbles nucleated during a spectator sector first-order phase transition in inflation. We construct a phenomenological model in which the spectator potential evolves with the rolling inflaton, allowing vacuum bubbles to nucleate and grow during inflation. The vacuum ordering subsequently reverses near the end of inflation, leaving the bubble interiors in a metastable false vacuum state. We examine their stability against reverse vacuum tunneling and impose benchmark conditions to suppress this process before and after reheating. Sufficiently large bubbles can subsequently undergo supercritical evolution and form PBHs. In this framework, the PBH abundance is determined by the vacuum tunneling history, while the characteristic mass depends on the nucleation epoch and bubble growth during inflation. For sufficiently light PBHs that evaporate before big bang nucleosynthesis, Hawking radiation can create locally superheated regions in which electroweak symmetry is restored, potentially generating a baryon asymmetry in the presence of additional CP-violating interactions. We also investigate the direct gravitational wave (GW) signals from Hawking radiation and the induced GWs from PBH density fluctuations, the latter arising if an early PBH dominated epoch occurs. For representative benchmark parameters, the resulting baryon asymmetry can reach the ten-percent level of the observed value, while the induced GW signal can reach a peak amplitude of $Ω_{\rm GW,0}h^2\sim10^{-7}$ at frequencies of order $10$-$10^2\,{\rm Hz}$.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: about 50 pages, 2 figures; comments are welcome

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Minimal-length kinematics of coherent light and a proposed two-color vacuum chronoscopy
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The unification of quantum theory and general relativity suggests the existence of a minimal measurable length, leading to a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) and an energy-dependent vacuum group velocity. Testing these effects with macroscopic objects typically encounters the ``soccer-ball problem,'' where applying Planck-scale deformations to the total momentum predicts observationally ruled-out velocity deviations. We adopt the prescription, natural in quantum field theory (QFT), in which the GUP modifies single-mode commutators, and verify by explicit calculation that the macroscopic group velocity of a multimode coherent pulse reduces to the single-photon GUP velocity evaluated at the central wavelength, multiplied by the classical Gaussian-beam factor, with no dependence on the total pulse energy. The energy--momentum relation $E=pc$ itself is unmodified; the deformation enters through the velocity--momentum relation and is equivalent to a modified dispersion relation in the wave vector, with a quadratic coefficient that depends on which of the two variables is used. The soccer-ball problem --- which arises only when the GUP is applied to the center-of-mass momentum of a composite system --- is therefore absent for coherent light, and macroscopic petawatt pulses probe the same parameter space as single high-energy photons. Building on this framework, we propose a two-color vacuum chronoscopy experiment using a short-pulse petawatt laser and its high-harmonic generation. By systematically varying the macroscopic beam waist, our setup separates Planck-scale kinematic shifts from classical diffraction delays, establishing a controlled, source-independent terrestrial methodology whose sensitivity we assess against current astrophysical bounds and against the dominant waist-independent systematics that limit it, residual-gas dispersion and the harmonic birth-time offset.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Investigating bottom quark effects in Higgs boson pair production
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate different effects of bottom quark masses in Higgs boson pair production, considering both bottom quark loops and bottom quarks in the initial state. While the effects are negligible at total cross section level, the situation is different for the Higgs boson pair invariant mass distribution close to the production threshold of the two Higgs bosons.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 25 pages, 9 figures, contribution to the Report 5 of the LHC Higgs Working Group

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Novel collider signatures in the type-I 2HDM+$a$ model
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The 2HDM+$a$ model is one of the main models used in the interpretations of dark matter searches at the LHC. So far, all the 2HDM+$a$ benchmarks considered by the ATLAS and CMS experiments are limited to a type-II Yukawa sector, in which the Higgs bosons $A$, $H$, and $H^\pm$ are all constrained to be mass-degenerate and heavier than around $600 \, {\rm GeV}$. In this work, we present the first detailed study of 2HDM+$a$ models with a type-I Yukawa sector, which, for moderate values of $\tanβ$, lift the constraints from flavour physics, allowing the extra Higgs bosons to be even lighter than the $125 \, {\rm GeV}$ Higgs boson discovered at the LHC. We discuss several benchmarks where the $A$, $H$, and $H^\pm$ states are not necessarily mass-degenerate and the signatures that arise in these models, some of which have not yet been explored at the LHC. We present the dominant channels in the studied benchmarks and the expected sensitivity in Run 2 data using truth-level analyses and discuss potential improvements in the experimental searches for Run 3.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 47 pages, 14 figures; v3: bounded-from-below conditions corrected ($P^4$ term added, misprints in (3.8) fixed), results unchanged. Thanks to Daniel Puigmartí Molano for pointing this out!

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Light Mediators at the Neutrino-Dark Matter Frontier: Coherent Scattering, Precision Constraints, and Complementary Searches
High Energy Phenomenology.summary:
Low-threshold neutrino and dark-matter experiments constrain light mediators through different momentum transfers, targets, and coupling combinations. We examine scalar and vector interactions in coherent neutrino--nucleus scattering, neutrino--electron scattering, and dark-matter direct detection. Three representative interaction models are used to compare recoil spectra and coupling degeneracies. For $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ and $^{131}\mathrm{Xe}$, the nuclear-charge response matrix has a condition number of approximately 115, so two different targets may still leave nearly parallel blind directions. An analytic profile-likelihood calculation shows how spectral overlap and uncertainties in neutrino interactions affect dark-matter discovery sensitivity in the neutrino fog. We discuss the implications of measurements from COHERENT, CONUS+, LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T and specify which theoretical inputs, detector responses, and statistical correlations are needed to combine their constraints.
  keyword : coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering; light mediators; neutrino--electron scattering; dark matter direct detection; non-standard interactions; solar neutrinos; complementarity

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Linking chiral nuclear forces to light-ion collisions: a global sensitivity analysis
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Ultrarelativistic $^{16}$O+$^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne+$^{20}$Ne collisions recently performed at the Large Hadron Collider have imaged quadrupole and octupole correlations between nucleons through the collective flow of emitted hadrons. We establish a quantitative link between these correlations and the low-energy constants (LECs) that enter chiral inter-nucleon interactions. Emulators built using the subspace-projected coupled-cluster method enable a global sensitivity analysis of the ground-state quadrupole mean-square eccentricity, revealing that quadrupole correlations respond linearly and additively to all 16 LECs at next-to-next-to-leading order in the chiral expansion. The sensitivities differ markedly in $^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne, and are complementary to those of the binding energy and charge radius, the bulk observables to which nuclear interactions are typically calibrated. In particular, $^{20}$Ne collisions dominantly probe the spin-orbit part of two-nucleon interactions. Soft-particle correlations in light-ion collisions thus constitute a new type of data to study nuclear forces and their emergence from quantum chromodynamics.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, plus 2 pages End Matter with 2 figures and 2 tables

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Spontaneous Scoto-leptogenesis
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We propose a low-scale spontaneous leptogenesis scenario within the dynamical minimal scotogenic model for accommodating neutrino masses and inert scalar dark matter simultaneously. Thus, we dub the mechanism Spontaneous Scoto-leptogenesis. In this setup, a rolling Majoron arising from the global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry breaking induces an effective chemical potential for the $B-L$ charge in the presence of $B-L$ violating interactions that allow for the efficient decays and inverse decays of right handed neutrinos (RHN) and RHN mediated scattering, so it gives rise to the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe through the electroweak sphaleron conversion. The mechanism becomes effective in the strong washout regime and successfully lowers the viable mass scale of the lightest RHN to the range of TeV scales, thereby making the thermal scotogenic leptogenesis with two hierarchical RHNs accessible to direct tests. We identify the roles of the $λ_5$ coupling for spontaneous leptogenesis and inert scalar dark matter through the efficient erasure of the inert scalar asymmetry. We also explore the regime for Majoron dark matter from the kinetic misalignment, showing that a multicomponent dark sector comprising the inert scalar and the Majoron can be realized in the model. The resulting framework provides a unified origin for low-scale baryogenesis, neutrino masses, and multicomponent dark sector, so it can be tested by complementary experimental probes through direct detection experiments, collider searches for inert scalars, and future detection of Majoron dark matter or dark radiation.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 24 pages, 7 figures, 1 table, new discussions associated to dark matter annihilation, $ΔL=2$ scattering effect on leptogensis are added

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Manifestation of scale symmetry in nuclear medium
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: This memorial tribute to Mannque Rho focuses on the role of scale symmetry in baryonic matter, especially on its profound influence on the possible resolution of the ``quenched $g_A$" problem in the Gamow-Teller transition of nuclei, the pseudoconformal structure of dense nuclear matter and the origin of the peak of sound velocity of nuclear matter. The discussion is based on the genuine dilaton scenario, anchored on the Crewther-Tunstall infrared fixed point, which provides a unified framework where scale symmetry---broken explicitly by the QCD trace anomaly---can be spontaneously broken, yielding the scalar $f_0(500)$ as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson. In nuclear medium, this scenario serves as a natural foundation of the Brown-Rho scaling---a relation that has been central to nuclear physics for over three decades. The sound velocity of nuclear matter exhibits a characteristic peak at intermediate densities arising from the kink behavior of the dilaton field, a unique signature of scale symmetry realization that distinguishes the dilaton-compensated effective theory from conventional Walecka-type models. At higher densities, the approach to the dilaton-limit fixed point produces pseudo-conformal behavior with sound velocity $v_s^2 = 1/3$ saturating from below at $n \gtrsim 3n_0$, while the trace of the energy-momentum tensor remains nonzero. The framework also provides a natural resolution of the long-standing ``quenched $g_A$" problem, demonstrating that nuclear correlations, not fundamental quenching, account for the effective axial coupling approaching unity. The continuity from the unitary limit at low density to the dilaton limit at high density suggests a pervasive role for scale symmetry in nuclear dynamics across all density regimes.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: Contribution to the volume to be published in Journal of Subatomic Particles and Cosmology in memorial of Prof. Mannque Rho

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Quantum transport of vortex electrons in bending magnets and circular accelerators
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Controlling the sizes and phase structure of single-particle wave packets in accelerators remains an experimental challenge and requires understanding how bending magnets transform these states. An important example is transporting relativistic vortex electrons through the magnets to a collision point while keeping a narrow orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) distribution. We derive an effective Hamiltonian that accounts for the packet acceleration, employ it to obtain a generalized BMT-like equation, match the electron state at both magnet boundaries, and calculate the mean OAM and its variance. A half turn can reverse the mean OAM relative to the momentum while broadening its distribution, so recovering the mean does not ensure state recovery. We identify windows in packet sizes and bend angles for a small OAM spread and show that weak bends can produce narrow distributions with the mean OAM tilted relative to the momentum, making these states candidates for spatiotemporal vortices. For a few MeV electrons, we propose to use half-turn magnets that leave the mean OAM nearly antiparallel to the momentum while keeping its distribution narrow. For a circular orbit in a uniform field, the OAM variance after the exit grows as $N^2$ over $N$ turns, favoring linear accelerators, such as LINAC at JINR, for first experiments in MeV range.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study slow-roll inflation in the context of metric-affine gravity. We consider the most general projectively invariant metric-affine theory at most quadratic in the distortion and linear in curvature with no propagating torsion and non-metricity and couple it non-minimally to a scalar field. We focus on the class of $ξ$-attractors, in which a single function $f(φ)$ fixes the whole scalar sector. Integrating out the non-dynamical distortion generates a correction to the kinetic term $k(φ)$ which is $f'(φ)^2$ times a ratio of polynomials in $f(φ)$. The new kinetic term can develop poles at finite field values, where the distortion field equations degenerate. We classify the poles and derive the conditions on the effective couplings for poles of order $p=2$ and $p=3$, the maximal order allowed in this setting. We then proceed to study inflation. Second-order poles realize $α$-attractors with $α$ fixed by the residue and are already available in the parity-even sector of the theory. Third-order poles instead require the parity-odd sector: whenever the parity-odd quadratic couplings vanish, the kinetic function splits into two independent terms with poles of order at most $p=2$. Third-order pole-inflation, as we confirm numerically for $f(φ)\proptoφ^2$, yields $r\propto N_*^{-3/2}$ with a tunable amplitude and $n_s\simeq 1-\tfrac{3}{2N_*}$, a spectral index mildly larger than the $α$-attractor prediction and well centered in the region preferred by the current combination of ACT, SPT and DESI data. Moreover, when inflation happens far away from the pole we also find a further universal attractor, an inverse-linear plateau, with $n_s \simeq 1-\frac{4}{3N_*}$ and $r\propto N_*^{-4/3}$, testable with the forthcoming BICEP/Keck observations.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: The Mass Gap Approach to QCD. III. Solution of the gluon confinement problem
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present reports on progress in the solution of the gluon confinement problem and in the explanation of the scale breaking in the asymptotic freedom regime in QCD. It is based on the previously formulated the mass gap approach to QCD, which sheds the light on a mass origin in its ground state. We have established the exact expression for the full gluon propagator. One of its solution allows to sum up all the severe (more singular than $1/q^2$) infrared singularities which can be accommodated by a single full gluon propagator. In order to correctly treat them, we have developed a formalism of the joint use of the theory of functions of complex variable, and the dimensional regularization method correctly implemented into the theory of distributions. Despite the presence of the mass gap, gluons remain massless. Our solution satisfies the two boundary conditions: it dominates over all other possible solutions at large distances but itself prevents gluons to appear in the physical spectrum. It possesses the asymptotic freedom behaviour at short distances. We discuss the connection of our results to the Elitzur's theorem.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Can Two-Point Correlations Determine Gravitational Waves from Sound Waves?
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Sound waves are expected to be a dominant source of gravitational waves (GWs) from cosmological first-order phase transitions. Their spectrum is commonly predicted using the fluid velocity two-point correlation function under the Gaussian approximation. However, since the GW source is quadratic in velocity, connected four-point correlations may also contribute to the GW spectrum. Through two analytical toy examples, we demonstrate that velocity two-point correlations alone does not always uniquely determine the GW spectrum. Moving beyond these idealized examples, we investigate a realistic acoustic source based on stochastic bubble nucleation and growth, proving that the connected contribution becomes subleading during subsequent linear acoustic propagation, although cosmic expansion limits this suppression. These results clarify when two-point reconstruction is reliable and how higher-order velocity correlations and the duration of acoustic emission affect GW predictions.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Generalized parton distributions of the nucleon in the chiral quark soliton model II: Chiral anomaly mediation in the polarized GPDs
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We calculate the polarized flavor-singlet generalized parton distributions (GPDs) $\widetilde H^{u+d}$ and $\widetilde E^{u+d}$ in the chiral quark soliton model at nonzero skewness and momentum transfer. Results are obtained with and without a singlet pseudoscalar meson $η_0$, whose mass is generated by the chiral anomaly. Relative to the pion-only model, the singlet field introduces a sizable contribution to $\widetilde E^{u+d}$ in the ERBL region but only a minor correction to $\widetilde H^{u+d}$. An explicit meson-exchange term qualitatively accounts for this contrast and displays the anticipated singlet pole. When the anomaly-induced mass is set to zero, the pole becomes massless, and the exchange term dominates $\widetilde E^{u+d}$ at small momentum transfer. These findings demonstrate how anomalous singlet-meson dynamics leaves distinct signatures in the polarized GPDs of the nucleon.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Quark-mass dependence of two-nucleon scattering
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Understanding how the properties of the visible Universe depend on the parameters of the Standard Model of particle physics requires \emph{ab initio} theoretical computations. To that end, we investigate the quark-mass dependence of low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering in the deuteron and dineutron channels. We perform lattice-QCD calculations at pion masses $M_π\approx 200$ and $280$ MeV and compare their results to phenomenology at the physical point and to a previous calculation at $M_π\approx 710$ MeV. Scattering amplitudes, phase shifts, and threshold parameters are determined from finite-volume spectra using quantization conditions that explicitly incorporate long-distance effects from one-pion exchange. We analyze the pion-mass dependence of scattering lengths and effective ranges using chiral effective field theory with Weinberg and Kaplan-Savage-Wise power countings. From this, we estimate the pion-mass derivatives of the inverse scattering lengths and binding momentum, at the physical point. Both power countings indicate that the deuteron unbinds near $M_π\approx 220$ MeV.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Long lived MeV scale bound state dark matter alleviates the ${}^7 Li$ tension
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate the impact of MeV scale unstable bound state dark matter on both thermal and non thermal Big Bang nucleosynthesis. Focusing on the weakly self interacting regime, we find that this framework can reproduce the theoretically predicted abundances through both short and long lived bound states. While long lived bound states can alleviate the cosmological ${}^7$Li problem, they simultaneously lead to discrepancies with other light element abundances. We show that this tension is resolved by incorporating non thermal nucleosynthesis, which act on these non standard initial light element abundances to alleviate the ${}^7 Li$ tension without violating observational constraints on the other elements. Remarkably, across the range of $\widetildeρ_B$ and $m_χ$ considered, long lived bound states with lifetimes $10^0\,{\rm s}\lesssimτ\lesssim10^2\,{\rm s}$ can simultaneously resolve the ${}^7$Li problem and a large parameter space remain consistent with the observed abundances of the other light elements. Our results demonstrate that non thermal effects are essential for obtaining a consistent nucleosynthesis history in unstable bound state dark matter scenarios.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Analysis of the $D_0^*(2300)$ resonance from lattice QCD under chiral symmetry
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We reanalyze the lattice spectra for $I=1/2$ $Dπ$ scattering in the $A_1^+$ irreducible representation from [Phys. Rev. D 111, 014503 (2025)] to investigate the impact of chiral and SU(3) flavor symmetries in $S$-wave $Dπ$ scattering and the $D_0^*(2300)$ resonance. By fitting the phase shifts obtained via Lüscher's formula with both traditional and chirally modified effective-range expansion and $K$-matrix parameterizations, we find that the chiral factor shifts the extracted pole mass closer to the threshold (especially for resonances) and substantially reduces the resonance width. These findings are confirmed by unitarized chiral perturbation theory through a direct fit to the lattice spectra with both the single-channel and the $Dπ$-$Dη$-$D_s\bar{K}$ coupled-channel schemes. Once the coupled channels are incorporated, the two-pole structure of the $D_0^*(2300)$ emerges. The trajectories of the two poles are investigated by varying the pion mass.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: The Colour Glass Condensate
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a comprehensive introduction to the Colour Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory, a first-principles framework for hadronic interactions in high-energy Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) at large parton densities. The focus is on the underlying physical picture and associated emergent phenomena, such as gluon saturation, transverse momentum broadening, and geometric scaling. We introduce the key components of the CGC formalism: the semiclassical approximation for dense gluon systems at saturation, the nonlinear JIMWLK equation governing the energy evolution of multi-gluon correlations, and its mean-field approximation, the BK equation. The formalism is illustrated through applications to selected "dilute-dense" processes, namely high-energy electron-nucleus and proton-nucleus collisions. Finally, we briefly discuss advanced topics including higher-order radiative corrections, the Langevin formulation of the JIMWLK equation, and the emergence of transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorisation from the CGC effective theory.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 60 pages, 16 figures. Contribution to the Elsevier Encyclopaedia of Nuclear Physics

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Phenomenological investigation of order statistics for multi-jet events
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate rank-ordered jet rapidity distributions as probes of multijet radiation in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. These observables retain information about the organization of jets within an event that is not resolved by the inclusive single-jet rapidity spectrum. We compare normalized predictions from the BFKL-based generator BFKLex and the collinear parton-shower generator PYTHIA 8.306, considering both fixed three-jet configurations and rank observables defined across multiplicities. We assess PDF and tune variations for PYTHIA 8.306, and PDF and factorization- and renormalization-scale variations for BFKLex. Total-variation and Wasserstein distances quantify the separation between the baseline shapes. Differences remain visible relative to the evaluated uncertainty bands in several well-populated regions. A minimum rapidity separation between the extremal jets modifies the discriminating power of the observables in a rank-dependent way. These results support rank-ordered rapidity spectra as experimentally accessible observables complementary to conventional Mueller-Navelet measurements for investigating high-energy QCD radiation.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Baryogenesis and EDMs in the 2HDM with a Complex Singlet
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We perform the first joint analysis of baryogenesis from initial Higgs charges (also called Higgsogenesis) and electric dipole moments (EDMs) in a model with two Higgs doublets, a complex scalar, and a Majorana fermion. In our proposed scenario, baryogenesis happens in three steps: (1) The decay of the scalar produces an asymmetry between the two Higgs doublets which is partly transferred to fermions via Standard Model processes. (2) This asymmetry is converted into a $B-L$ charge via interactions mediated by the Majorana fermion. (3) The weak sphaleron processes partially convert the resulting $B-L$ charge into a $B$ asymmetry. We perform a numerical analysis of baryogenesis and the EDM contributions and find that, due to resonant enhancement, baryogenesis is possible with singlet masses as low as $10^5$ GeV. We also find that for some parameters, the model can give large contributions to the electron and neutron EDM while also producing baryogenesis. The present scenario offers a new perspective on interpreting observational bounds in terms of cosmology: Because it relies on out-of-equilibrium decays, the questions of baryogenesis and $CP$ violation in the Higgs sector may be linked with EDM signals without the additional assumption of a first order electroweak phase transition.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Estimating Spectrum-Free Information Bounds for Generative Surrogates Beyond Conditional Collapse
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Conditional generative surrogates in high-energy physics, such as models that predict reconstructed jets from partons, are often evaluated on $1\text{D}$ marginal divergences among other metrics. Taken alone these metrics can reward conditional collapse. On a CMS simulation benchmark, a sampler that ignores the conditioner beats a trained Mixture Density Network (MDN) on all four target marginals under both KL and Wasserstein-1, and cannot be stably separated from a Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) model on two of the four. We instead score the models with the Continuous Ranked Probability Skill Score (CRPSS) from forecast verification, taking the exact marginal as the reference. We show how global skill depends on the evaluation spectrum, and we also report it within bins of a conditioning variable, where that dependence largely goes away. We then introduce a data-driven $k$-Nearest-Neighbor ($k$-NN) extrapolation that estimates the best CRPS the conditioning information allows. Both models agree with this estimate on all four targets, which suggests that current architectures have reached the information available in the conditioner, at least as far as these per-target scores can tell.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Search for dark matter axions at 1-2 micro-eV with a RADES-DarkQuantum haloscope at CERN
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The QCD axion remains one of the most compelling candidates for the dark matter of the Universe, yet the mass range around $1$\text{--}\SI{2}{\micro\electronvolt} remains essentially unexplored. In this paper, we describe a proposal to employ CERN's M1 superconducting magnet to deploy a haloscope to perform a search for galactic axion and axion-like particle dark matter providing continuous coverage from approximately 1.2 to 1.8 \SI{}{\micro\electronvolt}. Under conservative assumptions, the experiment can reach the QCD axion band over a significant fraction of the scanned range, while optimistic detector performance would allow sensitivity to benchmark models such as KSVZ and DFSZ over a large part of the explored mass interval. With the current long shut-down of CERN's accelerators providing a unique and timely window, such an experiment will deliver high-impact results even in conservative scenarios and potentially delivering a definitive test of the axion dark matter paradigm in the unexplored $1$\text{--}\SI{2}{\micro\electronvolt} mass range.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: prepared for submission to JHEP, 42 pages

High Energy Phenomenology.title: A consistent neutrino determination of the low-energy weak mixing angle
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The weak mixing angle, $\sin^2θ_W$, is a fundamental parameter of the Standard Model and a sensitive probe of electroweak physics across various energy scales. At low momentum transfer, the Standard Model prediction approaches a well-defined low-energy plateau, providing a target for precision tests of the electroweak theory. At the lowest momentum transfer, atomic parity violation (APV) in cesium provides one of the most precise determinations of the weak mixing angle. Here, we review and update the status of this determination and compare it with other available probes. We then consistently reanalyze low-energy neutrino scattering data and combine the resulting determinations from coherent elastic scattering (CE$ν$NS) and neutrino-electron scattering. The complementary sensitivity of these processes to electroweak couplings enables a neutrino-based determination of the low-energy weak mixing angle, accounting for electroweak radiative corrections and relevant theoretical uncertainties. Our global analysis yields $\sin^2θ_W^{\rm low}(ν\,\text{data}) = 0.232\pm 0.006$. We assess the consistency and relative impact of the individual neutrino measurements and discuss the prospects for future CE$ν$NS and neutrino-electron scattering experiments to improve the precision of this determination. Our analysis provides an independent test of the Standard Model at low momentum transfer, complementary to that provided by atomic parity violation.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables; Updated global fit including the latest CONUS+ Run 2 data

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Searching for axion-like particles with SPHEREx
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study prospects to detect axion-like particles (ALPs) with the upcoming near-infrared telescope SPHEREx. The signal under investigation is the ALP decay into two photons. Assuming dark matter (DM) to be in the form of ALPs, we analyze the signal from the DM halos of dwarf spheroidal galaxies, the Large Magellanic Cloud and the Milky Way. We find that SPHEREx can significantly improve current limits on the axion-photon coupling in the 0.5-3 eV ALP mass range.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. v3: sensitivities corrected, see note added. Conclusions unchanged

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Study of enhancing the signal-background separation for the Higgs boson production in association with a single top-quark in $pp$ collisions at the LHC
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In this paper, a multivariate analysis based approach for enhancing the extraction of the rare Standard Model (SM) process being studied - Higgs boson production in association with a single top quark (tH) - from the prevailing background processes is presented. The analysis was performed using a Monte Carlo generated dataset simulating the outcomes of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). A deep fully connected neural network was developed for signal-background discrimination, incorporating a masking mechanism designed to suppress the contribution of input variables associated with objects that were not reconstructed in a given event. The performance of the masked architecture was evaluated on independent Monte Carlo samples. The results of the proposed methodology are compared with a conventional cut-based approach in terms of the statistical significance of the tH production channel. The developed framework was tested using a simulated dataset corresponding approximately to the combined statistical samples of LHC Runs 1, 2, and 3.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: $P$-wave quarkonia in jets at the LHC
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present the first systematic theoretical study of the production of $P$-wave charmonium states $χ_{cJ}$ and bottomonium states $χ_{bJ}(nP)$ within jets at the LHC using the fragmenting jet function framework at next-to-leading order in $α_s$. Our calculation resums both collinear DGLAP logarithms and threshold double logarithms in the fragmentation functions and accounts for feeddown contributions from higher quarkonium states. We observe a notable contrast between the charmonium and bottomonium sectors. For $χ_{bJ}(nP)$, the normalized momentum-fraction distributions exhibit a nearly universal shape, with remarkably weak dependence on the choice of long-distance matrix element sets, the radial excitation ($n=1,2,3$), and the total angular momentum ($J=0,1,2$). We attribute this universality to the overwhelming dominance of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ fragmentation channel, while feeddown contributions from higher bottomonium states remain small. In contrast, the shape of $χ_{cJ}$ distributions exhibits a stronger dependence on the matrix-element set, reflecting the different relative contributions of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ and ${}^3P_J^{[1]}$ channels. We provide predictions for the $χ_{cJ}$ and $χ_{bJ}(nP)$ distributions for the CMS and LHCb kinematic selections across a range of jet transverse momenta. We also compare our predictions with \textsc{Pythia}~8 simulations for selected $P$-wave quarkonium states.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Higgs-Portal Stueckelberg Dark Matter
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study dark photon dark matter X associated with a dark $U(1)_X$ gauge symmetry. To evade laboratory and cosmological constraints on kinetic mixing with the Standard Model $U(1)_Y$, we assign a $Z_2$-odd dark parity to X that forbids such mixing. The leading interactions then arise from gauge-invariant dimension-6 Higgs-portal operators, including both parity-even and parity-odd terms. We assume that the dark matter mass is generated via the Stueckelberg mechanism. In the interacting Stueckelberg EFT, a gauge-invariant dimension-6 parent reduces in unitary gauge to the nominal dimension-4 Higgs-portal interaction $(H^†H)X_μX^μ$, with its coefficient correlated with $m_X^2/Λ^2$, while additional derivative operators are organized by the same longitudinal-mode power counting. We investigate freeze-in production of X from Higgs-pair annihilations after reheating, incorporating both field-strength and Stueckelberg-allowed operators. First, we consider the case in which the Wilson coefficients of the gauge-invariant dimension-6 operators, C and $\tilde C$, are of order unity. Under a conservative single-cutoff power counting in which the strong-coupling scales of the longitudinal mode lie above the cutoff of the field-strength effective theory, we find that the Stueckelberg contributions remain subdominant in dark matter production. We emphasize that this ordering of scales is an explicit assumption rather than a universal consequence of perturbative unitarity. Next, we explore a more general situation in which C and $\tilde C$ are smaller than unity. In this second case, Stueckelberg-allowed operators can become comparable and generate contributions proportional to $T_{reh}^3$, $T_{reh}^5$, and $T_{reh}^7$, including sign-dependent interference effects. For both cases, we show that there exists a wide parameter space consistent with the observed dark matter relic density.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 30 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Published version in Phys. Rev. D with a minor clarification

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Inflation, Cosmic Perturbations and Non-Gaussianities
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We review the theory of inflationary perturbations. Perturbations at both linear and nonlinear orders are reviewed. We also review a variety of inflation models, emphasizing their signatures on cosmic perturbations.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 84 pages, 36 figures. Based on lectures given at the 7th Asian Winter School on Strings, Particles and Cosmology. v2: observational aspects updated, references added, typos corrected. v3: references added, typos corrected, version to appear on Commun. Theor. Phys. v4: more typos corrected and some discussions clarified (assisted by GPT)

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Model analysis on the effectiveness of the HAL QCD method for hadron-hadron interactions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The HAL QCD method has been one of the powerful tools to extract hadron-hadron interactions directly from lattice QCD simulation data. In this paper, we aim at examining the effectiveness of the HAL QCD method by deriving a formula to calculate quantities in the HAL QCD method, such as the so-called R-correlators and HAL QCD local potentials, from the hadron-hadron scattering amplitudes within effective models. In this framework, we can judge whether the HAL QCD local potential, evaluated in the present formula, reproduces the properties of the original hadron-hadron interaction or not via the scattering amplitude, which is a solution of the Lippmann--Schwinger equation with the original hadron-hadron interaction as an input. In an analysis within a simple model of elastic scattering, we show that, when the original interaction is predominantly local, the HAL QCD local potentials quantitatively reproduce phase shifts of the hadron-hadron scatterings and correctly indicate the existence/absence of the bound state with its binding energy $\sim$ MeV. Higher-order corrections in the derivative expansion of the HAL QCD nonlocal potentials can provide a better description of the binding energies of the bound states. The lattice discretization and finite-volume effects of spacetime modify the results only slightly, as long as their scale is not comparable to the interaction range. Furthermore, we consider the $\bar{K} N$ potential in a bare to $\bar{K} N$ transition amplitude, which shows singular behavior around the origin in the recent HAL QCD results of the lattice QCD simulation data, and discuss the cause of such singular behavior in the HAL QCD method through our model analysis of the $\bar{K} N$ scattering.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 25 pages, 19 figures. Version accepted for publication in Physical Review D. Added discussions on the derivative expansion of nonlocal potentials and interactions with various ranges on the lattice

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Can cosmic neutrinos induce a cosmic birefringence signal?
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: A coupling of photons to the cosmic neutrino asymmetry current has been proposed to explain the hinted isotropic rotation of CMB polarization. Gauge invariant UV completions require a Kalb-Ramond field that is exactly dual to a massless axion. We show that, in this case, the product of the axion-photon coupling and the axion-neutrino current coupling is fixed by the signal, $g_{aγ}/f_\ell=1/Λ_*^2$ with $Λ_*\simeq10$ TeV. Using $SU(2)_L$ gauge invariance we show that the dual axion couples to electrons as $g_{aγ}g_{ae}=m_e/Λ_*^2\simeq5\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. This value is excluded by the measured electron magnetic moment combined with light-shining-through-a-wall searches, as well as by stellar evolution. Conserved anomaly-free currents may evade these bounds, but then either a contact interaction among SM fermions excludes the model, or the relic neutrinos decouple from the signal. We conclude that cosmic neutrinos cannot induce a birefringence signal.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Dilaton-Induced Resonant Production of Ultralight Vector Dark Matter
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We consider the production of ultralight vector dark matter through a dilatonic half-mass resonance in the presence of an oscillating spectator scalar. The cosmological condition is that the Floquet instability becomes efficient before the spectator contributes dominantly to the expansion. We express this condition in terms of the microscopic modulation parameter $ε_i=Φ_i/M$ and the gravitational onset fraction $r_i=Φ_i^2/(6\Mpl^2)$. For a background with constant equation-of-state parameter $w_b$, the narrow-band result gives $μ/H\propto a^{3w_b/2}$; the ratio therefore grows as $a^{1/2}$ during radiation domination and remains constant for matter-like expansion. Requiring delayed amplification to precede spectator domination gives the amplitude-independent bound $M/\Mpl\lesssim\sqrt6\,c_1\simeq0.31$, with $c_1\simeq1/8$ for the linear half-mass branch. An expanding-background calculation gives $a_\star<a_{\rm dom}$ for sub-Planckian $M$, whereas $M\simeq\Mpl$ delays efficient growth until after domination. Using the efficient-transfer normalization, we obtain $m_{γ'}\propto r_i^{-2}$, so that $m_{γ'}\sim10^{-20}$--$10^{-18}\,{\rm eV}$ corresponds to $r_i\sim10^{-5}$--$10^{-4}$ rather than to early spectator domination. The canonical polarization analysis shows a more infrared-localized longitudinal spectrum than the transverse spectrum, while derivative terms associated with canonical normalization change the leading Floquet exponents at order unity. Stückelberg and Higgsed realizations lead to different ultraviolet consistency conditions, including radial-mode decoupling and symmetry-restoration bounds. These conditions select a radiation-era, perturbative, infrared-dominated regime with a sub-Planckian kinetic scale for production.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Probing the Seed Effect of Supermassive Primordial Black Holes with Weak Gravitational Lensing
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate the cosmological implications of supermassive primordial black holes (PBHs) as a component of dark matter (DM), focusing on their seed effect on large-scale structure formation. In contrast to the Poisson effect associated with the discrete distribution of PBHs, the seed effect arises because PBHs act as early gravitational seeds, accreting surrounding DM and developing dense DM spikes to form dressed PBHs. These structures enhance the matter power spectrum, particularly on small scales. We model their contribution within the halo-model framework under two prescriptions for DM accretion: an optimistic scenario (Case 1) and a conservative scenario (Case 2), which predict different modifications to the 1-halo term. We constrain the PBH abundance using weak-lensing measurements from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3), performing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis to derive upper limits on the PBH fraction $f_{\rm PBH}$, as a function of the PBH mass $M_{\rm PBH}$. We find that weak lensing places competitive constraints on supermassive PBHs, with the upper limits on $f_{\rm PBH}$ becoming progressively stronger toward higher PBH masses. Case 1, which predicts more efficient DM accretion and hence a larger enhancement of the matter power spectrum, yields stronger constraints than Case 2; in particular, it excludes $f_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{-4}$ for $M_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{10} M_\odot$. We further forecast the sensitivity of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) using mock weak-lensing data and find that the constraints could improve by approximately two orders of magnitude. Our results establish weak gravitational lensing as a sensitive probe of the seed effect of supermassive PBHs and demonstrate its potential to complement other cosmological and astrophysical searches.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: LZ-Motivated Pseudo-Dirac Higgsinos in the Supersymmetric 331 Model from the Supersymmetric \texorpdfstring{$SU(6)$}{SU(6)} GUT Model
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The high-recoil event reported by LUX--ZEPLIN motivates a neutral electroweak state with an inelastic splitting in the sub-MeV range. We propose supersymmetric 331 model from the supersymmetric $SU(6)$ GUT model, and we study the electroweakino sector relevant to this recoil. Above the $331$-breaking scale hypercharge is not an independent gauge factor, and the leading bino--wino cancellation is replaced by a relation between the physical $U(1)_X$ and $SU(3)_L$ gaugino invariants, $I_X=-I_L$. A singlet--adjoint gauge-kinetic source also correlates the colored invariant. We diagonalize the neutral gauge--Higgs fermion sector of the renormalizable model and determine the tree-level Higgsino splitting without introducing an effective bino mass by hand. The required solutions form a continuous locus in the gaugino and $331$-breaking parameters. At the reference point, the solution lies close to the leading sum rule, while variation of the $331$-breaking coupling moves the locus continuously. The same calculation tests the ordering of the additional neutral states, the gauge/gaugino contribution to the $331$-breaking scalar mass, and the gravitino ordering. We compare this construction with recent $SU(5)$, singlino-assisted, electroweak-multiplet, nuclear-response and solar-capture analyses of the LZ event.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Power corrections to heavy-quark spin correlations in small-$x$ deep-inelastic scattering
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Heavy-quark spin correlations in small-$x$ deep-inelastic scattering receive corrections beyond the back-to-back limit. For a rotationally symmetric target at leading power, the target dependence cancels from the normalized spin density matrix after full azimuthal averaging, for fixed kinematics and spin axes related by transverse light-front boosts. We calculate the first nonvanishing correction at tree level for finite quark mass and finite $N_c$ in a homogeneous Gaussian target. The expansion through fourth order in the dipole sizes includes logarithms, contact terms and all interference contributions at that order. Comparison with the improved transverse-momentum-dependent approximation separates kinematic corrections from terms with additional insertions of the target current. Numerical integration of the unexpanded Gaussian kernel tests the approximation at 28 parameter points. Spin correlations differ between the two targets in all 12 kinematic comparisons; in one comparison both spin states remain separable. At fixed photon virtuality, the leading large-$P$ behavior of the fourth-order correction to the normalized transverse spin state is generically proportional to $m\ln P/P^3$. We also compare two fixed Gaussian targets using unpolarized momentum distributions and joint spin measurements. For a purely transverse photon, three narrow momentum bins and an ideal measurement of both spins along the common quark-momentum axis defined by the light-front boost, spin information adds 3.5-3.7 percent to the expected log likelihood ratio after the overall normalization is fitted. This increase depends on the spin analyzing power and bin selection. The calculation establishes a model-dependent effect, rather than an experimental sensitivity prediction.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Scale-Invariant Three-Component Dark Matter and Gravitational Wave Signals
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study a classically scale-invariant extension of the Standard Model (SM) with four new fields in a hidden sector: a complex scalar $S$, two Dirac fermions $ψ^{1,2}$ and the gauge boson $V_μ$ of a new $U(1)_D$ symmetry. The scalar $S$ couples to the SM through the Higgs portal. We identify regions of parameter space in which $V_μ$, $ψ^1$ and $ψ^2$ are all stable, giving a three-component dark matter (DM) scenario. The model is classically scale invariant, and the electroweak symmetry breaks because of the loop effects. We impose the observed relic density and current direct detection bounds, and then study the finite temperature effective potential. For a benchmark point, we find a first-order phase transition and compute the resulting gravitational wave (GW) spectrum, which we compare with the projected sensitivities of space-based interferometers. Although the viable parameter space is small, it can be probed by future experiments.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Scaling laws for amplitude surrogates
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Scaling laws describing the dependence of neural network performance on the amount of training data, the spent compute, and the network size have emerged across a huge variety of machine learning task and datasets. In this work, we systematically investigate these scaling laws in the context of amplitude surrogates for particle physics. We show that the scaling coefficients are connected to the number of external particles of the process. Our results demonstrate that scaling laws are a useful tool to achieve desired precision targets.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Optimal-Transport Contrastive Learning for Centrality Determination in Heavy-Ion Collisions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Determining centrality of heavy-ion collisions with high resolution is essential for event-by-event analyses, in particular for net-proton fluctuation measurements aimed at locating the QCD critical point. Supervised machine-learning approaches rely on labels generated by model and therefore inherit the model dependence of the training target. In this work, we propose an unsupervised method to determine collision centrality based on optimal transport. Each collision is represented by its 1-Wasserstein distances to a fixed set of landmark events chosen to cover the measured multiplicity range. A point-cloud network trained by contrastive learning then compresses these distances into a compact event embedding, which is partitioned into equal-size centrality classes. We find that this approach groups events with similar $N_{\rm part}$ and yields a better centrality resolution, quantified by the normalized width of the $N_{\rm part}$ distribution, than the conventional method of cutting on particle multiplicity. The method, however, encounters a bottleneck once realistic kinematic cuts are applied to the particles. We attribute this degraded performance to the loss of distinct features between central and peripheral collisions because of applying kinematic cuts. The application of optimal transport to centrality determination in experimental data, remains an open problem that needs further study.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: First broadband search for fixed-polarization dark photon dark matter with GigaBREAD
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present the first search for fixed-polarization dark photon (DP) dark matter in the 44-52$μ\mathrm{eV}$ mass range, corresponding to 10.7-12.5GHz. GigaBREAD is a room-temperature broadband dish antenna experiment in which DP convert to ordinary photons on a cylindrical metallic emission surface and are focused onto a radio-frequency receiver. Previous searches, including GigaBREAD and several other dish antenna searches, have assumed randomly polarized DP dark matter. However, vector dark matter produced by a misalignment-like mechanism may retain an approximately fixed polarization, leading to sidereal modulation of the detector response as the Earth rotates. We reanalyze the GigaBREAD data using a polarization-matched likelihood that accounts for the time-dependent projection of a fixed DP polarization onto the detector axis. We find no evidence for a fixed-polarization DP signal and set upper limits on the kinetic mixing parameter at the level of $χ\sim10^{-12}$. These limits are about $20\%$ better than a naive limit obtained by rescaling the previous GigaBREAD limit under the fixed-polarization assumption.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Enhancing Gravitational Waves from Global Strings via a First-Order Phase Transition
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We perform the first (3+1)-dimensional lattice simulations of a cosmological first-order phase transition (PT) in which true-vacuum bubbles with random phases nucleate, expand, and collide, producing a network of global strings. We find that the string network enters the scaling regime, and the coefficient of the logarithmic growth is smaller than the value obtained for a second-order PT. From the axion spectrum, we derive the dark-matter relic abundance and the dark-radiation bound from big bang nucleosynthesis on the axion decay constant $f_a$ and mass $m_a$. The ratio of the gravitational wave emission rate to the axion emission rate is found to be about two orders of magnitude larger than in the second-order case, and the resulting gravitational wave spectrum can be probed by pulsar timing arrays as well as by space- and ground-based interferometers.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Static Quark-Antiquark Interactions in Rotating SU(3) Gluodynamics
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study static quark--antiquark interactions in rotating SU(3) gluodynamics using quenched lattice simulations at imaginary angular velocity. At zero temperature, we extract the static potential from Wilson loops for quark--antiquark pairs aligned with the rotation axis, for transverse pairs with one source on the rotation axis, and for symmetric transverse pairs across the rotation axis. Within the present accuracy, no significant rotation dependence or anisotropy is observed in the zero-temperature potential. At finite temperature, imaginary rotation suppresses the color-averaged free energies obtained from Polyakov-loop correlators in both longitudinal and transverse geometries. Axial-diagonal comparisons are used to identify a bulk region where open-boundary artifacts are reduced. In this region, the large-distance longitudinal free-energy shift is well described by $ΔF_z(R_{xy})=A R_{xy}^2+B$. The transverse channels exhibit the same qualitative suppression, while their distance dependence additionally reflects the radial arrangement of the static sources and is compatible with a radial single-source free-energy shift in the bulk region. For the finite-temperature observables studied above $T_c$, the response weakens as the temperature is increased. These results provide lattice evidence for a position- and geometry-dependent response of bare static-source free energies to imaginary rotation in a gluonic medium.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Improved method for extracting low-energy expansion from OPE in mass-gapped theories
